# dal and dalgona

Dal is a complete terminal coding agent. Dalgona is dal with opinionated batteries, switched on through the same public extension door.

---

- [What is this](#what-is-this)
- [Install](#install)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Features](#features)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Development](#development)
- [License](#license)

## What is this

Dal works without dalgona. It ships the agent loop, providers, tools, Starlark extensions, terminal interface, session storage, manuals, and wire protocols in one product.

Dalgona reuses dal through the public extension interface and turns on batteries for orchestration, history, quality, judged rules, web, work, MCP, review, ask, skills, ttsr-rules, and procs. It keeps its own configuration, data, and sessions.

Binaries are `dalgon` (aliases `dal`, `dl`) and `dalgona` (alias `dg`). A plugin that loads in dalgon loads in dalgona.

Everything extends dal through one door. In process, the Host and Agent seam carries one snapshot, one change stream, one command path, one request and answer pair, and one blob read. Across processes, the same operations travel as JSON-RPC over stdio or a local socket. The manuals live behind that door at `dal://` and `dalgona://`.

## Install

In a POSIX shell, build from source. The install guide in this checkout describes a source route and lists no registry version to install.

You need git, the latest stable Rust toolchain, and a C toolchain. The symbol grammars compile through `cc`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona
cd dalgona
rustup update stable --no-self-update
cargo build --release --locked -p dalgon -p dalgona
export PATH="$PWD/target/release:$PATH"
```

The binaries land in `target/release/`: `dalgon` with `dal` and `dl`, plus `dalgona` with `dg`. The `export` line assumes POSIX `sh`; PowerShell needs different syntax to extend `PATH`.

Supported platforms are Linux, macOS, and Windows on x86_64 and aarch64. Unsigned Windows binaries may trigger SmartScreen; verify the checksum where one is published. Configuration and data use per-OS roots; on POSIX defaults these are `~/.config/dal/` and `~/.local/share/dal/`, and dalgona uses its own family directories. Plugins need no toolchain.

## Quick start

The outputs below summarize checked-in CLI help and docs.

```sh
dalgon docs
# prints the dal manual index starting with `# dal://`
dalgon docs dal://cli
# prints the command-line page titled `The command line`
dalgon login --help
# prints sign-in usage starting with `Sign in to a provider`
dalgon login status
# exit 1 with no credentials; lists providers as `not configured`
```

Run `dal` for the terminal once a provider is ready. Sign in with `dalgon login`, then pick a model.

## Features

- **Complete alone**: chat in the terminal, search and edit with approval, keep journals, and read `dal://` without installing dalgona.
- **Same door**: load any dal plugin in dalgona unchanged. Name a dalgona battery in `disabled_batteries` to leave it out.
- **Starlark plugins**: ship tools, commands, hooks, skills, rules, and prompt text from one `plugin.star` with no compile step. A broken plugin stops startup and names `path:line:col`. `/reload` keeps the previous set on failure.
- **Approval first**: ask before every `patch` and every `exec` by default. Headless runs deny when no person can answer. `eval` runs Starlark only and is not a sandbox.
- **Durable sessions**: continue with `-c`, resume with `-r`, branch with `/fork` and `/clone`, and share with `/export`. Compaction starts at 85 percent of the context window.
- **Terminal and headless**: work inline or fullscreen, print with `-p`, emit JSON with `--json`, or drive ACP, RPC, router, and A2A clients over one protocol.
- **Batteries on demand**: run dalgona for orchestration, plan and todo, ask, web search and fetch, MCP client, review, judged rules, quality guard, history, skills, ttsr-rules, symbol search, hashline edits, and the deferred `procs` tool over background jobs.

### Scope limits

Dal keeps its core small. It has no MCP client (dalgona ships one; a plugin can reach HTTP services with `net.fetch`), no plan or todo (dalgona ships both), and no subagents by default. There is no LSP in either product, no upload (`/export` writes a file you share yourself), no self-rebuild (`/reload` reloads plugins), nothing but Starlark in `eval`, no second store besides the journal, and no browser front end in the binary. The optional sandbox is off by default, guards the home directory, and sets no network restriction. A plugin runs with your permissions, so read it before you install it.

## Usage

### Sign in and list models

```sh
dalgon login
dalgon login status
dalgon models
dalgon logout
```

`login` signs in interactively or with `--api-key` or `--device-auth` where the provider supports it. `login status` exits 0 when at least one provider is ready and 1 otherwise, with a sign-in hint and no secret output. `models` lists models with built-in prices and sources. `logout` removes stored credentials. Secrets live in `auth.json` with mode `0600`; the loader refuses symlinks and group or other permission bits.

### Read the manual

```sh
dalgon docs
dalgon docs dal://cli
dalgona docs dalgona://batteries
```

With no URI, `docs` prints the index. With a page URI, it prints the page. Unknown URIs fail with a miss message on stderr and nothing on stdout.

### Run in the terminal

```sh
dal
dal --screen fullscreen
dalgona
```

`dal` starts the inline terminal by default once a provider and model are set. `--screen fullscreen` uses the alternate screen and replays the settled transcript on exit. `dalgona` starts the batteries product with its own config, data, and sessions. You can type while dal works; a steer reaches the model at the next safe point, a follow-up waits for the turn to end, and stop ends the turn at once.

### Run one turn without the TUI

```sh
dalgon -p "Summarize the staged diff"
dalgon --json "Summarize the staged diff"
dalgon -c -p "Continue with the next file"
dalgon -r my-session -p "Resume and finish"
```

These need a configured model; without one dalgon reports the missing model and how to set it. Print mode runs one turn and waits up to 3 seconds for extension status to go quiet. JSON mode writes one result line only after every status kind is quiet. Common run flags are `-m` for model, `--thinking`, `--mode`, `-n` for name, `-C` for workspace directory, and `--no-session` to skip saving.

### Control sessions and safety

```sh
dalgon --approval ask
dalgon --approval edits
dalgon --approval all
dalgon --sandbox
```

The default asks before every `patch` and every `exec`. `edits` approves edits without asking and still asks for `exec`. `all` approves every call; use it only inside an external sandbox. When no controller can answer, dal denies and says why. `--sandbox` runs `exec` children through the platform helper with workspace, temporary, cache, and `sandbox_writable` roots writable. `dalgon serve` binds loopback only unless `--public` is given with a token from `dalgon serve token`.

### Manage plugins

```sh
dalgon plugin list
dalgon plugin grant quality
dalgon plugin revoke quality
```

Plugins load from the data root only, never from the workspace. `list` shows configured plugins and persistent grants. `grant` and `revoke` change the stored grant; session grants end with their sessions.

### Serve and integrate

```sh
dalgon serve
dalgon serve token
dalgon serve --public
dalgon serve --a2a
dalgon rpc
dalgon rpc --socket /tmp/dalgon.sock
dalgon completion bash
dalgon rules test "check this text"
```

`serve` starts the local router; `--public` listens wider and requires a token, and `--a2a` enables the agent-to-agent surface. `rpc` serves JSON-RPC over stdio or a local socket. `completion` prints shell completions for `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `powershell`, and `zsh`. `rules test` simulates one stream rule against the given text with `--source`, `--tool`, and `--path` selectors.

## Documentation

The same pages live inside the binaries and in the checkout. Use `dalgon docs` for `dal://` and `dalgona docs` for `dalgona://`.

Core use:

- [Command line](docs/cli.md)
- [Slash commands](docs/commands.md)
- [Settings in dal.toml](docs/config.md)
- [Providers and models](docs/models.md)
- [Tools, modes, and approval](docs/tools.md)

Extension and session control:

- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md)
- [Rules](docs/rules.md)
- [Symbols and structural editing](docs/symbols.md)
- [Sandbox](docs/sandbox.md)
- [System prompt](docs/prompt.md)
- [Sessions and compaction](docs/sessions.md)
- [Terminal and keys](docs/terminal.md)

Clients and embedding:

- [Protocol](docs/protocol.md)
- [Router and A2A](docs/serve.md)
- [Embed in Rust](docs/sdk.md)
- [Build a client](docs/integrate.md)
- [Example plugins](docs/examples.md)
- [Philosophy: one door](docs/philosophy.md)

Dalgona product:

- [Batteries](dalgona/docs/batteries.md)
- [Settings that differ](dalgona/docs/config.md)
- [Orchestration](dalgona/docs/orchestration.md)
- [Eval packs](dalgona/docs/eval.md)
- [Dalgona philosophy](dalgona/docs/philosophy.md)
- [Dalgona readme](dalgona/README.md)

Project contracts:

- [Concepts](CONCEPTS.md)
- [Design](DESIGN.md)
- [Branding and names](BRANDING.md)
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
- [License](LICENSE.md)

## Development

No `CONTRIBUTING.md` is checked in.

Work from the repository root. It holds one Cargo workspace and one `Cargo.lock`. Use the latest stable Rust toolchain.

Run the checked-in gates before review:

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked
cargo deny --locked check
```

Regenerate the dal manual after doc changes with the `docs-gen` command recorded in `AGENTS.md`. Keep Linux, macOS, and Windows behavior in mind. Do not publish a crate, create or push a tag, create a release, or run a release workflow without explicit approval.

Report issues and propose changes as GitHub issues and pull requests against `gosuda/dalgona`.

## License

Dal and dalgona are source-available under the Sustainable Use License, Version 1.0, with licensor `metaphorics`. Read the full terms in [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md).

This repository also includes Starlark translations of examples from pi (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner, used under the MIT License; the license text is in [docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md).

In process, the Rust interface of the Host and Agent seam carries five operations over one snapshot, one change stream, one command path, one request and answer pair, one blob read; the TUI uses these and nothing else. Across processes, a JSON-RPC protocol carries the same operations, served by `dalgon rpc` over stdio or a local socket, with a JSON Schema for every message; `docs/read` serves both manuals.

## Plugins in Starlark

A plugin is a directory with one `plugin.star` in the data root. A plugin publishes one `plugin` value that registers tools, commands, hooks, skills, rules, and prompt text, and it declares the operations each tool and hook may request; every effect still needs your approval. Nine lifecycle events exist, each with a declared result type; a Rust extension sees a tenth. Questions travel as data to whichever way in you use. Load is free of compile steps. A broken plugin stops startup and names `path:line:col`. `/reload` re-evaluates and prints counts (for example `Reloaded 2 plugins: 3 tools. New turns use them. A running turn keeps the plugins it started with.`); on failure it prints `reload failed: <rendered error>` and `the previous plugin set stays live`. A plugin that loads in dalgon loads in dalgona. A plugin runs with your permissions, so read it before you install it.

## Models

Four API families exist. Run `dalgon login`, then pick a model. `/model` and `/thinking` change them in a session.

## History you can trust

Each session is a journal; a record counts as saved only after it is synced to disk. A session is a tree; `-c` continues, `-r` resumes; `/export` writes a file you can share yourself.

## Context you control

The system prompt is built from parts you control (`AGENTS.md` files, `SYSTEM.md`, skills, rules, plugin sections); `dal://prompt` lists them. Compaction starts by default at 85 percent of the context window. Long, stable text can go out as an image and the exact text stays readable at `letter://<id>`.

## Tools and approval

Normal mode gives the model `read`, `search`, `patch`, and `exec`; eval-first adds `eval`; eval-only leaves only `eval` visible. A call you deny outside `eval` is denied inside it, and `eval` is not a sandbox. `patch` speaks several edit styles, one setting picks the style, and the style follows the model. By default dal asks before every `patch` and every `exec`. `--approval ask|edits|all` carries the ladder. When no person can answer, dal denies and says why. An optional sandbox, off by default, guards the home directory.

## Steer or follow up

You can type while dal works. A steer reaches the model at the next safe point. A follow-up waits for the turn to end. Stop ends the turn at once.

## Many ways in, one protocol

| Way in | Start |
|---|---|
| Terminal (inline) | `dal` |
| Terminal (fullscreen) | `dal` with fullscreen screen |
| Print | `dalgon` print flags |
| JSON | `dalgon` JSON flags |
| ACP | editor ACP adapter |
| RPC | `dalgon rpc` |
| Router | `dalgon serve` |
| A2A | `dalgon serve --a2a` |

`dalgon serve` listens on your machine only unless you add `--public`, which requires a token. No desktop, web, or mobile app ships; any such app is a client of the protocol, not a fork.

## Built for large runs

One session can run more than 500 subagents or more than 200 shell commands at once and still answer your keys. The gate measures it: RSS under 256 MiB, open files under 2048, keypress echo P99 under 24 ms, against a scripted model. These are test gates, not promises about your machine.

## Text in every language

dal measures text the way your terminal draws it; the cursor, wrapping, and cuts never split a character.

## The manual is inside

dal documents itself at `dal://`; dalgona adds `dalgona://`; the model reads pages with `read`; you read them with `dalgon docs`.

## dalgona

dalgona is dal with batteries, and every built-in battery is enabled by default through dal's same public extension door. The built-in batteries are orchestration, history, quality, judged, web, work, MCP, review, ask, skills, and ttsr-rules. By default, Dalgona enables symbol search, AST edit, the `hashline` edit style, and the complexity guard; it also provides plan and todo, rich ask, web search and fetch, an MCP client, and a review loop. It keeps its own configuration, data, and sessions. Dalgona builds only against released dal crates. dal and dalgona are distributed under the Sustainable Use License; the licensor is `metaphorics`.

## What we did not build

No MCP client in dal (dalgona ships one; a plugin can reach HTTP services with the `net.fetch` operation). No plugins from the workspace. No sandbox by default and no network restriction. No plan or todo in dal (dalgona ships both). No subagents in dal by default (the `agents` operations are one door away). No LSP, ever, in either product (search plus AST edit is the surface). No upload (`/share` writes a file). No self-rebuild (`/reload` reloads plugins). Nothing but Starlark in `eval`. No second store (the journal is the only store). No browser front end in the binary.

## Install

```sh
cargo install dalgon
cargo install dalgona
cargo binstall dalgon
cargo binstall dalgona
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/dalgon-v0.1.0/dalgon-installer.sh | sh
```

```powershell
powershell -c "irm https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/dalgon-v0.1.0/dalgon-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Quickstart

```sh
dalgon login
dal
dalgon docs
```

## Documentation

Read `dal://` for dal and `dalgona://` for dalgona; `dalgon docs` prints pages.

## License

dal and dalgona are distributed under the Sustainable Use License with licensor `metaphorics`; the text is in `LICENSE.md` at the repository root.

This repository also includes Starlark translations of examples from pi (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner, used under the MIT License; the license text is in `docs/examples.md` and on the `examples` page of this manual.

task: Pin native release smoke runners

files.pre:
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      plan:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  release-available:
    if: fromJson(inputs.plan).releases[0].app_name == 'dalgon' && fromJson(inputs.plan).releases[1] == null
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Check exact dalgon package and release assets
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}"
          test "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "dalgon-v$version"
          curl -fsSL "https://index.crates.io/da/lg/dalgon" | grep -F "\"vers\":\"$version\""
          curl -fsSL -o /dev/null "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/dalgon-installer.sh"
  smoke-install:
    needs: release-available
    if: fromJson(inputs.plan).releases[0].app_name == 'dalgon' && fromJson(inputs.plan).releases[1] == null
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, os: ubuntu-latest, script: sh, mode: installer }
          - { target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, script: sh, mode: installer }
          - { target: x86_64-apple-darwin, os: macos-15-intel, script: sh, mode: installer }
          - { target: aarch64-apple-darwin, os: macos-latest, script: sh, mode: installer }
          - { target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, os: windows-latest, script: pwsh, mode: installer }
          - { target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, os: windows-11-arm, script: pwsh, mode: installer }
          - { target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, os: ubuntu-latest, mode: cargo-install }
          - { target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, os: ubuntu-latest, mode: binstall }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - name: Update Rust
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'cargo-install' || matrix.mode == 'binstall' }}
        run: rustup update stable --no-self-update
      - name: Install dalgon (shell installer)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'installer' && matrix.script == 'sh' }}
        run: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/dalgon-installer.sh" | sh
      - name: Version check (shell)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'installer' && matrix.script == 'sh' }}
        run: |
          expected="dalgon ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}"
          for b in dalgon dal dl; do
            command -v "$b"
            "$b" --version | grep -Fx "$expected"
          done
      - name: Reinstall dalgon (shell idempotency)
        if: ${{ matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu' && matrix.mode == 'installer' && matrix.script == 'sh' }}
        run: |
          before="$(dalgon --version)"
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/dalgon-installer.sh" | sh
          after="$(dalgon --version)"
          test "$before" = "$after"
          expected="dalgon ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}"
          test "$after" = "$expected"
          for b in dalgon dal dl; do
            "$b" --version | grep -Fx "$expected"
          done
      - name: Install dalgon (PowerShell installer)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'installer' && matrix.script == 'pwsh' }}
        shell: pwsh
        run: irm "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona/releases/download/$env:GITHUB_REF_NAME/dalgon-installer.ps1" | iex
      - name: Version check (PowerShell)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'installer' && matrix.script == 'pwsh' }}
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $expected = "dalgon " + $env:GITHUB_REF_NAME.Substring("dalgon-v".Length)
          foreach ($b in "dalgon", "dal", "dl") {
            $out = (& $b --version | Out-String).Trim()
            if ($out -ne $expected) { throw "version mismatch for ${b}: got '$out'" }
          }
      - name: Install dalgon from crates.io
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'cargo-install' }}
        run: cargo install dalgon --version "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}" --locked
      - name: Version check (cargo install)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'cargo-install' }}
        run: |
          expected="dalgon ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}"
          for b in dalgon dal dl; do
            "$HOME/.cargo/bin/$b" --version | grep -Fx "$expected"
          done
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@ab6895351a88b908e96a4697860d4ffea5e57dbe # v2
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'binstall' }}
        with:
          tool: cargo-binstall@latest
      - name: Install dalgon with cargo-binstall
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'binstall' }}
        run: |
          cargo binstall --no-confirm --strategies crate-meta-data "dalgon@${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}" 2>&1 | tee binstall.log
          grep -F "releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/dalgon-" binstall.log
      - name: Version check (binstall)
        if: ${{ matrix.mode == 'binstall' }}
        run: |
          expected="dalgon ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#dalgon-v}"
          for b in dalgon dal dl; do
            "$HOME/.cargo/bin/$b" --version | grep -Fx "$expected"
          done

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["gates", "crates/*"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.90"
license-file = "../LICENSE.md"
repository = "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona"

[workspace.dependencies]
allocative = "=0.3.6"
blake3 = "=1.8.2"
schemars = "=1.2.2"
serde = { version = "=1.0.229", features = ["derive", "rc"] }
sonic-rs = "=0.5.10"
shuttle = "=0.9.4"
thiserror = "=2.0.21"
uuid = { version = "=1.26.1", features = ["v7"] }
jiff = { version = "=0.2.37", features = ["serde"] }
toml = "=1.1.6"
toml_edit = "=0.25.15+spec-1.1.0"
proptest = "=1.11.0"
png = "=0.18.1"
unicode-width = "=0.2.2"
unicode-segmentation = { version = "=1.13.3", default-features = false }
tracing = "=0.1.44"
futures = "=0.3.34"
reqwest = { version = "=0.13.5", features = ["rustls", "json", "stream"] }
url = "=2.5.8"
globset = "=0.4.20"
regex-automata = "=0.4.18"
tempfile = "=3.27.0"
tokio = "=1.53.1"
tokio-util = "=0.7.19"
tokio-tungstenite = { version = "=0.30.0", features = ["rustls-tls-webpki-roots"] }
base64 = "=0.22.1"
hyper = "=1.11.1"
hyper-util = "=0.1.21"
bytes = "=1.12.1"
sha2 = "=0.11.0"
regex = "=1.13.1"
process-wrap = { version = "=10.0.1", features = ["tokio1", "process-group", "job-object", "kill-on-drop"] }
rustix = { version = "=1.1.5", features = ["process"] }
landlock = "=0.4.7"
similar = "=3.2.0"
dal-core = { path = "crates/dal-core", version = "=0.1.0" }
dal-agent = { path = "crates/dal-agent", version = "=0.1.0" }
dal-provider = { path = "crates/dal-provider", version = "=0.1.0" }

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"
missing_docs = "warn"
unused_lifetimes = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
correctness = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }
suspicious = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
complexity = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
perf = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "warn"
panic = "warn"
allow_attributes = "deny"
allow_attributes_without_reason = "deny"
exit = "deny"
disallowed_methods = "deny"
# Fast feedback: line tables keep backtraces readable while compiling much
# faster than full debug info; the few runtime-heavy dependencies stay
# optimized so test execution stays fast.
[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"

[profile.dev.package.sonic-rs]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.blake3]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.regex]
opt-level = 2
[profile.dev.package.ratatui]
opt-level = 2
[profile.dev.package.proptest]
opt-level = 2

[profile.dist]
inherits = "release"

task: Describe the digest lookup cf-pin runs

files.pre:
# dalgona-box on Cloudflare

Release flow for the box container image.

## Publish

Push a `v*` tag. `.github/workflows/box-image.yml` builds the
multi-arch image and pushes two tags: the version and the commit sha.
Backport and prerelease tags must not move a shared reference, so the
workflow never publishes `latest`.

## Pin

Cloudflare must run an immutable reference. After the release
finishes, resolve the published digest and pin it:

    just cf-pin <tag>

`<tag>` is the version or commit sha the release published. The
recipe hashes the raw manifest with `docker buildx imagetools inspect
--raw` and writes `ghcr.io/gosuda/dalgona-box@sha256:<digest>` into
`wrangler.jsonc`. It then runs `just cf-deploy-check` to prove the
pin. Commit the result.

`just cf-deploy-check` fails unless the image is a digest pin, so run
it as the deploy step before `wrangler deploy`. `just cf-check` stays
limited to typecheck and lint and never blocks on the pin.

files.pre:
# dalgona-box on Cloudflare

## Box tokens

The Go client sends `DALGONA_TOKEN` to the worker. The worker checks
it in constant time and accepts only that value. Each box gets its own
token. The token is HMAC-SHA256 over the box name keyed by
`DALGONA_TOKEN`. The durable object reads the box name from
`ctx.id.name` and fails with 500 when it is missing. It sets
`DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN` to the box token and replaces the Authorization
header with the box token before proxying into the container. A box
token cannot call worker routes.

# dalgona-box on Cloudflare

## Box tokens

The Go client sends `DALGONA_TOKEN` to the worker. The worker checks
it in constant time and accepts only that value. Each box gets its own
token. The token is HMAC-SHA256 over the box name keyed by
`DALGONA_TOKEN`. The durable object reads the box name from
`ctx.id.name` and fails with 500 when it is missing. It sets
`DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN` to the box token and replaces the Authorization
header with the box token before proxying into the container. A box
token cannot call worker routes.

A box that an earlier worker version started still holds `DALGONA_TOKEN`
as its box token. After you deploy this version, destroy and create each
existing box again. Until then the worker sends that box a token it does
not accept, and the box keeps a credential that opens every box.
Destroying a box discards its changes that you did not pull. First run
`dalgona pull <thread-id>` for each thread whose changes you need. Then
archive the threads of the box and run `dalgona runner gc --yes`, which
deletes each box whose threads are all archived. `dalgona cloud down`
refuses Cloudflare boxes.

# Exec server

## Purpose

The exec server runs processes and filesystem operations through one `Local` runner. A `Remote` runner calls it over a bidirectional stream. The same wire protocol works over standard input and output, an in-process stream, or a websocket.

## Framing

- Messages MUST use JSON-RPC 2.0. Each message MUST occupy one line. The maximum line size is 16 MiB.
- Requests MUST contain `id`, `method`, and `params`. The server MUST ignore unknown parameter fields.
- File and process output bytes MUST use standard base64 in `dataBase64`.
- Malformed JSON MUST produce error `-32700`. An unknown method MUST produce `-32601`. Invalid parameters MUST produce `-32602`.
- A missing process MUST produce `-32001`. A missing file MUST produce `-32002`. Other operation failures MUST produce `-32000`.
- The server MUST close the stream when cancellation ends the read operation. The client MUST wake every pending call when the stream closes.

## Methods

### `initialize`

Params contain `clientName`. The result contains `environmentInfo.executorVersion`.

`NewRemote` MUST compare this version with the local binary version. A mismatch MUST fail with:

```
runner: box <id> runs dalgona <v1>; this is <v2>; use the matching box image
```

An unstamped binary MUST use `(devel)` as its version.

### Process methods

`process/start` params contain `processId`, `argv`, `cwd`, `env`, and `sandbox`. `env` is an object. `sandbox` contains `mode` and `writableRoots`. The server MUST pass these values to `Local.Start`. `Remote.Start` MUST send sandbox mode `off`, because the box is the sandbox. A repeated `processId` MUST NOT start a second process. A request arriving over the websocket box channel MUST NOT weaken the sandbox below the server start mode: when the server floor is `workspace-write`, `process/start` with any other mode MUST fail with `-32602`. The floor is `workspace-write` only when the server itself started with `DALGONA_SANDBOX_MODE=workspace-write`; otherwise the box is the sandbox and `off` stays allowed.

`process/read` params contain `processId` and `offset`. The result contains `dataBase64`, `next`, `exit`, `alive`, and `path`. A non-null `exit` contains `code`, `signal`, and `endedAtMs`.

`process/signal` params contain `processId` and `signal`. The signal MUST be `term` or `kill`.

`process/terminate` params contain `processId`. It MUST send `kill`. The result MUST contain `running`.

### Filesystem methods

- `fs/readFile` takes `path` and returns `dataBase64`.
- `fs/writeFile` takes `path`, `dataBase64`, and numeric `mode`. A mode outside 0 to 4294967295 MUST produce `-32602`. When `DALGONA_SYNCFS` names a directory, the server MUST call `syncfs` on that directory after the rename completes. A sync failure MUST fail the call.
- `fs/getMetadata` takes `path` and returns `name`, `size`, `mode`, `modTimeMs`, `isDirectory`, and `isFile`.
- `fs/readDirectory` takes `path` and returns `entries`. Each entry uses the metadata fields above.
- `fs/remove` takes `path`.

The server MUST preserve the runner operation semantics. The client MUST preserve `ErrProcessNotFound` and `fs.ErrNotExist` through `errors.Is`.

## Server command

`ExecServerMain` accepts `--listen stdio://` or `--listen ws://IP:PORT`, plus `--root DIR` and optional `--data DIR`.

Websocket mode MUST require `DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN` with at least 32 characters. Startup without it MUST fail with:

```
exec-server: ws listen needs DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN (32+ characters)
```

Every websocket request MUST carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server MUST compare tokens in constant time. A wrong token MUST receive HTTP 401. Other paths MUST receive HTTP 404.

Path `/` serves the exec protocol. Path `/bridge` calls the supplied `BridgeFunc`. A missing bridge MUST produce HTTP 503.

With `--data`, the server MUST create `<data>/workspace` and `<data>/home`. It MUST link the selected root to the workspace and set `HOME` to the home directory. An existing non-symlink root MUST NOT be removed.

## Bootstrap

`Bootstrap` MUST probe `uname -m` and `~/.dalgona/bin/dalgona --version`. It MUST support `amd64` and `arm64`. The remote version is the last whitespace-separated field of the `--version` output. A version equal to the local binary version MUST skip the upload. A version mismatch MUST select the matching local Linux binary and upload it to `~/.dalgona/bin/dalgona` with mode 0755.

The upload MUST use standard base64 with 76-column lines, each ending in a newline. It MUST run `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$1")" && head -c "$3" | base64 -d > "$1" && chmod "$2" "$1"` with the destination, `0755`, and the exact encoded byte count. The box MUST stop reading after that count, so the upload MUST NOT depend on stdin EOF. A stream with `CloseWrite` MUST still half-close after the last byte. A stream without it MUST stay open until the command exits.

A missing sibling binary MUST report:

```
runner: no linux/<arch> dalgona binary next to <exe>; build it with GOOS=linux GOARCH=<arch> CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o <path> ./cmd/dalgona
```

A box without `base64` MUST report:

```
runner: box <id> has no base64; use an image with coreutils
```

## Workspace upload

`Upload` MUST enumerate `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z` in a git work tree. Outside a work tree it MUST walk regular files and skip `.git`. Both paths MUST skip `.dalgona-baseline`.

- At most 16 file writes MAY be in flight.
- Remote paths MUST be `/workspace/<slash-relative-path>`.
- Files MUST retain their permission bits. Files with mode 0755 MUST also pass through the prescribed `chmod +x` batch.
- The server MUST run `git init -q && git add -A && git write-tree` in `/workspace` and require exit code zero.
- The returned tree ID MUST be written to `/workspace/.dalgona-baseline`.
- Process output MUST be read until the durable exit record appears. A process without an exit record MUST NOT be treated as complete.

- `fs/writeFile` takes `path`, `dataBase64`, numeric `mode`, and `offset`. Offset zero MUST replace the file atomically. A nonzero `offset` MUST write one chunk of a paged upload at that byte position; the client MUST split large files into 1 MiB chunks so no request line exceeds the 16 MiB framing cap. A mode outside 0 to 4294967295 MUST produce `-32602`. A negative `offset` MUST produce `-32602`. # Web UI server

## Scope

`internal/webui` serves the built web UI and relays JSON-RPC between a browser and the daemon.
The caller supplies the listen address, the token, the TLS files, a daemon dialer, and an output writer.

## Assets

The package MUST embed `internal/webui/dist` with `//go:embed all:dist`.
If the root of `dist` holds no entry other than `.gitkeep`, every path except `/rpc` MUST return status 503 with the body `web UI not built; run just web`.
Otherwise the server MUST serve the files in `dist`. `/` MUST serve `index.html`.

## Token

A loopback listen address is `localhost` or a loopback IP. Every other address, including an empty host, is a LAN address.

A LAN address MUST have a configured token of at least 32 characters. Characters are Unicode code points.
Otherwise startup MUST fail before it listens, with this exact error:

```text
web: listening on <addr> needs [web] token (32+ characters)
```

`<addr>` is the configured listen address.

A loopback address MUST use the configured token when one is set.
Otherwise it MUST use a new token for each start. The token MUST be 32 bytes from `crypto/rand`, encoded as unpadded base64url.

The server MUST compare SHA-256 digests of the presented token and the expected token with `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`.

## TLS

When `CertFile` and `KeyFile` are both set, the server MUST serve TLS with `tls.VersionTLS13` as the minimum version.
When only one of them is set, startup MUST fail with `web: cert_file and key_file must both be set`.
A file that does not load MUST fail startup with an error that starts with `web: load cert_file and key_file: `.

## Startup output

All output goes to the caller's writer. Each message is one line.

On a LAN address without TLS, the server MUST write this line once, before the URL:

```text
web: the token travels unencrypted on <addr>; set cert_file and key_file to use TLS
```

The server MUST then write `http://<addr>/#token=<token>`, or `https://<addr>/#token=<token>` with TLS.
In both lines `<addr>` is the bound listener address. The token stays in the URL fragment, so a browser does not send it in page requests.

## RPC relay

`/rpc` MUST require the query parameter `token`. A missing or wrong token MUST get status 401. The server MUST NOT dial the daemon for a rejected request.

For an accepted token, the server MUST dial the daemon with a 10 second limit before the websocket upgrade.
A dial failure MUST get status 502 and MUST write `web: dial daemon: <error>`.
The upgrade MUST use `github.com/coder/websocket` with its default origin check.

The relay MUST NOT decode, re-encode, or change message bytes.

- Browser to daemon: each websocket text message MUST become one line: the message bytes followed by one `\n`, in one write.
- Daemon to browser: each `\n`-terminated line MUST become one websocket text message without the `\n`. A line longer than the 64 KiB read buffer MUST be streamed as one message.
- A browser message MUST be at most 16 MiB minus 1 byte, which is the daemon line limit without the newline.

Failure behavior:

- A binary message MUST close the websocket with status 1003 (`rpc message is not text`). The daemon MUST receive no bytes from it.
- A text message that contains `\n` MUST close the websocket with status 1007 (`rpc message contains a newline`). The daemon MUST receive no bytes from it.
- When the daemon closes, the server MUST drop an unterminated last line and close the websocket with status 1001.
- When the browser closes, the server MUST close the daemon connection.
- Any other relay failure MUST close the websocket with status 1011 and MUST write `web: rpc relay: <error>`.

## Server limits and shutdown

The HTTP server MUST set a 10 second header read timeout, a 30 second read timeout, a 60 second write timeout, and a 120 second idle timeout. A websocket connection is not subject to these limits after the upgrade.

When the context ends, the server MUST stop accepting, end every live relay, close every daemon connection, and only then return.
A clean shutdown MUST return `nil`. Shutdown waits at most 5 seconds for open page requests.

## Browser client

The client in `web/` reads the token from the URL fragment and opens `/rpc`. It speaks the Codex v2 protocol, and `web/src/lib/validation.ts` checks every payload against the shapes in `internal/rpc/testdata/codex-schema`.

### Layout

- Above 52rem the page has two columns, the thread list and the workspace. The workspace holds the status bar, the thread heading, the transcript, and the composer. The transcript scrolls inside its own column.
- At 52rem or narrower the page stacks the parts and the document scrolls. The thread list keeps a maximum height of 18rem.
- At 320px nothing may clip or scroll sideways.
- The transcript follows new output only while the reader is within 32px of its end. It follows the transcript at wide widths and the window at narrow widths. Opening a thread follows its end.

### Status bar

The status bar shows the connection state as text. The turn state follows it as text: `Working`, `Turn completed`, `Turn interrupted`, or `Turn failed`.

It also shows model, approval, sandbox, runner, and advisor. The advisor entry comes from `dalgona/advisor/status`. The client loads it when a thread opens or starts, and again after each `dalgona/advisor/note` for the open thread. It shows one of:

- One advisor: its status (`idle`, `reviewing`, `halted`, or `off`) and its note count.
- Several advisors: `<n> advisors · <k> reviewing`.
- `off` when the server answers `-32001`.
- `unavailable` for any other failure.

No advisor failure opens the error banner.

### Transcript

- Item statuses read `Running`, `Done`, `Failed`, or `Declined`.
- Unknown item kinds show their type in plain words, such as `Web search`.
- A `dynamicToolCall` item with tool `advisor` shows as a note card: `advisor · <severity>: <note>`. The note is the text of `contentItems`. The severity is always text. The card's inline-start border marks the severity as a second cue.
- Other dynamic tools show their `contentItems` text as output.
- `turn/plan/updated` shows the latest plan of the current turn as a checklist. Each step has a text status: `Done`, `In progress`, or `Pending`. The step in progress carries `aria-current="step"`. A new turn clears the plan.
- The streaming cursor and "Reasoning in progress" show only while the turn runs.
- A failed turn ends with `The turn failed: <message>. Send your message again to retry, or start a new thread.`
- A turn that is retrying after an error shows `Retrying after an error: <message>`.
- An interrupted turn shows `Turn interrupted. Send a message to continue.`

### Empty states and errors

- With no open thread the transcript says `Pick a thread or start a new one`. When connected, it adds that earlier threads are in the list. When not connected, it says to connect to dalgona.
- With no connection the thread list says `Threads unavailable` and does not claim that no threads exist. A thread without a name shows its preview once.
- A failed connection reads `Unable to connect to dalgona: <detail>. Check that dalgona web is still running, then select Reconnect.`
- Selecting Reconnect loads the thread list, then resumes the open thread on the new connection, so its transcript keeps streaming. The resume MUST keep queued follow-ups. Opening a different thread MUST discard them.
- Other request failures read `<action>: <detail>. Reconnect and try again.`
- In the approval dialog, Decline uses the quiet style. The danger hue marks only Interrupt.

# Sandbox services

The daemon MUST expose one service seam for remote boxes. A service MUST create, attach, connect, and destroy a box. A pipe service MUST run commands in `/workspace`. The exec-server endpoint MUST run `$HOME/.dalgona/bin/dalgona exec-server --listen stdio:// --root /workspace`. The bridge endpoint MUST run `$HOME/.dalgona/bin/dalgona bridge`. Bootstrap failures MUST fail attach.

## Modal

`NewFromEnv` MUST use the Modal default profile. The profile MUST come from the Modal environment or `~/.modal.toml`.

Create MUST use the app `dalgona`. It MUST create the app when absent. The default image MUST be `docker.io/library/buildpack-deps:stable`. A configured image MUST replace the default.

Create MUST use a named volume with version 2. The volume name MUST equal the box name. Create MUST mount the volume at `/data`. The sandbox name MUST have the form `<box>-<n>`, where `n` starts at 1. Name collisions MUST advance `n`. Create MUST stop after 100 collisions.

The sandbox MUST have a 24-hour timeout and a one-hour idle timeout. It MUST set `HOME=/data/home` and `DALGONA_SYNCFS=/data`. Its entry command MUST create `/data/workspace` and `/data/home`. It MUST link `/workspace` to `/data/workspace` and then sleep indefinitely.

A box identifier MUST have the form `<sandbox-id>/<volume-name>`.

Attach MUST poll the sandbox. A running sandbox MUST retain its identifier. A finished sandbox MUST cause the service to create the next numbered sandbox on the same volume. Attach MUST return the new identifier. It MUST run bootstrap against the replacement. A bootstrap failure MUST terminate the replacement without deleting the volume. The volume MUST retain `/workspace` and `/data/home` across this replacement.

Destroy MUST terminate the sandbox and wait for termination. It MUST then delete the named volume. A termination failure MUST prevent volume deletion.

A process MUST pipe stdin, stdout, and stderr. Reads MUST serve stdout. Process closure MUST close all three streams. A process wait MUST end no later than 25 hours after the wait starts.

## Sandbox0

`NewFromEnv` MUST require `SANDBOX0_TOKEN`. `SANDBOX0_BASE_URL` MUST override the default service URL when set.

Create MUST claim the configured template. An empty template MUST mean `default`. The claim MUST set a 1800-second soft lifetime, a zero hard lifetime, and automatic resume to false.

Create MUST run this workspace command through a CMD context:

```sh
mkdir -p /workspace 2>/dev/null || { sudo -n mkdir -p /workspace && sudo -n chown "$(id -u)" /workspace; }
```

A command error, missing exit code, or nonzero exit code MUST fail create. Create MUST delete the claimed sandbox before returning this error:

```text
runner: sandbox0 template <template> cannot create /workspace; use a template whose user can write it
```

Attach MUST return the same identifier. It MUST resume a paused sandbox and wait for the resume. A bootstrap failure MUST fail attach.

The writable root filesystem MUST persist across pause and resume. `/tmp` has no persistence guarantee. Paused processes MUST NOT be reported as live after resume.

Each open command stream MUST start a refresh task. The task MUST refresh the sandbox every 10 minutes. Stream closure or context cancellation MUST stop the task. Refresh failures MUST NOT close the stream.

The stream adapter MUST send each write as one `SendInput` call with an empty request identifier. Reads MUST return only stdout data. A read smaller than the available stdout chunk MUST retain the remainder for the next read. Reads MUST log stderr at debug level without returning it. A done message MUST return `io.EOF`. A zero-length read MUST NOT receive from the remote stream.

Close MUST send `TERM` before closing the remote stream. It MUST attempt the remote close after a signal failure. Repeated close calls MUST have no additional remote effect.

# Daemon service

## Run

`Run(ctx, home, newHost, serve)` MUST build the host before it touches the socket. The host factory opens the journal, and the journal takes the exclusive lock on `<home>/daemon.lock`. The daemon MUST NOT take a second lock.

When the lock is held by another process, `Run` MUST return `another dalgona process owns <home>`. It MUST NOT remove or replace `<home>/dalgona.sock` in this case.

After the lock is held, `Run` MUST remove a stale `dalgona.sock` and then listen on it. A failure to remove or listen MUST stop `Run` with an error.

`Run` MUST call `Host.Recover` once, in the background. Recovery MUST NOT delay the accept loop. Each connection MUST get its own `serve` call, so a client gets its `initialize` answer while recovery runs. Recovery errors MUST be logged. They MUST NOT stop the daemon.

When the context ends, `Run` MUST stop accepting, close every open connection, and wait for the connection and recovery work. It MUST then close the host and the journal, which releases the lock. Closing the listener removes the socket file. An accept failure that does not come from the context MUST stop `Run` with an error.

## Ensure

`Ensure` MUST reuse an accepting socket. If the socket is unavailable, it MUST start `<executable> daemon` detached and append stdout and stderr to `daemon.log`. On Unix the child MUST run in a new session. On Windows it MUST use `DETACHED_PROCESS` and `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`. `Ensure` MUST retry for five seconds. On timeout it MUST return `daemon did not start: see <home>/daemon.log`.

Two clients MAY start two daemons at the same time. The lock rule above makes the second daemon exit without effect on the first.

## User service

Linux installation MUST write `~/.config/systemd/user/dalgona.service` with `ExecStart=<absolute executable> daemon` and `Restart=always`, then run `systemctl --user enable --now dalgona.service`. macOS installation MUST write `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.dalgona.daemon.plist` with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`, then run `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>`. Windows installation MUST run `schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /TN dalgona /TR "<absolute executable> daemon" /F`. Uninstall MUST disable the service and remove the file or task.

Service commands MUST be injectable in tests. Installation errors MUST be returned.

## Commands

`dalgona` without a command, `-p`, `--resume`, `-c`, and `models` MUST reach the core only through a daemon connection from `Ensure`. The client MUST accept `-m <model>`, `--approval auto|ask|yolo`, `--sandbox workspace-write|off`, and `-C <directory>`. With `-p`, `--json` MUST print one JSON status line. `--resume` and `-c` MUST exclude each other.

`dalgona login [provider]` and `dalgona logout <provider>` MUST use `<home>/auth.json`. Without a remote selection, these commands MUST use the client credential store and MUST NOT require a daemon connection. With `--remote <name>`, login MUST authenticate inside the box through the daemon protocol. Login without a provider MUST list providers. The daemon's credential store MUST reread `auth.json` when its size, time, or identity changes, so a new login applies to the next model request. Writers MUST serialize on `<home>/auth.lock`, MUST reread the file under that lock, and MUST change only their own provider entry. When a changed `auth.json` cannot be reread, `Mask` MUST return `secret masking failed: auth.json could not be reread` and MUST record the error. A cached OAuth token MUST be dropped when the stored credential changes outside the daemon.

`dalgona daemon` MUST run `Run` with the dalgona host. It MUST stop cleanly on interrupt and on `SIGTERM`. The host MUST start the `[mcp_servers.*]` servers once. For each thread working directory, it MUST start the servers that enabled discovery sources name for that directory, except names that `[mcp_servers.*]` already uses. A thread's skills MUST come from `<home>/skills`, `<thread cwd>/.dalgona/skills`, and discovery for that directory. MCP servers MUST start in parallel and in the background, so they do not delay the socket. Each server MUST start within 30 seconds. A server that fails or times out MUST be logged and skipped. A thread's tool list MUST wait until its servers have started or failed. MCP clients MUST be closed when the host closes. The host MUST load `<home>/plugins/*.star`, MUST log each plugin file that fails, and MUST keep the plugins that load.

The dalgona host MUST bind `[runners.<name>]` runners through the remote binder and MUST use the local runner for every other runner name. `dalgona pull <thread>` and `dalgona runner gc [--yes]` MUST run inside the daemon through the protocol extensions `dalgona/remote/pull {threadId}` and `dalgona/remote/gc {yes}`, because the daemon holds the journal lock. Each extension MUST answer `{"exitCode":<int>,"output":<text>}`. Without `--yes`, `runner gc` MUST answer no to every destroy question. `dalgona cloud up|down|pull` MUST run in the client process.

`dalgona bridge` MUST splice standard input and output to a local `Ensure` connection. `dalgona exec-server` MUST serve the exec protocol and MUST use the same splice for its `/bridge` path. The TUI, `models`, `dalgona app-server`, `dalgona web`, `pull`, and `runner gc` MUST dial the local daemon through `Ensure`. When `--remote <name>` is given, or `remote` is set in configuration, they MUST dial the remote box daemon through the binder's bridge instead. The flag MUST win over the configuration. `bridge` and `exec-server` MUST NOT redirect their local listener with `--remote`.

`--config <key>=<value>`, `--config=<key>=<value>`, and `-c <key>=<value>` pairs MAY come before the `app-server` subcommand, as the Codex clients send them. When the first argument after these pairs is `app-server`, the pairs MUST reach the app-server command unchanged. In every other case, `-c` keeps its client meaning.

`dalgona service install|uninstall` MUST install or remove the platform user service. `dalgona codex install|uninstall|status` MUST manage or inspect the desktop override. `dalgona codex record --real <path> [args...]` MUST run the selected Codex executable and record protocol metadata in `<home>/census/<unix-seconds>.jsonl`. Without forwarded arguments, it MUST run `app-server`.

`dalgona run <file.star> [--arg k=v ...]` MUST run a durable Starlark workflow as defined in [starlark.md](starlark.md).

Inside herdr (`HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_PANE_ID` set), the TUI status MUST be reported as `working` while a turn runs, `blocked` while an approval waits, and `idle` otherwise. The reported `--seq` MUST be the sequence the TUI reports for the thread. A status without a thread MUST NOT be reported. While the thread stays the same, a status equal to the previous one or with a lower sequence MUST NOT be reported. A change of thread MUST reset this comparison. When `[herdr] subagent_panes` is true, each child spawn MUST open a pane that resumes the child. herdr commands MUST run on one worker, so they never block the TUI. Each command MUST time out after five seconds. While the worker is busy, only the newest status for each thread MUST wait; at most 64 pane requests MAY wait. On exit, the process MUST wait at most five seconds for waiting commands, MUST then cancel any command still running, and MUST then release the pane.

package daemon

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/gosuda/dalgona/internal/config"
	"github.com/gosuda/dalgona/internal/rpc"
)

const realDaemonEnv = "DALGONA_TEST_REAL_DAEMON"

func runRealDaemon() int {
	home := config.ProductDalgona.Home()
	pid := []byte(strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid()))
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(home, "daemon.pid"), pid, 0o600); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		return 1
	}
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	if err := Run(ctx, home, appHost, rpc.Serve); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

# Local runner

The local runner MUST store one directory per call. The directory MUST be `<dir>/<call_id>/`. It MUST contain the files `out`, `pid`, and `exit`. It MAY contain `pgid` and `cancel`.

Callers MUST escape a call id that contains `/`, such as a nested `<run>/<n>` cell call id, to a single path component before `Start`. A call id with `/` MUST NOT reach the runs directory.

The parent MUST start the shim detached. The invocation MUST be `<self> __shim --dir <runs/call_id> -- argv...`. On Linux `<self>` MUST be `/proc/self/exe`, so the shim and the parent are one build when an upgrade replaces the file at the start path. On macOS and Windows `<self>` MUST be `os.Executable()`. The runner passes writable roots to the shim in `DALGONA_SANDBOX_ROOTS`. The value is an internal format between the parent and the shim of one build. On Unix the parent MUST start the shim with `Setsid`. On Windows the parent MUST start the shim with `DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`.

`ProcessSpec.Argv[0]` equal to `@self` MUST resolve to the parent build: `/proc/self/exe` on Linux and `os.Executable()` on macOS and Windows. On a remote exec server it MUST resolve to the exec-server binary path.

`Start` MUST be idempotent. An existing call directory for the same call id MUST make `Start` return success. It MUST NOT start a second process. When `Start` fails after it creates the call directory, it MUST remove that directory, so a retry with the same call id starts the command.

The shim MUST write `pid` before it starts the command. `pid` MUST store the process id and the process start time. Recovery and `Read` MUST accept a process only when both values match. A recycled process id MUST NOT count as the shim. `Start` MUST write `pid` before it returns. The parent MUST write the same values as the shim. On Windows a write of at most 4 KiB whose staged bytes and writable state equal the existing regular file MAY keep the existing file instead of replacing it. On Windows a file replace that fails with a sharing violation or access denied MUST wait and retry for up to one second before it fails. The first `Read` after `Start` MUST report a live process when no `exit` exists.

The shim MUST start the command in a new process group on Unix. It MUST record the group id in `pgid`. On Windows it MUST assign the command to a named job object. On Windows it MUST start the command suspended. It MUST assign the suspended command to the job object. It MUST resume the command after the assignment. The shim MUST start the command on Windows with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. On Windows the shim MUST run a `cmd /C <command>` argv verbatim as `cmd /S /C "<command>"`. The `/S` switch MUST make `cmd` strip exactly the outer quote pair. The parent MUST reap the shim without waiting for the command in the caller.

`Read` MUST take a byte offset into `out`. It MUST return `Data`, `Next`, `Exit`, `Alive`, and `Path`. `Data` MUST be the bytes from the offset. `Next` MUST be the next unread offset. `Exit` MUST be the exit record when `exit` exists, otherwise unset. `Alive` MUST be true only when the stored pid and start time still name the shim. `Path` MUST name the `out` file. `Read` MUST check `exit` before taking the final output snapshot, and when `exit` appears after an empty check it MUST drain `out` again. A terminal response MUST carry every byte written before the exit record, across as many pages as that takes.

On Windows the runner MUST retry a call-directory file open that fails with a sharing violation. It MUST retry for up to one second and then fail. The rename that publishes the file can fail a concurrent open with a sharing violation. A sharing violation MUST NOT count as a missing file.

`Signal` MUST accept `TERM` and `KILL`. The caller MUST send `TERM` before `KILL`. On timeout the caller MUST wait 5 s after `TERM`, then send `KILL`. On Unix `Signal` MUST target the command process group. It MUST NOT signal the shim. On Windows `Signal` MUST kill the process tree through the job object. The shim MUST survive the signal and write the command exit record.

`Signal` MUST return success when `exit` exists. Otherwise it MUST write the file `cancel` before it reads `pid` or `pgid`. `cancel` MUST hold `TERM` or `KILL`. The write MUST use a temporary file and rename, then sync the call directory. A missing call directory MUST make `Signal` return `ErrProcessNotFound`. When `pid` or `pgid` does not exist yet, `Signal` MUST return success and leave the request to the shim. When `pid` names a gone process and `exit` does not exist, `Signal` MUST return `ErrProcessNotFound`. A process group that no longer exists MUST count as success. On macOS a group whose members have all exited but are not yet reaped MUST report EPERM instead of ESRCH. The runner MUST treat that EPERM as success when the group holds no live member. It MUST return EPERM when a live member remains.

The shim MUST read `cancel` after it writes `pid` and before it starts the command. If `cancel` exists, the shim MUST NOT start the command. It MUST write `exit` as for a command that the recorded signal stopped: on Unix `code` -1 and `signal` the signal text, on Windows `code` 1 for `TERM` and 137 for `KILL`. The shim MUST read `cancel` again after it writes `pgid` and assigns the job object. If `cancel` exists, the shim MUST send the recorded signal to the command itself. If that fails, it MUST kill the command process. Each side writes its own file before it reads the file of the other side. So a terminate request that arrives before `pid` or `pgid` exists MUST still stop the command, and the command MUST NOT outlive the request. `cancel` is on disk, so the request MUST survive a daemon restart.

A tool that signals a run MUST poll `Read` until `Exit` exists before the tool returns. The poll MUST stop at a bounded deadline. The tool MUST report a deadline timeout as an error.

The shim MUST pause at startup only when `DALGONA_SHIM_TEST_PAUSE` is set to `<phase>:<duration>`. Phase `pid` pauses before the shim writes `pid`. Phase `start` pauses after the first `cancel` check and before the command starts. Only tests MAY set this variable.

The shim MUST append stdout and stderr to `out`. After `out` reaches 1 GiB the shim MUST stop appending command bytes. It MUST append this line once:

```
[dalgona: output beyond 1 GiB discarded]
```

The shim MUST keep draining both pipes. The command MUST keep running until it exits. The cap is a storage limit. It is not a process limit.

The command environment MUST be the caller environment plus these defaults. Each default MUST apply only when that variable is unset:

- `CI=1`
- `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`
- `GIT_EDITOR=:`
- `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=:`
- `GIT_MERGE_AUTOEDIT=no`
- `GIT_PAGER=cat`
- `PAGER=cat`
- `EDITOR=:`
- `npm_config_yes=true`
- `PIP_NO_INPUT=1`

The shim MUST write `exit` by a temporary file and rename. `exit` MUST be JSON `{"code":N,"signal":"","ended_at":"RFC3339"}`. `code` MUST be the numeric exit code. `signal` MUST be the signal text, or empty. `ended_at` MUST be an RFC3339 timestamp.

On Linux, if `DALGONA_SYNCFS` is set, the shim MUST call `syncfs` on that path after the `exit` rename. It MUST NOT call `syncfs` before the rename completes. On other systems the variable MUST have no effect.

Crash recovery for class `Exec` MUST follow these rules. A recorded `exit` MUST complete the call with that output. A live shim MUST stay running until exit. A gone process with no `exit` MUST complete with the output so far and error `interrupted: the host restarted while this command ran; it may have partly run`. Recovery MUST set `recovered=interrupted`. Recovery MUST NOT start the command again.

File methods MUST be `ReadFile`, `WriteFile`, `Stat`, `ReadDir`, and `Remove`. `WriteFile` MUST write a temporary file and rename it. The write MUST keep the requested permission mode. On Windows `WriteFile` MUST replace a read-only destination file. The replaced file MUST keep the read-only attribute. Each method MUST stop when the context is cancelled before the operation. `ReadFile` and `Stat` MUST NOT follow a symbolic link in the final path component; the call MUST fail instead.

Output projection for `exec` MUST use `tool.Project` with `Keep` `Tail`. Output of 64 KiB or less MUST be returned whole. Larger output MUST keep the last 64 KiB. The cut MUST fall on a UTF-8 rune boundary. The projected text MUST end with this line, with `<N>` the total byte count and `<spill>` the `out` path:

```
[output truncated: <N> bytes total; full output: <spill>; page it with read offset/limit]
```
