# Changes by version

This page lists the user-visible changes in each version. The `/changelog` command prints it.

## Unreleased

- An eval cell can now ask the session judge one question (`judge.ask`) or up to 32 at once (`judge.batch`). The cell may request `judge.ask` or `judge.batch` only when that operation is in its `uses` and in `eval.uses`, and every eval cell receives the `judge` and `judge_batch` globals. See [tools](tools.md#the-eval-tool).
- Only an eval cell that declares `judge.ask` or `judge.batch` can ask the session judge; plugin handlers, commands, and models are refused at declaration.
- The `/login` provider picker puts an exact provider id first when the filter matches one: typing `openai` and pressing Enter starts the OpenAI sign-in, not a longer id like `azure-openai-responses` that only contains the text.
- A scoped model id offered by several providers is priced for admission from each listed row instead of failing as unpriced: the configured price for a `provider/id` key wins, then the live catalog price, then the compiled table. A route that names its provider also prices through its `provider/model` spelling.
- Provider definitions supply per-family auth, dialect, and request schema from one source, and scoped models are gated through config limits.
- Products declare typed startup settings, and the settings picker confirms them: an edit rewrites `dal.toml` atomically with owner-only permissions, preserves your comments and formatting, and is refused when invalid. A saved next-start value shows beside the running value when they differ, and a remote connection refuses product setting edits. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#tables-with-their-own-keys).
- `dalgon dev run` evaluates a scenario with the invoking product's configuration kind, defaults, and extensions instead of a fixed one.
- A URI scheme resolver runs with the identity of the extension that registered the scheme, so it queries records through its own capability-scoped services. See [Plugins](plugins.md).
- Breaking Rust API: `ProductFactory` gains `config_product` and `settings`, and `Reply::Choose` gains `thinking_levels`. Callers that construct either value must provide the new fields, and pattern matches must handle them or use `..`.
- A user plugin can replace one bundled skill or rule with `replace = True` and `battery = "<bundled extension>"`: for example the `find-anything` skill owned by `skills`, or the `fabricated-unavailable-tool-call` rule owned by `quality`. Without the pair a name clash is still refused; the replacement moves only that record and inherits no service, tool, or grant. Removing the claim restores the bundled record on reload. See [Plugins](plugins.md#add-skills-rules-and-prompt-text).
- `[limits.plugins]` Starlark budgets take positive integers and report the key to raise: a real load, handler, or eval-cell breach names `raise limits.plugins.<key> to allow more`, while a user `fail()` that repeats the vendor wording gains no such remedy. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#tables-with-their-own-keys).
- A reopened session shows the model, thinking level, approval mode, execution mode, and name its journal recorded. Before, it showed the defaults of the host that opened it. A session that never chose a model still follows the configured default and names no model. Changing another setting no longer makes the default look selected. See [sessions](sessions.md).
- API model routes can name their provider. A route that does, such as a row picked in the model picker, resolves exactly that provider. It never resolves another provider or a synthetic model that lists the same id. It fails with a typed error when the provider is unavailable. Routes without a provider resolve as before.
- `models/list` rows add `route` and `reference`. The remote model picker selects by route for the session only and scopes by provider. Servers without them keep the older selection by name. The protocol version is still 1.
- Fix remote API-key sign-in outcome reporting. See [remote sign-in](commands.md#remote-sign-in).
- Persist turn identities before acknowledging queued work. Cancelling a queued turn no longer invalidates later journal entries. Restarting a session cannot reuse its reserved identity. Queued text is not restored.
- New turn-ID reservations use journal format 2. Other records retain format 1. Existing journals need no conversion. A reader must support format 2 after a reservation is written. See [durable turn identities](sessions.md#durable-turn-identities).
- Rust code that uses `dal-tools` can call `patch::styles::tier` again, also in constant expressions. It returns the prompt-intensity tier of an edit style.
- Reject unsupported Unicode duration units with a configuration error instead of panicking.
- Report incomplete patch rollback with the affected paths and retained backup locations. Continue restoring other files when one restoration fails.
- Retain service cancellation receipts until service admission consumes them, so repeated cancellations do not strand `ask` or `run` capacity.
- Add `ArtifactFile::StatusTxt` (`status.txt`) to task isolation directories, saved atomically with file mode 0600 on Unix. Rust callers with exhaustive matches on `ArtifactFile` must handle the new variant.
- Azure OpenAI entries resolve their endpoint from an explicit `base_url` first, then `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, then `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME`. A resource name an entry never needs is never validated and cannot fail setup; entry `api_version` and `deployments` values win over the matching environment values. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#azure-openai).
- Devin request failures now carry a short readable detail from the server reply when it holds one. Markup pages are skipped, unsafe characters are rejected, the text is bounded, and credentials stay redacted.
- Google account-validation failures now show the verification link the server names, when its error calls for account validation. The link is rendered, never opened on its own; ordinary quota messages are unchanged.
- Add canonical `github-copilot` device sign-in (`dalgon login github-copilot`), supporting optional GitHub Enterprise domains, user verification code display, and completion polling. Stored credentials persist to `auth.json` as an API-key token or structured envelope containing the token, enterprise domain, and discovered account endpoint. Sign-in applies best-effort model policy enablement without fetching the model catalogue at sign-in time. API keys can also be supplied via `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `--api-key`.
- Bedrock provider readiness checks captured AWS credential sources (environment variables, shared configuration and credential files, SSO, credential processes, or instance roles) and stored bearer tokens across effective configured provider families and aliases. `dalgon login status` reports Bedrock entries as `ready` or `not configured` instead of attempting an interactive sign-in flow.
- In GitHub Copilot device sign-in, submitting a blank enterprise domain defaults to `github.com`. Prompts for required OAuth authorization codes or redirect URLs continue to require non-empty input.
- Cancelling CLI device-code authorization with Ctrl+C during completion polling restores the terminal cleanly and cancels the sign-in request without saving incomplete credentials.
- Prefer device authorization over an API key in terminal sign-in when the provider does not offer browser sign-in, matching the interactive CLI.
- Fix terminal cancellation reporting. The terminal now says what happened to a cancellation:
  - A refused cancellation request reports its own error while that turn is still running.
  - A transport error while waiting reports that error. The run no longer finishes as if nothing failed.
  - When the turn already finished, quit and resume complete normally with no cancellation line.
  - A lost replay, a closed subscription, or no confirmation in time reports that the cancellation could not be confirmed. It asks you to resume the session to check its state.
  - Resuming after such a failure closes both the old session and the opened replacement session.
  - A turn that ends cancelled still shows the inline cancellation line. Any other end shows no line. Fullscreen never shows the inline line.
  - On quit, an earlier terminal error still wins over a later failure to show the cancellation line.
- Recover completed background-job reports after failed writes or interrupted appends without duplicating them. Report cancellation persistence failures instead of success.
- Stop nested inference when a hook times out or its owning turn is cancelled.

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-26; no tag, build from source)

- First v0: the headless loop, the terminal, Starlark plugins, the wire surfaces, and this manual. No tagged release exists. See [Install](install.md).

## Where to go next

- [Slash commands](commands.md): run `/changelog` to print this page.
- [Install dal and dalgona](install.md): build the current source.

- The `/login` provider picker puts an exact provider id first when the filter matches one: typing `openai` and pressing Enter starts the OpenAI sign-in, not a longer id like `azure-openai-responses` that only contains the text.
- A scoped model id offered by several providers is priced for admission from each listed row instead of failing as unpriced: the configured price for a `provider/id` key wins, then the live catalog price, then the compiled table. - Products declare typed startup settings, and the settings picker confirms them: an edit rewrites `dal.toml` atomically with owner-only permissions, preserves your comments and formatting, and is refused when invalid. See [Plugins](plugins.md#add-skills-rules-and-prompt-text).

See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#tables-with-their-own-keys).

- Fix remote API-key sign-in outcome reporting. See [remote sign-in](commands.md#remote-sign-in).

- Reject unsupported Unicode duration units with a configuration error instead of panicking.

- Retain service cancellation receipts until service admission consumes them, so repeated cancellations do not strand `ask` or `run` capacity.

# dal JSON-RPC protocol reference

The dal protocol lets another process drive dal. Use it to build a GUI, an editor integration, or a test harness on the same operations that the terminal uses. Run `dalgon rpc` to serve it. This page lists the methods, the rules for each method group, and the rules for updates.

Each frame is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message on one line, ended by a line feed. A frame holds at most 16777216 bytes. A larger frame ends the connection. Frames run over stdio or a local socket. `initialize` negotiates capabilities. The protocol version is 1. A client that can answer approval requests lists `approval` in its `initialize` capabilities. A client that can answer extension questions lists `question`. A session with no such client attached denies approvals. It gives questions their default answer at once.

| method | params | result | capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| initialize | protocolVersion, capabilities | ready | none |
| protocol/schema | none | schema | none |
| commands/list | none | commands | none |
| session/list | limit, cursor, search | sessions | sessions |
| session/open | ref | session | sessions |
| session/close | sessionId | ok | sessions |
| session/view | sessionId, limit, before | view | sessions |
| session/subscribe | sessionId, gen, after | stream | sessions |
| session/unsubscribe | sessionId | ok | sessions |
| session/submit | sessionId, command | reply | sessions |
| session/answer | sessionId, requestId, answer | ok | sessions |
| blob/read | sessionId, blobId | bytes | blobs |
| models/list | none | models | models |
| docs/read | uri | text | docs |
| host/subscribe | none | stream | host.updates |
| host/unsubscribe | none | ok | host.updates |
| auth/status | none | providers | auth |
| auth/login | provider, method, apiKey | pending, then ok | auth |
| auth/cancel | loginId | cancelled | auth |
| auth/logout | provider | removed | auth |

## Start a connection

Run `dalgon rpc`. Send `initialize` as the first request. A request before `initialize` fails with `-32006` and the message `initialize must be the first request`. A second `initialize` fails with `-32600`. Only `protocol/schema` may come first.

Write this line to standard input:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,"capabilities":["sessions"],"clientInfo":{"name":"demo"}}}
```

The server writes one line back. It names the protocol version, the server, the capabilities it accepted, and your client id. In this reply, `<version>` is the server version and `<n>` is a connection number:

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"serverInfo":{"name":"dal","version":"<version>"},"capabilities":["sessions"],"clientId":"demo#<n>"}}
```

The reply lists only the capabilities that the server supports and that you asked for. It never echoes `approval` or `question`. A method that needs a capability you did not get fails with `-32007` and the message `capability "<name>" is not enabled on this connection`.

## Request rules

Requests need exactly one answer. Blobs are content-addressed. Error codes follow JSON-RPC. `experimental/` methods may change.

## Authentication methods

An `auth/login` with `method` `browser` or `device` answers `pending` with the `loginId` and `url` (and `userCode` for `device`) as soon as the provider flow reports one. When the flow ends, the host publishes one `login_finished` host update naming the attempt's `loginId`. `method` `api_key` takes the key in `apiKey`. It answers `ok` after the key is stored. `auth/cancel` takes the `loginId` of a pending login. It cancels the attempt. It answers whether one was still pending. `auth/status` lists each provider as `ready`, `not_configured`, or `expired`. `auth/logout` without `provider` removes every stored credential. A `provider` that is present but not a string is refused with `-32602`. The host removes nothing.

## Error handling

Seven methods decode their params strictly: `auth/login`, `auth/cancel`, `auth/logout`, `session/list`, `session/view`, `session/subscribe`, and `docs/read`. In them, an omitted optional member selects its default. A present member of the wrong type (or non-object params) is refused with `-32602`. Members that take no default stay required (`provider` and `method` for `auth/login`, `sessionId` wherever used). Invalid parameter errors format their message as `invalid params for <method>: <detail>` with code `-32602`. ACP `session/list` accepts null `cwd` and `cursor` filters.

## Session commands

`session/submit` takes every command type the `Command` decoder knows. An unknown `type` is refused with `-32602`. `session/submit` refuses an `export` command whose path is absolute or climbs with `..`. It answers `-32602` and writes no file. Relative paths inside the workspace and the default target stay valid.

### Chooser replies

A command may reply with `choose` (`{"type":"choose","chooser":<name>,"filter":<string>}`) asking the client to display an interactive picker. For `chooser` `"thinking"`, the reply carries an optional `thinkingLevels` array listing the canonical level names supported by the active model:

```json
{"type":"choose","chooser":"thinking","filter":"","thinkingLevels":["off","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]}
```

`thinkingLevels` is included only when `chooser` is `"thinking"`. For all other choosers (`model`, `settings`, `scoped_models`, `session`, `tree`, `fork_point`, `login`, `logout`), `thinkingLevels` is omitted.

When `thinkingLevels` is omitted from the wire, the deserializer preserves the field as absent, treating capability information as unsupported rather than guessing supported levels. When `thinkingLevels` is present as an explicit empty array (`[]`), the active model supports no thinking levels. When the user selects a level, the client submits that selection as a `/thinking <level>` command rather than setting the level directly, allowing the host to validate the choice against its model capabilities.

## Updates

Updates carry `seq` and `gen`. Clients resync on gaps.

## Extension status

An extension that registers a status kind reports changes as `ext_status` updates with `ext`, `state` (`busy` or `quiet`), and optional `text`. For example: `{"type":"ext_status","ext":"focus","state":"busy","text":"indexing"}` and `{"type":"ext_status","ext":"focus","state":"quiet"}`. The host polls each kind on a short fixed interval. It sends an update only when the state or text changes. A quiet extension with no text is the starting state. It sends nothing until it has been busy. A fresh wire subscription has no status seed. It receives changes as they occur. An embedded client reads the current busy or text-bearing statuses with `Agent::ext_status`. ACP clients receive the same change as a `_dal/notice` with `kind` `status` and the text `<ext>: <text>`, `<ext>: busy`, or `<ext>: quiet`. A2A streams carry it as the `dal.status` metadata of a status update. The router sends nothing. `dalgon --json` writes its result line only after every status kind is quiet.

## Shutdown

A server that is stopping answers each new request with `-32009` (`server_draining`). It gives running requests one second to finish. Then it closes the connection.

## Model rows

Each `models/list` row carries `id`, `provider`, `name`, and an optional `contextWindow`. `provider` is the label of the row's API family. Every chat and responses provider reads `openai`. It does not name a configured provider. Two rows can therefore share `id` and `provider`. Each row also carries `route`, the typed route that selects exactly that row, and an optional `reference`:

| Row | `route` | `reference` |
|---|---|---|
| API model with a known provider | `{"kind":"api","family":..,"model":..,"provider":..}` | `provider/model` |
| API model without a known provider | the same without `provider` | absent |
| Synthetic or harness model | `{"kind":"synthetic","id":..}` or `{"kind":"harness","id":..}` | the id |

A client that selects a row submits its `route` in `set_model`. It submits nothing it rebuilt from `id` or `provider`. A server that predates `route` and `reference` omits them. A client then keeps its older selection by name. That name cannot tell same-family providers apart. A member that is present but malformed is an error, not an absent member. `auth/status` rows and the protocol version 1 are unchanged.

## Assistant entries

Assistant entries carry one `model` identifier. Their optional `route` member identifies the route that produced the response:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{"api":"openai_chat"}` | An API route, with its API family. The other family values are `openai_responses`, `openai_codex`, and `anthropic`. |
| `"synthetic"` | A named synthetic model. |
| `"harness"` | A built-in harness mode. |

The route describes the existing `model` identifier. Its API family is independent of the entry's top-level `api` member, which describes the provider wire format. New responses include `route`. An absent member means the route is unknown, not that it is an API route. The decoder rejects `null`, unknown route kinds, and model identifiers that do not fit the declared synthetic or harness kind.

`protocol/schema` includes this optional, non-null member. Protocol version 1 and the format-1 encoding of assistant entries remain unchanged. Turn-ID reservations use journal format 2. See [durable turn identities](sessions.md#durable-turn-identities).

## Next

- [Build a client on the dal protocol](integrate.md): connect a program through `dalgon rpc`.
- [Embed dal in a Rust program](sdk.md): call the same operations in process.
- [Command line](cli.md): start `dalgon rpc`, `dalgon acp`, or `dalgon serve`.

# Sessions, history, and compaction

Sessions live under the data root. Use `-c` to continue a session. Use `-r` to resume one. Names label sessions. Exit lines and `/name` print the `-r` argument in the exact form the shell accepts. Names that are unsafe to paste degrade to the session id. Use `/tree`, `/fork`, and `/clone` to inspect or change branches. Use `/export` to write a shareable file. Read an entry at `session://<id>/<entry>`. `--no-session` runs without saving.

Child sessions also write a `dal-agent` `child_policy` record with their inherited approval mode and tool allowlist. An absent tool list means unrestricted access. Session replay requires at most one policy record. Duplicate or conflicting records fail replay.

A reopened session shows the model, thinking level, approval mode, execution mode, and name its journal recorded. The last record of each kind wins. A session that never chose a model keeps following the configured default. Its settings name no model while it runs and after it reopens. A default saved after it opened applies the next time it opens. A route the session chose shows exactly as recorded, with its provider when the record names one.


## Durable turn identities

For saved sessions, dal writes a turn-ID reservation to the journal before it acknowledges a prompt, follow-up, or wake allocation. A record counts as saved only after it is synced to disk. The first reservation creates the journal even if the turn never starts.

Private tool effects also require saved receipts. In a saved session, the first private loop or effect receipt creates the journal even if no user turn has started. dal saves the start receipt before running the effect. Ephemeral sessions keep these records in memory and do not create journal files.

Cancelling queued work does not release its identity. Later turns keep their allocated IDs. When a session reopens, unused reservations remain consumed. dal does not restore queued text. Submit it again if you still want to run it. A reservation alone does not create a completed turn.

Reservation records use journal format 2. All other record kinds retain format 1, so one journal can contain both versions. Existing journals remain readable and are not rewritten. Once a format-2 reservation is written, a build that reads only format 1 cannot open that journal. Use a build that supports both formats.

Multi-record batches still lack atomic framing against process crashes. An interrupted batch is not guaranteed to roll back cleanly on reopen.


## Compaction

Compaction starts by default at 85 percent of the context window, remote first. Use `/compact <focus>` to force it. Compaction retains recent entries and inserts summary text. dal drops raw provider-native history items. They do not continue into subsequent model requests.

## Context measurements

Measured context use applies only to the model route that produced the latest
assistant response on the selected branch after compaction. The route includes
its kind and, for API routes, its API family. A matching model name alone is not
enough. When both routes name a provider, the providers must match too. A
response recorded without a provider still counts for the same model that now
names one.

Completed and partial responses retain this identity when the session reopens.
If the latest response has no route metadata, dal uses a context estimate rather
than an older measurement. Existing journals stay readable and are not rewritten.

# Sessions, history, and compaction

Sessions live under the data root. Use `-c` to continue a session. Use `-r` to resume one. Names label sessions. Exit lines and `/name` print the `-r` argument in the exact form the shell accepts. Names that are unsafe to paste degrade to the session id. Use `/tree`, `/fork`, and `/clone` to inspect or change branches. Use `/export` to write a shareable file. Read an entry at `session://<id>/<entry>`. `--no-session` runs without saving.

Child sessions also write a `dal-agent` `child_policy` record with their inherited approval mode and tool allowlist. An absent tool list means unrestricted access. Session replay requires at most one policy record. Duplicate or conflicting records fail replay.

A reopened session shows the model, thinking level, approval mode, execution mode, and name its journal recorded. The last record of each kind wins. A session that never chose a model keeps following the configured default. Its settings name no model while it runs and after it reopens. A default saved after it opened applies the next time it opens. A route the session chose shows exactly as recorded, with its provider when the record names one.


## Durable turn identities

For saved sessions, dal writes a turn-ID reservation to the journal before it acknowledges a prompt, follow-up, or wake allocation. A record counts as saved only after it is synced to disk. The first reservation creates the journal even if the turn never starts.

Private tool effects also require saved receipts. In a saved session, the first private loop or effect receipt creates the journal even if no user turn has started. dal saves the start receipt before running the effect. Ephemeral sessions keep these records in memory and do not create journal files.

Cancelling queued work does not release its identity. Later turns keep their allocated IDs. When a session reopens, unused reservations remain consumed. dal does not restore queued text. Submit it again if you still want to run it. A reservation alone does not create a completed turn.

Reservation records use journal format 2, and mail delivery records use journal format 3. All other record kinds retain format 1, so one journal can contain several versions. Existing journals remain readable and are not rewritten. Once a record of a newer format is written, a build that does not read that format reports the newer format and does not open the journal. Use a build that supports formats 1 to 3.

Multi-record batches still lack atomic framing against process crashes. An interrupted batch is not guaranteed to roll back cleanly on reopen.


## Compaction

Compaction starts by default at 85 percent of the context window, remote first. Use `/compact <focus>` to force it. Compaction retains recent entries and inserts summary text. dal drops raw provider-native history items. They do not continue into subsequent model requests.

## Context measurements

Measured context use applies only to the model route that produced the latest
assistant response on the selected branch after compaction. The route includes
its kind and, for API routes, its API family. A matching model name alone is not
enough. When both routes name a provider, the providers must match too. A
response recorded without a provider still counts for the same model that now
names one.

Completed and partial responses retain this identity when the session reopens.
If the latest response has no route metadata, dal uses a context estimate rather
than an older measurement. Existing journals stay readable and are not rewritten.
See [assistant entries](protocol.md#assistant-entries) for the stored field.

## Next

- [Slash commands](commands.md): run `/tree`, `/fork`, `/clone`, `/export`, `/compact`, and `/resume`.
- [Command line](cli.md): continue or resume a session with `-c` and `-r`.
- [Protocol](protocol.md): list, open, and subscribe to sessions over JSON-RPC.

This page lists the user-visible changes in each version. The `/changelog` command prints it.

## Unreleased

- An eval cell can now ask the session judge one question (`judge.ask`) or up to 32 at once (`judge.batch`). The cell may request `judge.ask` or `judge.batch` only when that operation is in its `uses` and in `eval.uses`, and every eval cell receives the `judge` and `judge_batch` globals. See [tools](tools.md#the-eval-tool).
- Only an eval cell that declares `judge.ask` or `judge.batch` can ask the session judge; plugin handlers, commands, and models are refused at declaration.
- The `/login` provider picker puts an exact provider id first when the filter matches one: typing `openai` and pressing Enter starts the OpenAI sign-in, not a longer id like `azure-openai-responses` that only contains the text.
- A scoped model id offered by several providers is priced for admission from each listed row instead of failing as unpriced: the configured price for a `provider/id` key wins, then the live catalog price, then the compiled table. A route that names its provider also prices through its `provider/model` spelling.
- Provider definitions supply per-family auth, dialect, and request schema from one source, and scoped models are gated through config limits.
- Products declare typed startup settings, and the settings picker confirms them: an edit rewrites `dal.toml` atomically with owner-only permissions, preserves your comments and formatting, and is refused when invalid. A saved next-start value shows beside the running value when they differ, and a remote connection refuses product setting edits. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#tables-with-their-own-keys).
- `dalgon dev run` evaluates a scenario with the invoking product's configuration kind, defaults, and extensions instead of a fixed one.
- A URI scheme resolver runs with the identity of the extension that registered the scheme, so it queries records through its own capability-scoped services. See [Plugins](plugins.md).
- Breaking Rust API: `ProductFactory` gains `config_product` and `settings`, and `Reply::Choose` gains `thinking_levels`. Callers that construct either value must provide the new fields, and pattern matches must handle them or use `..`.
- A user plugin can replace one bundled skill or rule with `replace = True` and `battery = "<bundled extension>"`: for example the `find-anything` skill owned by `skills`, or the `fabricated-unavailable-tool-call` rule owned by `quality`. Without the pair a name clash is still refused; the replacement moves only that record and inherits no service, tool, or grant. Removing the claim restores the bundled record on reload. See [Plugins](plugins.md#add-skills-rules-and-prompt-text).
- `[limits.plugins]` Starlark budgets take positive integers and report the key to raise: a real load, handler, or eval-cell breach names `raise limits.plugins.<key> to allow more`, while a user `fail()` that repeats the vendor wording gains no such remedy. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#tables-with-their-own-keys).
- A reopened session shows the model, thinking level, approval mode, execution mode, and name its journal recorded. Before, it showed the defaults of the host that opened it. A session that never chose a model still follows the configured default and names no model. Changing another setting no longer makes the default look selected. See [sessions](sessions.md).
- API model routes can name their provider. A route that does, such as a row picked in the model picker, resolves exactly that provider. It never resolves another provider or a synthetic model that lists the same id. It fails with a typed error when the provider is unavailable. Routes without a provider resolve as before.
- `models/list` rows add `route` and `reference`. The remote model picker selects by route for the session only and scopes by provider. Servers without them keep the older selection by name. The protocol version is still 1.
- Fix remote API-key sign-in outcome reporting. See [remote sign-in](commands.md#remote-sign-in).
- Persist turn identities before acknowledging queued work. Cancelling a queued turn no longer invalidates later journal entries. Restarting a session cannot reuse its reserved identity. Queued text is not restored.
- New turn-ID reservations use journal format 2. Other records retain format 1. Existing journals need no conversion. A reader must support format 2 after a reservation is written. See [durable turn identities](sessions.md#durable-turn-identities).
- Rust code that uses `dal-tools` can call `patch::styles::tier` again, also in constant expressions. It returns the prompt-intensity tier of an edit style.
- Reject unsupported Unicode duration units with a configuration error instead of panicking.
- Report incomplete patch rollback with the affected paths and retained backup locations. Continue restoring other files when one restoration fails.
- Retain service cancellation receipts until service admission consumes them, so repeated cancellations do not strand `ask` or `run` capacity.
- Add `ArtifactFile::StatusTxt` (`status.txt`) to task isolation directories, saved atomically with file mode 0600 on Unix. Rust callers with exhaustive matches on `ArtifactFile` must handle the new variant.
- Azure OpenAI entries resolve their endpoint from an explicit `base_url` first, then `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, then `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME`. A resource name an entry never needs is never validated and cannot fail setup; entry `api_version` and `deployments` values win over the matching environment values. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md#azure-openai).
- Devin request failures now carry a short readable detail from the server reply when it holds one. Markup pages are skipped, unsafe characters are rejected, the text is bounded, and credentials stay redacted.
- Google account-validation failures now show the verification link the server names, when its error calls for account validation. The link is rendered, never opened on its own; ordinary quota messages are unchanged.
- Add canonical `github-copilot` device sign-in (`dalgon login github-copilot`), supporting optional GitHub Enterprise domains, user verification code display, and completion polling. Stored credentials persist to `auth.json` as an API-key token or structured envelope containing the token, enterprise domain, and discovered account endpoint. Sign-in applies best-effort model policy enablement without fetching the model catalogue at sign-in time. API keys can also be supplied via `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `--api-key`.
- Bedrock provider readiness checks captured AWS credential sources (environment variables, shared configuration and credential files, SSO, credential processes, or instance roles) and stored bearer tokens across effective configured provider families and aliases. `dalgon login status` reports Bedrock entries as `ready` or `not configured` instead of attempting an interactive sign-in flow.
- In GitHub Copilot device sign-in, submitting a blank enterprise domain defaults to `github.com`. Prompts for required OAuth authorization codes or redirect URLs continue to require non-empty input.
- Cancelling CLI device-code authorization with Ctrl+C during completion polling restores the terminal cleanly and cancels the sign-in request without saving incomplete credentials.
- Prefer device authorization over an API key in terminal sign-in when the provider does not offer browser sign-in, matching the interactive CLI.
- Fix terminal cancellation reporting. The terminal now says what happened to a cancellation:
  - A refused cancellation request reports its own error while that turn is still running.
  - A transport error while waiting reports that error. The run no longer finishes as if nothing failed.
  - When the turn already finished, quit and resume complete normally with no cancellation line.
  - A lost replay, a closed subscription, or no confirmation in time reports that the cancellation could not be confirmed. It asks you to resume the session to check its state.
  - Resuming after such a failure closes both the old session and the opened replacement session.
  - A turn that ends cancelled still shows the inline cancellation line. Any other end shows no line. Fullscreen never shows the inline line.
  - On quit, an earlier terminal error still wins over a later failure to show the cancellation line.
- Recover completed background-job reports after failed writes or interrupted appends without duplicating them. Report cancellation persistence failures instead of success.
- Stop nested inference when a hook times out or its owning turn is cancelled.

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-26; no tag, build from source)

- First v0: the headless loop, the terminal, Starlark plugins, the wire surfaces, and this manual. No tagged release exists. See [Install](install.md).

## Where to go next

- [Slash commands](commands.md): run `/changelog` to print this page.
- [Install dal and dalgona](install.md): build the current source.
"),
    ("cli", "# dalgon command-line reference: flags, subcommands, exit codes

`dalgon` is the dal coding agent. `dal` and `dl` run the same program. With no subcommand and no prompt, it opens the terminal UI on a terminal. With `-p` or `--json`, it runs one turn and exits. Use this page to look up a flag, a subcommand, an exit code, or an environment variable. Run `dalgon --help` for the flag list. Run `dalgon <subcommand> --help` for one subcommand.

## Run one turn

```sh
dalgon -p "Summarize the staged diff"
dalgon --json -o reply.md "Summarize the staged diff"
git diff | dalgon -p - "Review these changes"
```

These runs need a configured model. Without one, dalgon reports the missing model and how to set it.

Print mode (`-p`) runs one turn. Then it waits up to 3 seconds for its extension status kinds to go quiet. JSON mode (`--json`) writes a result as one JSON line. It writes the line only after the turn ends and every extension status kind is quiet. A run that leaves an extension busy delays the result line.

If a kind stays busy, print mode reports `dalgon: extension status is not quiet: <extensions> still busy after 3 seconds` on stderr. It exits 1 if a kind remains busy after the quiet wait. JSON mode has no time limit. It waits for quiet or a stop signal. A stop ends the run without a JSON result line.

With `--approval ask` and no terminal, a headless run denies `patch` and `exec` calls. Use `--approval edits` to approve edits without asking. Use `--approval all` to approve every call, and only in a run that an external sandbox already confines.

## Root flags

A flag overrides the matching key in `dal.toml` for one run. See [Settings in dal.toml](config.md).

| flag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `-p`, `--print` | Print the assistant response and exit. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON result object or error object. Exit 1 on error. |
| `-o FILE`, `--output-last-message FILE` | Write the last assistant message to FILE after a successful run. |
| `-c`, `--continue` | Continue the newest session in this workspace. |
| `-r [SESSION]`, `--resume [SESSION]` | Resume a session by id or name. Without SESSION, open the session picker. |
| `-n NAME`, `--name NAME` | Name the session. |
| `-m ID`, `--model ID` | Use model ID for this run. ID may name a provider route, an alias, a registered synthetic model, or a dalgon mode. |
| `--mode MODE` | Set the harness mode: `normal`, `eval-first`, or `eval-only`. |
| `--thinking THINKING` | Set the reasoning level: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. |
| `--approval APPROVAL` | Set the approval policy for `patch` and `exec`: `ask`, `edits`, or `all`. |
| `--sandbox` | Turn on the sandbox for this run. |
| `--no-session` | Do not persist this session. |
| `--screen SCREEN` | Select the terminal screen: `inline` or `fullscreen`. |
| `--color COLOR` | Select terminal color: `auto`, `always`, or `never`. |
| `-C DIR`, `--cd DIR` | Use DIR as the workspace without changing the process working directory. |
| `--connect ADDR` | Connect to a remote dalgon host and run the interactive terminal UI. Without it, dalgon uses a host in this process. |
| `--token-file FILE` | Read the bearer token from FILE. dalgon sends it only to non-loopback WebSocket endpoints. Needs `--connect`. |
| `PROMPT...` | Attach text, image, or piped standard-input content to the first user message. A prompt of `-` reads piped standard input. |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print help. |
| `-V`, `--version` | Print the version. |

Some flags cannot combine:

- `--mode` and a `dalgon/` mode id in `--model` cannot combine. Pass the mode once.
- `--continue` and `--resume` cannot combine.
- `--connect` needs the terminal UI. Do not pass it with `--print` or `--json`.

## Subcommands

`dalgon` has 12 subcommands.

| subcommand | what it does |
|---|---|
| `login` | Sign in to a provider or inspect sign-in state. |
| `logout` | Sign out from a provider. |
| `models` | List models with built-in prices. |
| `docs` | Read a documentation page. |
| `serve` | Start the local control server or create its token. |
| `rpc` | Serve the JSON-RPC protocol on standard input and output, or on a local socket. |
| `acp` | Serve the Agent Client Protocol on standard input and output. |
| `app-server` | Serve the Codex app-server protocol on standard input and output. |
| `completion` | Generate shell completion scripts. |
| `plugin` | Manage configured plugin grants. |
| `rules` | Inspect or test stream rules. |
| `dev` | Inspect and drive sessions for debugging. |

A hidden `__sandbox` subcommand is the helper that the sandbox launches. Do not run it by hand.

## dalgon login

Sign in to a model provider. Then run `dal` and pick a model.

```sh
dalgon login
printf %s "$KEY" | dalgon login anthropic --api-key
dalgon login status
```

Without PROVIDER, `dalgon login` shows a provider picker. The interactive CLI prefers browser sign-in first, then device authorization, then an API key prompt. Terminal sign-in lists each sign-in method for providers that offer several, so device code stays selectable without flags. `--api-key` reads an API key from standard input. `--device-auth` uses the provider device flow, where the provider supports it.

Providers with browser OAuth:
- OpenAI Codex opens the sign-in page in your browser and completes via a local loopback callback or a pasted redirect URL, falling back to device authorization if the callback port is busy. Device code can also be chosen directly from the terminal sign-in methods or with `--device-auth`.
- Anthropic and GitLab Duo open the sign-in page in your browser and complete either via local loopback callback or by pasting the authorization code or redirect URL. An empty line leaves the paste prompt open; the browser callback can still complete sign-in.

Device-code sign-in binds no local callback port: dalgon requests a code, displays the server's verification URL and user code to complete in a browser on any device, and polls for approval. During CLI device polling, pressing Ctrl+C cancels authorization and restores the terminal.
- Factory Droid (`factory-droid`) automatically uses this device-code flow without `--device-auth`, polling WorkOS and verifying the session through whoami.
- GitHub Copilot (`github-copilot`) device sign-in prompts for an optional GitHub Enterprise domain; pressing Enter on a blank line chooses `github.com`.

Credentials live in `auth.json` under the data root, with mode `0600` (owner read and write only; dal refuses symbolic links and group or other permission bits). Stored secrets and tokens are never echoed to standard output or error.

Run `dalgon login status` to inspect stored credentials and configured API keys. The command exits 0 when at least one provider is ready. If all credentials are missing or expired, it exits 1. It prints a sign-in hint. OAuth rows show their expiry date. The output does not include tokens or API keys.

## dalgon logout

Remove stored credentials.

```sh
dalgon logout
dalgon logout anthropic
```

`dalgon logout` removes the credentials of every provider and prints `Removed all credentials.`. `dalgon logout PROVIDER` removes one provider and prints `Removed credentials for PROVIDER.`. When nothing is stored, it prints `No stored credentials.`.

## dalgon models

List models with built-in prices, the price source, and the fetch date.

```sh
dalgon models
dalgon models claude
dalgon models --json
```

PATTERN keeps the rows whose provider or id contains it. The table has the columns `PROVIDER`, `ID`, `CONTEXT`, and `PRICE`. It ends with a `Prices: <source>, fetched <date>.` line. `--json` prints one JSON array. Each row has `provider`, `id`, and `context`.

## dalgon docs

Read the embedded manual. Usage: `dalgon docs [URI]`. With no URI, it prints the index. The first index line is `# dal://`. With a page URI, it prints the page. Unknown URIs exit 1 with a miss message on stderr and nothing on stdout.

```sh
dalgon docs
dalgon docs dal://config
```

A mistyped page name prints two lines on stderr. The first is `dalgon: no dal document at <uri>`. The second is `Did you mean <nearest page>? Run dalgon docs for the list.`.

## dalgon serve

Start the model router. It listens on your machine only, unless you pass `--public` with a token.

```sh
dalgon serve
dalgon serve token
dalgon serve --public
dalgon serve --a2a
```

`--a2a` enables the agent-to-agent surface. `--bind ADDR` and `--port PORT` override `serve.bind` and `serve.port`. `--token-file FILE` reads the token from FILE. `--public` needs a token. It serves plain HTTP, so the token crosses the network in plain text.

`dalgon serve token` creates the bearer token and prints it once. It refuses to replace an existing token. `--force` replaces it. Every client must then use the new token. See [dalgon serve](serve.md).

## dalgon rpc

Serve the JSON-RPC protocol on standard input and output. Each line holds one JSON object.

```sh
dalgon rpc
dalgon rpc --socket /tmp/dalgon.sock
```

`--socket [FILE]` listens on a local socket instead. FILE defaults to `rpc/dal.sock` under the data root. See [the dal JSON-RPC protocol](protocol.md).

## dalgon acp

Serve the Agent Client Protocol on standard input and output. Each line holds one JSON-RPC message. Point an ACP-capable editor at this command.

```sh
dalgon acp
```

## dalgon app-server

Serve the Codex app-server protocol on standard input and output.

```sh
dalgon app-server
```

## dalgon completion

Print a shell completion script. SHELL is `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `powershell`, or `zsh`.

```sh
dalgon completion zsh
```

## dalgon plugin

Manage plugin grants.

```sh
dalgon plugin list
dalgon plugin grant quality
dalgon plugin revoke quality
```

`list` shows configured plugins and their persistent grants. `grant NAME` grants the capabilities that plugin NAME declares. `revoke NAME` revokes every persistent grant for NAME. List a plugin in `plugins` in `dal.toml` before you grant it. Session grants end with their session. The name `quality` is the plugin from [Write a first plugin](plugins.md#write-a-first-plugin).

## dalgon rules

List the effective stream rules and any skipped-rule problems. Then test a rule against one input.

```sh
dalgon rules
dalgon rules test "check this text"
dalgon rules test --source tool --tool patch --path src/main.rs "let x = 1;"
```

`--source` selects the input stream: `text` (the default), `thinking`, or `tool`. For `tool`, `--tool` names the tool (default `patch`) and `--path` sets the path context. A TEXT of `-` reads at most 1048576 bytes from standard input. See [Rules](rules.md).

## dalgon dev

Inspect and drive sessions for debugging.

```sh
dalgon dev run scenario.jsonl
dalgon dev fold journal.jsonl
dalgon dev journal replay journal.jsonl
```

- `run FILE` drives a scripted headless session from a scenario file. Each nonblank line holds one step as a JSON object. `--keep` keeps the data root and workspace of the run. `--root DIR` reuses an earlier kept run root. `--consent` lets steps that authorize actions act with your privileges. Without it, the scenario file alone cannot grant them.
- `fold FILE` prints which folded fields each journal record changes.
- `journal replay FILE` folds a journal and prints the recovered state.
- `journal diff BEFORE AFTER` prints the folded fields that differ between two journals.
- `journal torn IN OUT` copies a journal with its tail cut mid-record.
- `journal sidecar DIR [NAME]` lists the sidecar files in a session directory, or dumps one.

## Files and environment

The config file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dal/dal.toml`, or `~/.config/dal/dal.toml` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset. The data root is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dal/`, or `~/.local/share/dal/`. `dalgona` uses `dalgona/` in both places. dalgon ignores an `XDG_` path that is not absolute. The layout is the same on every OS. On Windows, `~` is absolute `HOME`, then absolute `USERPROFILE`, then absolute `HOMEDRIVE` plus `HOMEPATH` combined.

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `DAL_LOG` | Selects the log level. |
| `DAL_NO_MOTION` | Disables terminal motion. |
| `DAL_DEBUG` | Enables terminal diagnostics. |

Other `DAL_` names do not override config keys. Use `dal.toml` or command-line flags to change settings.

## Exit codes

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | requested failure |
| 124 | usage error |
| 125 | internal error |
| 130 | interrupted run |
| 141 | broken pipe |

Every error names what happened and the fix.

## Next

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md): sign in and run a first turn.
- [Settings in dal.toml](config.md): set the defaults that these flags override.
- [Tools, modes, and approval](tools.md): choose an approval policy and a mode.

    ("commands", "# Slash commands

Built-in commands, in registry order. Plugin commands appear after these with their own names.

| command | hint | summary |
|---|---|---|
| /settings |  | view and change settings |
| /model | [provider/model] | pick the model |
| /tree |  | navigate the session tree |
| /thinking | [level] | set the thinking level |
| /scoped-models |  | choose the models that /model lists |
| /export | [path] | write the session to a .md or .jsonl file |
| /import | <path> | open a session from a .jsonl file |
| /share |  | not in dalgon: use /export |
| /bug |  | not in dalgon: use /export and /session |
| /copy |  | copy the last reply to the clipboard |
| /name | [name] | set or show the session name |
| /session |  | show session details and usage |
| /changelog |  | show what changed in each version |
| /hotkeys |  | show keyboard shortcuts |
| /fork |  | new branch from a previous message |
| /clone |  | copy this session into a new one |
| /trust |  | not in dalgon: plugins load only from the data directory |
| /login | [provider] | sign in to a provider |
| /logout | [provider] | remove stored credentials |
| /new |  | start a new session |
| /compact | [instructions] | summarize older context now |
| /resume | [id or name] | open another session |
| /reload |  | reload plugins |
| /quit |  | quit dalgon |
| /mode | <normal\|eval-first\|eval-only> | set the harness mode |

`/exit` is an alias for `/quit`.

`/name`'s confirmation prints a resume token after the name: `Resume it with dalgon -r <token>.` The token is the name itself when it is shell-safe. Shell-safe means letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` bare, and spaces and apostrophes in double quotes. Otherwise the token is the session id. Paste it as shown. Anything the shell would expand or split always arrives as the id.

`/share`, `/bug`, and `/trust` never upload. `/share` directs you to `/export`, which writes a file you can send yourself. A conflicting command name is an error `command "<name>" is already registered by plugin "<first>"; plugin "<second>" cannot register it`. The numeric-suffix form `/review:1` is rejected. Completion matches name prefixes and orders them by name.

## Thinking and settings

`/thinking <level>` sets the model reasoning level when `<level>` is supported by the active model. The command saves the level to the session and default configuration. Passing an unsupported or unrecognized level returns an error listing valid options.

Without arguments, `/thinking` opens the thinking chooser. The host returns the active model's supported levels in `thinkingLevels`. An explicit empty array indicates the model supports no levels. When `thinkingLevels` is missing, the client treats the picker as unsupported rather than guessing levels. Selecting a level submits `/thinking <level>`, ensuring the host validates the requested level against its current capabilities.

`/settings` opens an interactive picker that pairs live controls with startup product rows:

- Live controls change runtime behavior immediately. The diagram setting toggles rendering in the current session, accompanied by a row to save the preference to `dal.toml`. `/model` opens the model chooser. `/thinking` displays `thinking · <current level>` and opens the thinking level chooser.
- Startup product rows configure extensions and defaults, including disabled batteries, rule sets, and web search options. Edits write atomically to `dal.toml`. When a saved value differs from the running value, the row displays both values with a restart notice, and changes take effect on the next launch.

## Remote sign-in

Esc cancels a remote API-key sign-in only before you submit the key. After submission, wait for the server's result. If it succeeds, use `/logout` to remove the stored credential.

## Skills

A skill is not a slash command. `/` completion never lists `skill:` entries. Run one with `/skill:<name> [text]`. The command sends `text` with it. Or run one with a `$` token in any prompt.

- `/skill <name>` runs the skill when the name is exact. Any other text lists the skills whose name contains it and runs nothing: `/skill find-` prints every candidate and starts no turn.
- In the composer, a token that starts with `$` opens a skills-only completion list. The list has the same match and order as `/`. Tab puts the first match in place of that token.
- A prompt that holds the whole token `$<name>`, `$<plugin>:<name>`, or `/skill:<name>` runs that skill. A prompt may name several. The body of each named skill joins the turn once, after your message, in order of first mention. Any other token stays text.

The file is `dal.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dal/` (default `~/.config/dal/dal.toml`). Data lives under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dal/`. Layering: code defaults, then product defaults, then user `dal.toml`, then CLI flags. A later layer replaces an earlier value by key path. `dalgona` reads `dal.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dalgona/` with data under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dalgona/`.

The table shows dal's built-in defaults before product TOML, user settings, and CLI overrides. The meaning column identifies dalgona's different defaults. `none` means omit the key, not the TOML string `"none"`. An omitted table still uses the field defaults listed below. Replace `<data-root>` with your product's data directory.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `normal` | harness mode: `normal`, `eval-first`, or `eval-only`; `--mode` overrides it for one run; see [Tools](tools.md) |
| `model` | string | `none` | the default model reference; dal writes it when you pick a model; `-m` overrides it for one run |
| `thinking` | string | `medium` | the default reasoning level: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`; `--thinking` overrides it for one run |
| `approval` | string | `ask` | the approval policy for `patch` and `exec`: `ask` asks before each call, `edits` approves edits and asks for `exec`, `all` approves every call; `--approval` overrides it for one run; see [Tools](tools.md) |
| `screen` | string | `inline` | the terminal surface: `inline` keeps terminal scrollback; `fullscreen` uses the alternate screen and replays the settled transcript on exit; `--screen` overrides it for one run; see [Terminal](terminal.md) |
| `theme` | string | `auto` | the terminal colors: `auto` follows the terminal background, `palette` uses the terminal's own palette, or name one of the nine shipped themes, such as `catppuccin-mocha` |
| `sandbox` | bool | `false` | `true` runs every `exec` child through the platform sandbox; `--sandbox` turns it on for one run; see [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `images` | bool | `false` | `true` enables inline images in terminals that support an image protocol; diagrams render as text when images are off |
| `motion` | bool | `true` | `false` turns off repeated terminal motion; the `DAL_NO_MOTION` environment variable turns it off too |
| `compact_ratio` | number | `0.85` | the share of the context window at which compaction starts, from `0.5` to `0.95`; `0.85` means 85 percent; see [Sessions](sessions.md) |
| `edit_style` | string | `anchor` | the patch format; dalgona defaults to `hashline` |
| `guard` | table | `{ enabled = false }` | guard settings; dalgona defaults to `enabled = true`; see [Guard](guard.md) |
| `search_symbols` | bool | `false` | whether search includes symbols; dalgona defaults to `true` |
| `judge` | table | `none` | shared judge settings, including `gate`; readiness checks do not generate a response; see [Judged rules](rules.md#judged-rules) |
| `plugins` | list | `[]` | the names of the plugins to load; each name is a directory under `<data-root>/plugins/` that holds a `plugin.star`; see [Plugins](plugins.md) |
| `aliases` | table | `none` | short names for models; each key is an alias and each value is a non-empty model id; `-m` accepts an alias |
| `serve` | table | `none` | local control endpoint settings; field defaults apply when omitted |
| `serve.bind` | string | `127.0.0.1` | the address the router binds; `--bind` overrides it; an address that is not loopback needs `--public` and a token |
| `serve.port` | number | `7437` | the TCP port the router listens on, from 0 to 65535; `--port` overrides it |
| `serve.token_file` | path | `"<data-root>/serve.token"` | the authentication token file |
| `serve.approval` | string | `ask` | the approval policy for requests that reach the endpoint: `ask`, `edits`, or `all`; it follows `approval` when you leave it unset |
| `serve.origins` | list | `[]` | the browser origins that may open a WebSocket to the endpoint; write each origin exactly; a WebSocket upgrade that carries any other `Origin` header gets `403` |
| `prices` | table | `none` | per-model prices in USD per million tokens, one `prices.<model-id>` table per model; a price set here wins over the compiled price table; each table needs all four rates, and each rate is a number that is not negative |
| `prices.<model-id>.input` | number | `none` | the rate for uncached input tokens; required in each `prices.<model-id>` table |
| `prices.<model-id>.cached_input` | number | `none` | the rate for cached input tokens; required |
| `prices.<model-id>.cache_write` | number | `none` | the `prices.<model-id>.cache_write` setting; `none` keeps the historical fallback to the applicable input rate |
| `prices.<model-id>.output` | number | `none` | the rate for output tokens, not counting reasoning tokens; required |
| `prices.<model-id>.reasoning` | number | `none` | the rate for separately reported reasoning tokens; required; a rate of `0` is a known price |
| `prices.<model-id>.tiers` | list | `[]` | request-wide context tiers in any order; each tier has `size` (input threshold) and optional `input`, `cached_input`, `cache_write`, `output`, `reasoning` overrides |
| `rules` | table | `none` | rule matching and retry settings; field defaults apply when omitted |
| `rules.watch` | bool | `true` | whether to watch stream rules |
| `rules.interrupt` | string | `always` | interrupt mode when a rule does not set its own |
| `rules.repeat` | string | `once` | repeat mode when a rule does not set its own |
| `rules.repeat_gap` | number | `10` | turn gap for `after-gap` repeats |
| `rules.max_retries` | number | `3` | maximum rule interrupts per turn |
| `rules.disabled` | list | `[]` | the rule names to drop before rule sets are built, such as `no-sleep`; a name starts with a letter or digit and has at most 64 characters from letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-` |

| `agents` | table | `none` | child-session settings: `enabled` publishes the `agent` model tool, `max_concurrent` caps running children, `max_depth` caps nesting; see below |
| `limits` | table | `none` | the Starlark budgets under `limits.plugins`; see below |
| `models` | table | `none` | provider-layer defaults: `default`, `thinking`, and `aliases`; see below |
| `retry` | table | `none` | provider retry limits: `request_max_retries` and `stream_max_retries`; see below |
| `providers` | table | `none` | one `providers.<id>` table per provider; a built-in id changes that provider and any other id adds a named provider; see below |
| `ask` | table | `none` | holds one key, `timeout`; see `ask.timeout` |
| `ask.timeout` | string | `"30m"` | how long one raised question stays open; extension grant prompts ignore it and wait 120 s; clamped into `1m` to `120m` at load, with one startup notice naming the key, the value, and the clamp |
| `compact` | table | `none` | an extension-owned table that dal accepts without checking its keys; no part of dal reads a key from it; use `compact_ratio` to set when compaction starts |
| `rule_sets` | table | `none` | read by dalgona only: `rule_sets.enabled` lists the bundled rule sets to load; dal accepts the table and reads no key from it; see `dalgona://rules` |
| `plugin` | table | `none` | per-plugin settings, one `plugin.<name>` table per plugin; the plugin's `config` schema checks the table when the plugin loads; see [Plugins](plugins.md#read-settings) |
| `eval` | table | `none` | holds one key, `uses`; see `eval.uses` |
| `eval.uses` | list | `[]` | the operations that eval cells may request, such as `tools.read`, `tools.search`, `tools.patch`, `tools.exec`, `judge.ask`, `judge.batch`, or an exported `tools.<plugin>.<tool>`; each effect still goes through normal approval, with at most 64 entries and no wildcards or duplicates; empty means eval cells can only compute and cannot act |

`[aliases]` maps model aliases. `[serve]` holds router settings. `[limits]` holds run budgets. `[plugin.<name>]` holds per-plugin settings. `[providers.<id>]` configures named provider endpoints or overrides built-in provider routes.

A `[providers.<id>]` table sets connection and authentication settings:

- `api`: wire API family (`openai_chat`, `openai_responses`, `openai_codex`, `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `cursor`, `devin`, `droid`, `gitlab`, `google-generative-ai`, `google-vertex`, `google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`, `mistral`, `ollama`, or `pi-messages`).
- `base_url`: endpoint base URL.
- `transport`: transport protocol, either `"https"` (default) or `"websocket"` (supported for `openai_responses` and `openai_codex`).
- `key_env`: name of the environment variable that holds the API key. Required for custom named providers unless `auth = "none"`. For built-in providers, `key_env` is optional and overrides the default environment variable.
- `auth`: authorization header style for API keys:
  - `"bearer"`: sends the key in an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header (default for chat and responses).
  - `"x-api-key"`: sends the key in an `x-api-key: <key>` header (default for Anthropic).
  - `"api-key"`: sends the key in an `api-key: <key>` header.
  - `"none"`: sends no API-key authorization header; the entry carries no API key and builds no credential header. It does not make an OAuth-only family usable without its required credential: such a credential-less row is still refused at request admission.
- `max_concurrent_requests`: maximum simultaneous requests for this provider, between 1 and 64 (default 4).
- `api_version`: the `api-version` query value for an Azure-shaped entry. An entry value wins over `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION`.
- `deployments`: a table mapping catalog model ids to Azure deployment names. An entry value wins model by model over `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP`; a model with no mapping is sent under its own id. Quote a model id that holds a dot (`"gpt-5.5" = "..."`), or TOML reads the dot as a table path.

## Tables with their own keys

These tables take more keys than the table above lists. An unknown key in any of them is an error.

- `[agents]`: `enabled` (default `false`) publishes the `agent` model tool. `max_concurrent` (default `32`) caps running children. `max_depth` (default `1`) caps nesting. Both caps are whole numbers above zero.
- `[limits.plugins]`: the Starlark budgets `load_ticks` (default `1000000`), `load_heap_bytes` (`16777216`), `handler_ticks` (`200000`), `handler_heap_bytes` (`8388608`), `cell_ticks` (`2000000`), `cell_heap_bytes` (`33554432`), and `stack_depth` (`100`). Each key holds one positive integer. The six tick and heap budgets accept `1` through `9223372036854775807`; `stack_depth` accepts `1` through `4294967295`. Zero, a negative, a fraction, a string, a boolean, or a list is refused as an invalid value that names the key and the accepted range. A missing key keeps its default. Each key named replaces only its default; layers merge per key.
- `[limits.plugins]` placement: the seven budget names directly under `[limits]` are refused and point at `limits.plugins.<name>`, for example `limits.load_ticks` suggests `limits.plugins.load_ticks`. The singular `[limits.plugin]` table is refused and points at `limits.plugins`. An unknown key inside `[limits.plugins]` is refused as an unknown key that names the full `limits.plugins.<name>` path, suggests the closest accepted spelling, and lists the seven accepted keys. A valid `[limits]` sibling such as `agents = 64`, and a valid `[agents]` table beside the budgets, stays legal.
- `[limits.plugins]` failures are actionable. A real load, handler, or eval-cell budget breach names the configured key with `raise limits.plugins.<key> to allow more`, alongside the applied budget and the vendor prefix (`Execution duration limit` for ticks, `Heap memory limit` for heap, `Starlark call stack overflow` for depth). `load_ticks` and `load_heap_bytes` guard plugin loading, `handler_ticks` and `handler_heap_bytes` guard one handler call, `cell_ticks` and `cell_heap_bytes` guard one eval cell, and the single `stack_depth` fans out to all three contexts. A user `fail()` that carries the vendor wording, or a source comment that mentions it, gains no remedy: the remedy appears only on a typed budget breach, never on a user failure or a source-text match.
- `[models]`: `default` is the model that an empty reference selects. `thinking` is a reasoning level (default `medium`). `aliases` maps short names to model references.
- `[retry]`: `request_max_retries` (default `4`) and `stream_max_retries` (default `5`). Each is a whole number from 0 to 100.
- `[providers.<id>]`: `api`, `base_url`, `transport` (`https` or `websocket`), `key_env`, `auth` (`bearer`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, or `none`), and `max_concurrent_requests` (1 to 64, default `4`). Some providers also take `api_version`, `deployments`, `region`, `project`, `location`, `namespace`, `binary`, or `integration`. A new id needs `api` and `base_url`, and it needs `key_env` unless `auth` is `none`. The id `dal` is reserved.
- `[prices.<model-id>]`: besides the four rates, `cache_write` sets the cache-write rate. Without it, dal prices cache writes at the input rate. `tiers` is a non-empty array of tables for prompts above a context size. Each tier needs `size`, a context token count, and at least one rate: `input`, `cached_input`, `cache_write`, `output`, or `reasoning`. Tier sizes must strictly increase.
- `[ask]`: `timeout` only.

## Azure OpenAI

Azure is a shape on a Chat or Responses entry, not a separate `api` value: an entry with `auth = "api-key"`, an `api_version`, or a `deployments` table is sent through the Azure adapter. The key travels in an `api-key` header, never as `Bearer`; OAuth sign-in is refused for these entries.

For Azure entries, an explicit `base_url` always wins. When you omit it, `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` takes precedence over `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME`. The resource name must be one valid DNS label, but dal does not validate it when a higher-priority URL already supplies the endpoint. Blank environment values are ignored. Non-Azure entries ignore these Azure variables.

Configure the built-in OpenAI provider and select a provider-qualified model:

```toml
[providers.openai]
auth = "api-key"
key_env = "AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"
api_version = "2025-03-01-preview"

[providers.openai.deployments]
"gpt-5.4" = "my-gpt54-deployment"
```

With `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` and either `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` or `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME` in the environment, select `openai/gpt-5.4` (for example with `/model openai/gpt-5.4`). When neither `api_version` nor `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION` is set, Responses defaults to `v1` and Chat to `2024-10-21`.

`dal.toml` strictly refuses supplied secrets. Setting keys such as `api_key`, `key`, or `secret` directly in configuration is rejected as an unknown key at load time. Credentials must come from environment variables named by `key_env` or through `dalgon login`.

Stored credentials live in `auth.json` under your product's data directory (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dal/auth.json` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dalgona/auth.json`), written atomically with mode `0600` permissions (owner read and write only). Non-owner permission bits and symbolic links are refused. Stored entries record raw API keys, OAuth tokens, or structured envelopes; for example, GitHub Copilot stores a JSON envelope holding the token alongside any enterprise domain and discovered API endpoint.

Built-in providers resolve credentials from specific environment variables:
- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`: GitHub token for GitHub Copilot (`github-copilot`) authentication.
- `GITLAB_TOKEN`: personal access token for GitLab Duo API key authentication.
- `GITLAB_CLIENT_ID`: overrides the default OAuth client ID for GitLab Duo.
- `GITLAB_REDIRECT_URI`: overrides the loopback redirect URI for GitLab Duo browser OAuth callback.
- `RADIUS_API_KEY`: API key for Radius (`radius`), sent as a bearer token.

Bedrock entries (`api = "bedrock"`) authenticate through captured AWS credential sources (environment variables such as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, shared credentials and configuration files under `~/.aws/`, SSO tokens, external credential processes, or IAM roles) or a stored bearer token in `auth.json`. Provider readiness verifies credential availability against the effective configured provider family, including configured aliases, without performing network requests or writing to cache.

```toml
plugins = ["todo"]

[providers.custom]
api = "openai_chat"
base_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
key_env = "CUSTOM_API_KEY"
auth = "api-key"
```

## Write a minimal dal.toml

Set the defaults you would otherwise pass as flags on every run. A flag still wins for one run.

```toml
approval = "edits"
thinking = "high"
compact_ratio = 0.8

[serve]
port = 8080
```

This file approves edits without asking and still asks before `exec`. It raises the reasoning level, starts compaction at 80 percent of the context window, and moves the router to port 8080. Pick a model in the terminal, and dal saves `model` for you.

Add a plugin name to `plugins` only after its directory exists under `<data-root>/plugins/`. A plugin that fails to load stops startup. After you write the plugin from [Write a first plugin](plugins.md#write-a-first-plugin), add this line at the top of the file:

```toml
plugins = ["quality"]
```

Every config error names the key and the fix.
