# Agent instructions for [dal and dalgona](README.md)

- You MUST run `just verify` from [justfile](justfile) before every commit.
- You MUST keep the package boundaries in [.golangci.yml](.golangci.yml). A new import across a boundary MUST have a decision in [docs/decisions](docs/README.md#decisions).
- Each behavior change MUST update its topic in [docs/spec](docs/README.md#specifications) in the same commit.
- You MUST keep the journal append-only under [journal.md](docs/spec/journal.md). Recovery MUST follow [recovery.md](docs/spec/recovery.md).
- Hashline profile changes MUST follow [the shared contract](docs/spec/hashline/hashline-common-v1.md), [Light](docs/spec/hashline/hashline-light-v1.md), [Enhanced](docs/spec/hashline/hashline-enhanced-v1.md), and [conformance](docs/spec/hashline/hashline-conformance-v1.md).
- You MUST keep one concern per commit for the module in [go.mod](go.mod). You MUST use the global git identity. You MUST NOT add agent trailers.
- You MUST apply the contribution contract in [CONTRIBUTE.md](CONTRIBUTE.md) and the review contract in [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md).

# Contribute

## Define the change

State the required behavior, the failure your change prevents, and the affected consumer. Do not add an interface, option, dependency, or helper for a possible future need.

When you replace an implementation, migrate all callers in the same change and remove the old code. Do not leave compatibility shims, unused exports, duplicate routes, or commented-out implementations. The `unused`, `staticcheck`, `ineffassign`, and `godox` checks in [.golangci.yml](.golangci.yml) enforce part of this rule. Review the parts that lint cannot detect.

## Keep the implementation direct

Use names, types, and control flow to explain the implementation. Do not use comments to hide unclear logic. Keep required build directives. Use a source citation when it explains a non-obvious protocol rule.

Use `encoding/json/jsontext` for wire, journal, and hot-path JSON. Use `protowire` for Protobuf. You can use `encoding/json/v2` for cold config-shaped data. Use HTTP and streaming codecs for provider adapters, not provider SDKs. [The dependency decision](docs/decisions/dependencies.md) and depguard in [.golangci.yml](.golangci.yml) define the import restrictions.

Avoid an allocation or copy when a slice, reused buffer, or stream can do the same work. Add a package only when it hides a real decision, not when it only forwards calls.

## Prove the behavior

Make each test detect a distinct, plausible defect. Take expected values from an independent oracle or an explicit contract. Do not assert source text, use saved output as proof, or repeat the implementation as the oracle.

For persistence changes, test interruption and damaged input against [journal.md](docs/spec/journal.md) and [recovery.md](docs/spec/recovery.md). For protocol changes, preserve [protocol.md](docs/spec/protocol.md) and the vendored schema tests in `internal/rpc`. For edit changes, test refusal without partial writes under [edit-styles.md](docs/spec/edit-styles.md).

## Use the declared tools

Use the versions pinned in [go.mod](go.mod) and [web/package.json](web/package.json). Do not weaken a gate, raise a limit, or exclude a failing test to make a change pass.

[justfile](justfile) declares `fmt-check`, `vet`, `lint`, `test`, `vuln`, `hashline-model`, `web-check`, and `cf-check`. Run them together with `just verify`. `test` uses the race detector. `hashline-model` skips when `uv` is absent; do not report that skip as a pass.

Use `just web` to install the locked web dependencies and build the assets. `web-check` uses the installed web tools. `cf-check` installs the locked Cloudflare dependencies before its checks. `just dist` builds release binaries, and `just box-image` builds the remote box image.

Report the checks you ran, their results, and any untested requirement. Distinguish local checks from live-provider, reboot, desktop-app, and cloud-service checks.

## Keep the delivery bounded

Ship real behavior, not stubs, placeholder implementations, debug output, or deferred required paths. Write documentation that explains a contract, an action, or a decision the reader needs. Do not add process records without a durable use.

A contribution does not authorize a push, publication, deployment, credential transfer, or cloud resource deletion. Get separate authorization for each action.

# dal and dalgona

## Identity

`dal` (달, "moon") is the minimal agent and terminal interface. `dalgona` (달고나, the Korean sugar candy) is the batteries-included harness built on the same core. One brand family, two products.

Use lowercase `dal` and `dalgona` in running text. The executable names are `dal` and `dalgona`. Keep headings in sentence case and actions verb-first. Errors name what happened and how to fix it. Use no exclamation marks or moon puns in errors and status text. Keep any moon motif to at most one visual mark on a user-facing surface.

## Choose a product

Use dal for the agent and terminal interface without a daemon. Use dalgona for a per-user daemon, durable Starlark workflows, remote runners, MCP tools, a web interface, and Codex desktop integration. Both use the same agent core and Codex-compatible client protocol. An optional advisor reviews a thread and sends notes. It does not approve actions.

Sessions use an append-only JSONL journal with a SQLite mirror. Recovery follows recorded tool outcomes rather than assuming that an interrupted command did nothing. See [recovery](docs/spec/recovery.md) for the cases that can resume and those that must report interruption.

## Build from this checkout

Install the Go toolchain declared in [go.mod](go.mod), then run from the repository root:

```sh
go install ./cmd/...
dal --version
dalgona --version
```

Go installs both binaries in `GOBIN`, or in `GOPATH/bin` when `GOBIN` is unset. Add that directory to `PATH` if your shell cannot find them.

Use `just dist` to build release binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64. `just box-image` builds the remote box image from those binaries.

## Start dal

Start the terminal interface:

```sh
dal
```

In the terminal interface, run `/login <provider>` to sign in, then `/model` to select an offered model. Replace `<provider>` with your provider id, such as `openai` or `anthropic`. API-key providers can use their provider environment variables. No default thread model is shipped.

Enter a task in the composer. Use `/resume` to select an existing session, `/new` to start another, and Esc to interrupt a turn. [The TUI contract](docs/spec/tui.md) lists the commands and keys.

Dal uses `$DAL_HOME`, or `~/.dal` when the variable is unset.

## Start dalgona

Start the daemon-backed terminal interface:

```sh
dalgona
```

The client starts the user daemon when needed and connects to it. Use `/login <provider>` and `/model` in the terminal interface. Reopen a recorded thread with:

```sh
dalgona --resume <thread-id>
```

For login-time startup, use `dalgona service install`. Use `dalgona service uninstall` to remove that startup configuration. The platform service rules are in [daemon.md](docs/spec/daemon.md).

Dalgona uses `$DALGONA_HOME`, or `~/.dalgona` when the variable is unset. It does not share dal's home.

## Configure a product

Put user configuration in `<home>/config.toml`. The program stores mutable settings in `<home>/settings.toml`. Settings override config, which overrides defaults. Client flags such as `-m`, `--approval`, and `--sandbox` set thread options. `--remote` overrides the configured `remote`. Unknown config keys fail loading.

Both products accept this configuration:

```toml
approval = "auto"
sandbox = "workspace-write"

[approval_decider]
decider = "decisions:typesafe/jev-1.14"
threshold = 0.9

[advisor]
enabled = false
```

`auto` uses static rules and an automated decider. A missing or failed decider declines actions that need its decision. Use `ask` for human approval. Use `yolo` only when you intend to bypass the decider and turn off harness confinement.

Set `enabled = true` in `[advisor]` to request transcript reviews. Use `[advisors.<name>]` for named reviewers. There is no `--advisor` CLI flag. [The advisor contract](docs/spec/advisor.md) defines model selection, review timing, and note delivery.

Use `[approval_decider]`, not `[approval]`. TOML cannot use `approval` as both a scalar and a table. See [configuration](docs/spec/config.md) for keys, provider endpoints, edit styles, and product restrictions.

Use these table names and keys:

| Scope | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Both products, top level | `model`, `reasoning`, `approval`, `sandbox`, `sandbox_writable_roots`, `edit_style`, `compaction_threshold`, `compaction_keep_tokens`, `stream_start_timeout`, `stream_idle_timeout` |
| `[providers.<name>]` | `base_url`, `api_key_env` |
| `[models.<name>]` | `context_window` |
| `[approval_decider]` | `decider`, `threshold` |
| `[roles]` | `smol`, `slow`, `advisor` |
| `[advisor]` | `enabled`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `continue_severity`, `immune_turns`, `max_notes`, `tools`, `subagents` |
| `[advisors.<name>]` | `model`, `instructions`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `tools`, `enabled` |
| `[secrets]` | `patterns` |
| `[keywords.<name>]` | `notice`, `text`, `hue`, `effort`, `requires`, `enabled` |
| Dalgona only, top level | `tool_mode`, `runner`, `remote` |
| `[runners.<name>]` (dalgona) | `service`, `image`, `template`, `url` |
| `[remotes.<name>]` (dalgona) | `service`, `image`, `template`, `url`, `box_id` |
| `[mcp_servers.<name>]` (dalgona) | `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` |
| `[discovery]` (dalgona) | `sources` |
| `[eval]` (dalgona) | `uses` |
| `[herdr]` (dalgona) | `subagent_panes` |
| `[web]` (dalgona) | `listen`, `token`, `cert_file`, `key_file` |

`edit_style` accepts a style name or a table of model globs with a required `default` entry. Styles are `anchor`, `replace`, `hashline`, `hashline-light`, `hashline-enhanced`, `apply_patch`, `simple`, `balanced`, and `strict`. Model globs match in declaration order. Dal rejects the dalgona-only settings.

## Run inside an outer sandbox

Run dalgona inside a lightweight outer sandbox, such as a container, microVM, or cloud sandbox runner. The local harness sandbox prevents accidental writes outside the workspace and configured writable roots. It is not a security boundary. It permits reads and network access.

Windows has no harness confinement. Linux runs without it when Landlock is unavailable. A remote box supplies the sandbox instead of the local write policy. See [sandbox.md](docs/spec/sandbox.md).

## Connect the Codex desktop app

Install the desktop override:

```sh
dalgona codex install
```

Restart the Codex desktop app after installation. The installer records prior settings before it changes the user-level executable override. Use `dalgona codex status` to inspect the override and `dalgona codex uninstall` to restore it. The integration does not patch the signed app bundle. See [Codex app integration](docs/spec/codex-app.md).

`dalgona app-server` bridges the desktop protocol. Its default listener is standard input and output. The app-server and the terminal interface use the same daemon protocol.

## Choose where execution runs

### Keep the orchestrator local

Set `runner` to a named entry in dalgona's config. For example:

```toml
runner = "devbox"

[runners.devbox]
service = "docker"
```

The runner uploads the workspace, records its baseline, and runs tools and subagents in the box. Supported service choices are `docker`, `sprites`, `modal`, `sandbox0`, and `cloudflare`. A fork shares its parent's box. Archiving one thread does not destroy a box still used by another thread.

Use `dalgona pull <thread-id>` to apply the box's changes to the local workspace with `git apply --3way`. Conflicts leave markers and return exit code 1 with the affected files. `dalgona runner gc` lists unused boxes without deleting them. Use `dalgona runner gc --yes` to delete them.

### Run the whole daemon in a box

Configure `[remotes.<name>]`, then run:

```sh
dalgona cloud up <name>
dalgona --remote <name>
dalgona cloud pull <name>
dalgona cloud down <name>
```

The named remote uses Docker, Sprites, Modal, or Sandbox0. Cloudflare cannot host a durable whole-daemon home because its containers lose their files on stop.

`cloud up` does not copy credentials unless you pass `--copy-auth`. Without credential copying, use `dalgona --remote <name> login` to authenticate in the box. Remote service and box identifiers live in `[remotes.<name>]` in `settings.toml`.

`cloud down` destroys the box and its journal after confirmation. `--yes` skips that confirmation for scripts. Pull changes you need before deletion.

Use `--remote <name>` with the terminal client, `web`, or `app-server` to connect to the in-box daemon through its bridge. See [the service decision](docs/decisions/sandbox-services.md) and [exec-server wire](docs/spec/exec-server.md) for persistence and transport rules.

## Other product commands

Both products accept these client commands and flags:

| Command or flag | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dal`, `dalgona` | Open the terminal interface. |
| `login [provider]` | List providers or sign in to one. |
| `logout <provider>` | Remove a stored credential. |
| `models` | List offered models. |
| `-p <prompt>` | Run one turn and exit. |
| `--json` | With `-p`, print one JSON status line. |
| `--resume <thread-id>` | Resume a recorded thread. |
| `-c` | Continue the latest thread; cannot combine with `--resume`. |
| `-m <model-id>` | Select the model for a new thread. |
| `--approval auto\|ask\|yolo` | Set the approval mode. |
| `--sandbox workspace-write\|off` | Set the harness sandbox mode. |
| `-C <directory>` | Change the working directory. |
| `--help`, `--version` | Print client flag help or the build version. |

Prefix client commands with the product name, for example `dal models` or `dalgona -p "Explain this repository"`. Dalgona also accepts `--remote <name>` to select a configured remote instead of the local daemon.

These commands are specific to dalgona:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dalgona daemon` | Run the per-user daemon. |
| `dalgona app-server [--listen <address>]` | Bridge the desktop protocol over standard input and output or a loopback WebSocket. |
| `dalgona service install\|uninstall` | Add or remove login-time daemon startup. |
| `dalgona pull <thread-id>` | Apply a thread box's changes locally. |
| `dalgona runner gc [--yes]` | List unused boxes, or delete them with `--yes`. |
| `dalgona cloud up <name> [--copy-auth]` | Create a whole-daemon box. |
| `dalgona cloud pull <name>` | Apply a whole-daemon box's workspace changes locally. |
| `dalgona cloud down <name> [--yes]` | Destroy a whole-daemon box. |
| `dalgona codex install\|uninstall\|status` | Manage the desktop executable override. |
| `dalgona codex record --real <codex-path> [args...]` | Record protocol metadata while running the selected Codex executable. |
| `dalgona web` | Serve the web interface; set its listener, token, and TLS files in `[web]`, not CLI flags. See [web access rules](docs/spec/web.md). |
| `dalgona run <file.star> [--arg k=v ...]` | Run a durable Starlark workflow. A value that is valid JSON is passed as JSON; any other value is passed as a string. |
| `dalgona exec-server [--listen <address>] [--root <directory>] [--data <directory>]` | Serve process and filesystem operations inside a box. |
| `dalgona bridge` | Connect standard input and output to the local daemon, starting it if needed. |
| `just dist` | Build release binaries for remote bootstrap. |
| `just box-image` | Build the remote box image. |

`app-server` defaults to `stdio://`. Its WebSocket listener accepts `ws://<loopback-address>:<port>`. Use repeated `-c key=value` or `--config key=value` arguments to set `model`, `approval_policy`, or `sandbox_mode` for new desktop threads.

`exec-server` defaults to `--listen stdio:// --root /workspace`. Its WebSocket listener accepts `ws://IP:PORT` and requires `DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN` with at least 32 characters. `--data` selects a persistent data directory. The bridge and exec server run where you invoke them; `--remote` does not redirect them.

`codex record` defaults to forwarding `app-server` when you omit arguments. It writes protocol metadata to `<home>/census/<unix-seconds>.jsonl`.

## Read the contracts and contribute

[The documentation index](docs/README.md) links every current specification and decision. Start with [journal](docs/spec/journal.md), [recovery](docs/spec/recovery.md), and [protocol](docs/spec/protocol.md) for the core contracts.

Read [CONTRIBUTE.md](CONTRIBUTE.md) before changing code and [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md) before reviewing it. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) contains repository instructions for coding agents. [justfile](justfile) declares the available checks. `just verify` runs the Go, web, and Cloudflare checks. It also runs the hashline model check when `uv` is installed.

# Review

## Report defects, not preferences

Each finding MUST name the defect, its location, the affected consumer, and the consequence. It MUST quote or cite the evidence. Severity MUST describe the harm in plain words. A review MUST NOT invent a failure or claim that an unrun check passed.

A finding SHOULD include a test that fails on the defect. It MUST use a declared check from [justfile](justfile), a focused Go test, or a web script from [web/package.json](web/package.json). A saved-output pin or source-text assertion MUST NOT count as proof.

## Check the authority boundaries

A journal change MUST preserve raw event bytes, sequence order, CRC, and the hash chain. It MUST NOT silently discard a committed event. A damaged session MUST remain read-only. Use [journal.md](docs/spec/journal.md) and the tests in `internal/journal`.

A recovery change MUST classify each pending tool call under [recovery.md](docs/spec/recovery.md). It MUST NOT rerun an unknown command outcome as if the command never ran. A repeated runner call id MUST NOT create a second process. Use [runner.md](docs/spec/runner.md) and the recovery tests in `internal/agent`.

A protocol change MUST preserve request ids, item ids, notification order, and the Codex schema. The review MUST inspect both the server response and its client consumer. Use [protocol.md](docs/spec/protocol.md) and `internal/rpc/testdata/codex-schema`.

An approval change MUST preserve the gate order in [approvals.md](docs/spec/approvals.md). A static refusal MUST NOT reach the automated decider. An advisor note MUST NOT approve an action. Use [advisor.md](docs/spec/advisor.md) for the advisor boundary.

A secret-handling change MUST keep raw secret values out of model input and the journal. It MUST preserve restart-safe placeholder mappings. Unmasking MUST remain at the exec and patch boundary. Use [secrets.md](docs/spec/secrets.md).

The local harness sandbox MUST NOT be described as a security boundary. An unavailable sandbox MUST NOT be reported as active. Use [sandbox.md](docs/spec/sandbox.md).

## Reject unnecessary structure

The review MUST flag a forbidden import, a dependency cycle, a pass-through layer, or an interface with no required seam. [.golangci.yml](.golangci.yml) defines the package boundaries and import bans.

The review MUST flag dead code, unused exports, placeholder paths, duplicate implementations, commented-out code, and temporary debug output. It MUST also flag a partial caller migration or an obsolete compatibility path. A line-count goal MUST NOT justify removal of a required error path, evidence clause, or test oracle.

## Record the result

The review MUST state which defects remain and which checks supplied evidence. It MUST distinguish a passing test from inspection and from an untested claim. Approval MUST NOT imply that live credentials, host reboot, the Codex desktop app, or a cloud service were exercised when they were not.

# Automated approval

## Invariant

Approval mode `auto` MUST use mechanical rules and an automated decider. It MUST NOT wait for a human. Human approval MUST occur only in `ask`. Mode `yolo` MUST bypass the decider and disable the harness sandbox.

The gate MUST apply hooks, mode handling, mechanical allows, static refusals, and the selected decision path in the order in [approvals.md](../spec/approvals.md). A static refusal MUST NOT reach the decider. A missing or failed decider MUST decline. An advisor MUST NOT approve or reject an action.

## Scope

This decision applies to primary, child, script-inner, remote-tool, and advisor investigative calls that enter the agent gate. Config MUST put the mode in `approval` and the decider settings in `[approval_decider]`. [config.md](../spec/config.md) defines that TOML shape. [decide.md](../spec/decide.md) defines adapter answers.

## Enforcement

`internal/agent/approval_test.go` checks score thresholds, static refusals, decider timeouts, `yolo`, session grants, and `ask` without a client. `internal/config/config_test.go` checks mode validation and rejects the old approval table. `just test` runs these tests.

# Journal authority and mirror

## Invariant

JSONL MUST be the event authority. SQLite MUST remain a repairable mirror. A successful JSONL append MUST NOT disappear because a mirror write fails. The store MUST validate the sequence, CRC, and hash chain before replay.

Repair MUST use verified records. A damaged session MUST retain its valid prefix and remain read-only. The store MUST quarantine damaged bytes. It MUST NOT discard a committed event without reporting the damage.

## Scope

This decision applies to `internal/journal` and all state derived from its events. [journal.md](../spec/journal.md) defines the record, append, repair, backup, and lock rules. [recovery.md](../spec/recovery.md) defines tool recovery. SQLite is not an independent source of session truth.

## Enforcement

`internal/journal/journal_test.go` checks truncated tails, middle-record repair, damage without a usable mirror, corrupt SQLite, restored tails, and writer exclusion. Event-fold tests in `internal/agent/event/state_test.go` check derived state. `just test` runs these tests with the race detector.

# Minimal harness sandbox

## Invariant

The harness sandbox MUST prevent accidental writes outside the allowed roots. It MUST NOT claim to isolate hostile code. Users SHOULD run dalgona in an outer container, microVM, or cloud sandbox.

`workspace-write` MUST be the default local policy. Reads and network access MUST remain allowed. `off` MUST disable confinement. Approval mode `yolo` MUST force `off`. Windows and Linux without Landlock MUST report that no harness sandbox is active.

## Scope

This decision applies to local execution in `internal/runner`. It does not add a second sandbox inside a remote box. [sandbox.md](../spec/sandbox.md) defines roots, platform behavior, and failure handling.

## Enforcement

Runner sandbox tests in `internal/runner` check policy construction and platform behavior. The shim MUST write a nonzero exit record when policy application fails. Review MUST reject any status or documentation that calls the harness policy a security boundary. `just test` runs the Go tests; platform-specific behavior still requires the matching host.

# Model presets

## Invariant

The program MUST NOT ship a default thread model. The user MUST select the thread model. A role preset MUST NOT grant access to a model that the provider does not offer.

`internal/model/presets.go` MUST hold the native provider identifiers in one table:

| Provider | default selection hint | smol | slow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openai`, `chatgpt` | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `gpt-6-luna` | `gpt-6-astra` |
| `anthropic` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `claude-fable-5-1` |
| `google` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `gemini-4-argon` |
| Other providers | First offered id | First offered id | First offered id |

An explicit `[roles]` value MUST override the preset. An unavailable role preset MUST fall back to the thread model and log `roles.<name> preset <id> is not offered; using <model>`. The `advisor` role MUST resolve through its explicit role, the explicit `slow` role, the provider slow preset, and then the thread model. Advisor effort MUST be `medium`, clamped to the model's supported effort levels.

## Scope

This decision applies to model selection and role resolution, not provider entitlement. [providers.md](../spec/providers.md) and [advisor.md](../spec/advisor.md) define runtime behavior. The `default` column is a model-picker hint, not a configured thread model.

## Selection evidence

The approved selection record dated 2026-11-08 cites the native model guides for [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md), [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview.md), and [Google](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models). It selected Sol over Astra for the same recorded Terminal-Bench score at a lower price. It selected Opus over Fable for the default role. These are the recorded design inputs, not new measurements from this repository.

| Recorded comparison | Selection evidence |
| --- | --- |
| [Terminal-Bench 4.0](https://snorkel.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/), page dated 2026-10-27 | Opus 5.5 with Claude Code at max effort: 64.8 +/- 3.1. Sonnet 5.5: 61.8 +/- 2.9. Astra with Codex: 58.2 +/- 2.8. Sol with Codex: 58.2 +/- 3.1. |
| [SWE-bench Pro public](https://labs.scale.com/leaderboard/swe_bench_pro) | Muse Spark 1.1: 61.50 +/- 3.10. GPT-5.4 at xHigh: 59.10 +/- 3.56. The record notes no run date and a table that predates GPT-6. |
| [SWE-bench Verified](https://openai.com/index/why-we-no-longer-evaluate-swe-bench-verified/) | The record excludes this benchmark after OpenAI stopped reporting it on 2026-02-23 because of contamination. |
| [OpenRouter programming usage](https://openrouter.ai/collections/programming/), data through 2026-11-07 | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: 26.4%. GLM 5.3 Flash: 6.3%. Step 5 Preview: 6.1%. These figures measure traffic, not quality. |

The record cross-checked native names against [OpenRouter's catalog](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models). OpenRouter identifiers MUST NOT replace native identifiers on a provider wire. Subscription availability MUST still follow the provider's offered list. The record cites [ChatGPT model documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models/) and [Claude Code model aliases](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config/), not an endpoint allowlist.

## Enforcement

`TestResolveRole` and `TestClampEffort` in `internal/model/model_test.go` check fallback and effort handling. `TestRoleResolutionUsesPresetsAndFallsBack` in `internal/agent/misc_test.go` checks host role resolution. `internal/config/advisor_test.go` checks advisor role inheritance. `just test` runs these tests. None of these tests proves that a live account offers a preset.

# Secret masking

## Invariant

Raw secret values covered by the masker MUST NOT enter the journal or a model request. Reversible placeholders MUST enter those surfaces instead. Values shorter than eight bytes are outside the masking contract.

Exec and patch MUST restore known placeholders at the execution or edit-resolution boundary. Other tools MUST NOT gain a general unmask step. Unknown placeholders MUST remain unchanged. Pattern mappings MUST persist before masked text leaves the masker. A persistence failure MUST return an error, not a raw secret or an unrecoverable placeholder.

## Scope

This decision applies to credentials, configured secret patterns, prompts, tool output, and the exec and patch tools. [secrets.md](../spec/secrets.md) defines placeholder formats and file permissions. Masking is not a claim that every possible secret string can be detected.

## Enforcement

`internal/auth/auth_test.go` checks longest matches, short values, placeholder stability, OAuth field separation, persistence, and failure retry. `TestSecretsAreMaskedInJournalAndUnmaskedInExec` in `internal/agent/misc_test.go` checks the journal and model boundary. `internal/tool/patch/property_test.go` checks locator and body restoration without path substitution. `just test` runs these checks.

# Two products

## Invariant

`dal` MUST remain the minimal agent and terminal interface. `dalgona` MUST compose the same core with daemon and battery packages. Both products MUST live in one Go module. The repository MUST NOT maintain a private implementation split.

Each product MUST use its own home. `dal` MUST use `$DAL_HOME` or `~/.dal`. `dalgona` MUST use `$DALGONA_HOME` or `~/.dalgona`. Config MUST reject a dalgona-only setting in dal.

## Scope

This decision applies to `cmd/dal`, `cmd/dalgona`, and `internal/config`. [README.md](../../README.md) defines the product names. [config.md](../spec/config.md) defines the config boundary.

## Enforcement

The `dal` depguard rule in [.golangci.yml](../../.golangci.yml) rejects battery imports from `cmd/dal`. The `core` and `clients` rules keep interface packages out of the core and core packages out of clients. Config tests in `internal/config` check product-specific key rejection. `just lint` and `just test` run these checks.

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Fix `read dalgona://<page>`: the model can now read the Dalgona manual, not only the `dalgona docs` command.
- Fix the review battery: `/review` can now read the git status and diff of a session, so it reports findings instead of failing with a workspace-size error.
- Fix the history compaction notice for a model that reads images when this host cannot store them: it now says `history: this host cannot commit image parts.` instead of `history: the journal source is unavailable.`, and the text summary still runs.
- Fix goal saving errors: a failed write of the goal file now reports `goal: saving the goal failed: <message>` instead of a raw file error.
- Make `/abort` continue cancelling child sessions when status checks fail, report unexpected replies, and stop after a bounded sweep with active session ids.
- Fix finished orchestration children that kept their runtime until the session ended: a run now closes each child as soon as its report arrives, with or without a connected client, and shows a notice if the close fails.
- Require the user to run `/review` before a capped review can restart, and clear unused restart grants when a session closes.
- Keep compaction images within the request size limit: history compaction now subtracts the bytes of the images that stay in the request from its image byte budget, so it draws fewer images, or declines, instead of building a request the provider rejects.
- Add opt-in fenced-diagram rendering to TUI transcript rows and ask previews; Dalgona asks models for supported diagram fences when enabled.
- Assemble Dalgona's batteries as bundled Rust extensions through dal's public extension API.
- Stop the review tool at the round cap and list the findings still open; running `/review` after the cap starts a new session through the new `restart` argument, which never discards rounds in progress.
- Fix MCP servers that use OAuth when several calls get a 401 at once: one token refresh serves all of them. A refresh that fails for a temporary reason, such as a network error or a server error, no longer forces a new login, and a token from a new login replaces the old token for every connection.
- Fix `/abort` and session end with orchestration children: every queued or running child and its descendants are cancelled, and a failed cancel or list no longer stops the sweep. `/abort` reports each failure with the child id, and `agents cancel` tries every named id and reports each refusal.

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-26)

- Initial release of the headless loop, terminal, compiled batteries, wire surfaces, and manual.

# Advisor

The advisor is an optional reviewer. It reads the transcript of a primary thread and sends short notes back into that thread. Both products, `dal` and `dalgona`, MUST support it. The advisor MUST NOT approve or reject actions. The advisor MUST NOT change primary session state, except when it delivers a note.

## Configuration

`config.toml` and `settings.toml` MAY contain an `[advisor]` table and an `[advisors.<name>]` roster. Both products MUST accept both tables. `settings.toml` MUST override `config.toml` key by key. Unknown keys MUST fail `config.Load` with `<file>:<line>: unknown key "<key>"`.

| Key | Type | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `advisor.enabled` | bool | `false` | `--advisor` MUST set it to `true` for one run. |
| `advisor.review` | string | `"turn"` | `turn`, `agent-end` |
| `advisor.interval` | int | `1` | 1 or more |
| `advisor.sync` | string | `"off"` | `off`, `final`, `strict` |
| `advisor.continue_severity` | string | `"blocker"` | `nit`, `concern`, `blocker` |
| `advisor.immune_turns` | int | `3` | 0 or more |
| `advisor.max_notes` | int | `3` | 0 or more |
| `advisor.tools` | string list | `["read", "search"]` | Tool names. `[]` grants no investigative tool. |
| `advisor.subagents` | bool | `false` | `true` MUST advise subagents too. |

An `[advisors.<name>]` entry MAY set `model`, `instructions`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `tools`, `subagents`, and `enabled`. An omitted `review`, `interval`, `sync`, or `tools` MUST inherit the `[advisor]` value. An explicit `tools = []` MUST replace the inherited list. An omitted `subagents` MUST inherit the subagent decision of `[advisor]`. `enabled` MUST default to `true`. `model` and `instructions` MUST default to `""`.

When no `[advisors.<name>]` entry exists, the roster MUST contain exactly one advisor named `advisor` with inherited values. When one or more entries exist, the roster MUST contain only those entries.

An advisor runs only when `advisor.enabled` is `true` and its entry has `enabled = true`.

### Validation

`config.Load` MUST reject an invalid value with `<file>:<line>: <message>`. The line MUST point at the key. Each message MUST match byte for byte:

| Key | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `advisor.review` | `[advisor] review must be one of turn, agent-end` |
| `advisor.interval` | `[advisor] interval must be at least 1` |
| `advisor.sync` | `[advisor] sync must be one of off, final, strict` |
| `advisor.continue_severity` | `[advisor] continue_severity must be one of nit, concern, blocker` |
| `advisor.immune_turns` | `[advisor] immune_turns must not be negative` |
| `advisor.max_notes` | `[advisor] max_notes must not be negative` |
| `advisors.<name>` | `[advisors.<name>] name must be lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, 1-32 chars` |
| `advisors.<name>.model` | `[advisors.<name>] model must be smol, default, slow, advisor, or provider/model` |
| `advisors.<name>.review` | `[advisors.<name>] review must be one of turn, agent-end` |
| `advisors.<name>.interval` | `[advisors.<name>] interval must be at least 1` |
| `advisors.<name>.sync` | `[advisors.<name>] sync must be one of off, final, strict` |

A name MUST match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`. When a name is invalid, the loader MUST report only the name error for that entry. Errors MUST come in this order: `[advisor]` keys, then entries sorted by name. Inside one table, the order MUST be `review`, `interval`, `sync`, then the table-specific keys.

### Model role

`[roles] advisor` names the advisor model. An empty entry `model` MUST mean the role `advisor`. The role `advisor` MUST resolve in this order:

1. `[roles] advisor`, when set.
2. `[roles] slow`, when set.
3. The `slow` preset of the thread model's provider, when the provider offers it.
4. The thread model.

When the preset is not offered, the resolver MUST log `roles.advisor preset <id> is not offered; using <model>`. The advisor request MUST ask for effort `medium`, clamped to the efforts that the model supports.

## WATCHDOG.md

`WATCHDOG.md` holds guidance for the advisor only. The primary thread MUST NOT receive it.

`Watchdog(home, cwd)` MUST read candidates in this order:

1. `<home>/WATCHDOG.md`.
2. For each directory from the repository root down to `cwd`: `<dir>/WATCHDOG.md`, then `<dir>/.dalgona/WATCHDOG.md`.

The repository root is the nearest ancestor of `cwd`, or `cwd` itself, that contains a `.git` directory or file. When no such ancestor exists, step 2 MUST use only `cwd`. A path MUST appear at most once. The first occurrence MUST keep its position. A candidate that is missing, unreadable, or not a regular file MUST be skipped without error. A FIFO or a directory named `WATCHDOG.md` MUST NOT block discovery.

Each file MUST be wrapped as `<watchdog path="<path>">` + content + `</watchdog>`. The path MUST be HTML-escaped. The content MUST NOT be changed. Blocks MUST be joined with one blank line. When no file is read, the result MUST be the empty string.

## Advisor system prompt

`System(maxNotes, instructions, watchdog)` MUST return the embedded prompt with `{{max_notes}}` replaced by `maxNotes`. Non-empty trimmed `instructions` MUST follow as `<specialization>\n<instructions>\n</specialization>`. A non-empty `watchdog` MUST follow last. Parts MUST be joined with one blank line.

## Runtime

There MUST be one advisor runtime per pair of thread and advisor name. The runtime MUST be a child session in the journal: `session.created` with `parent` and `advisor: <name>`. Its transcript, usage, and in-flight review MUST recover after a crash like any thread. The advisor MUST NOT be a peer. `thread/list` MUST NOT list it. Clients MUST NOT address it, except read-only through `thread/read`.

`Attach(ctx, host, thread, cfg)` MUST build one runtime for every roster entry of the thread. The runtime MUST create the advisor session at its first review. An existing advisor session MUST be resumed with the advisor tools and prompt. `Runtime.Close` MUST remove the boundary hook, stop the review loops, and close every advisor session. A later `Attach` MUST then resume the session with its own tools. When `Attach` fails, it MUST close every advisor session that it opened.

The advisor model MUST be the first non-empty value of: the entry `model`, `[roles] advisor`, `[roles] slow`, the role `advisor`. The host role resolver MUST then resolve that value against the thread model.

### Review input

A review MUST receive the primary's new active-path events after the advisor cursor (a journal seq). The cursor MUST reset on compaction, revert, leaf move, and fork. After a reset, the next review MUST replay the bounded current active path. When the advisor is enabled mid-session, the cursor MUST start at the current head. A fork without an advisor session MUST start its cursor at 0.

The review text MUST be at most 64 KiB minus 1024 bytes, so that the journal keeps it inline. The runtime MUST keep the newest rendered events that fit. When older events do not fit, the text MUST start with `[<n> earlier events omitted]`. The newest event that does not fit MUST keep its first and last bytes, joined by `\n[<k> bytes omitted]\n`, when at least 64 bytes of budget remain.

The advisor session MUST receive the review as one prompt: `<review seq="<head>">\n` + review text + `</review>\n`. `<head>` MUST be the primary journal head that the review covers. The review prompt MUST be submitted with `Input.Verbatim`, so that keywords and `@path` mentions in the primary transcript add no notice, no attachment, and no effort change. Each review prompt MUST request effort `medium`. After a restart, the cursor MUST be the `seq` of the last review prompt whose advisor turn completed. When no such prompt exists, the cursor MUST start at the current head. The last review prompt MUST then complete once. When it succeeds, the cursor MUST move to its `seq`.

`Render(events)` MUST produce the review text with these elements, one per line group:

| Event | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `user.message` | `<user>\n<text>\n</user>` |
| `assistant.message` reasoning | `<reasoning>\n<text>\n</reasoning>` |
| `assistant.message` text | `<assistant>\n<text>\n</assistant>` |
| `assistant.message` tool call | `<tool_call name="<name>" id="<id>">\n<args>\n</tool_call>` |
| `tool.completed` | `<tool_result id="<id>" ok="<bool>" exit="<code>">\n<output>\n</tool_result>`. `exit` MUST appear only when the event has an exit code. |
| `compaction` | `<summary>\n<summary text>\n</summary>` |
| `turn.completed` with status other than `completed` | `<turn_end status="<status>"><error></turn_end>` |

Every element MUST end with a newline. Text MUST escape `&`, `<`, and `>`. Attributes MUST be HTML-escaped. A blob reference MUST render as `[<bytes> bytes in blob <sha256>]`. Other event types MUST NOT render. `tool.started` MUST NOT render, because the assistant tool call already carries the arguments. Tool output MUST be the masked model-visible projection.

Delivered notes MUST NOT appear in review input. The `advisor.note` event MUST NOT render. Every complete `<advisory ...>...</advisory>` element in user text MUST be removed. The remaining user text segments MUST be trimmed and joined with one newline. A user message with no remaining text MUST NOT render. An unclosed `<advisory` MUST stay as escaped text.

### Cadence

A boundary is the point after a model step whose tool calls all completed (`turn`) or the point where the model stops calling tools (`agent-end`). The end of a failed or interrupted turn MUST also be an `agent-end` boundary, but the primary MUST NOT wait there. With `review = "turn"`, every boundary MUST be eligible. With `review = "agent-end"`, only `agent-end` boundaries MUST be eligible. A boundary of a continuation turn MUST NOT be eligible. Only an advisor `continue` delivery while idle MUST start a continuation turn. Input that arrives while the `turn_end` hook runs MUST start a normal turn when auto-continue is on, and MUST NOT start a turn when auto-continue is off. The advisor MUST review at every `interval`-th eligible boundary. Events from skipped boundaries MUST go into the next review. A review MUST NOT start while the previous review of the same advisor runs. Reviews that are requested during a running review MUST merge into one review.

### Tools

The advisor MUST have the `advise` tool with arguments `{note, severity}`, where `severity` is `nit`, `concern`, or `blocker`. It MUST also have the tools in its `tools` list that the runtime can build: `read`, `search`, `exec`, and `web_fetch`. Other names MUST NOT give the advisor a tool. Those tools MUST run through the same approval gate and runner as primary tools, in the advisor's own snapshot store. An advisor session has no approval client, so it MUST NOT wait for a human decision: in `ask` mode its calls fall back to the configured decider, and decline when no decider is configured. A call to a tool that is not granted MUST return `Tool <name> not found`.

The `advise` result MUST be exactly one word: the guard verdict, or `discarded` when the review output is unsafe (see Failures). An accepted `blocker` MUST go to the primary before the tool returns. An accepted `nit` or `concern` MUST stay pending until the review ends. At the end of a completed review, the runtime MUST deliver the pending notes in order. The runtime MUST compute them from the advisor journal: the accepted `advise` results of this review, applied in order through a fresh guard. A pending note that a later admission names in `Displaced` MUST be dropped. Because `Thread.Deliver` journals each (advisor, review_seq, note) once, a repeated delivery after a crash MUST NOT add an event.

### Emission guard

Each advisor MUST have its own guard. `Normalize(note)` MUST apply, in order: NFKC, lowercase, replace each run of characters that are not Unicode letters or numbers with one space, and trim the ends.

`Guard.Admit(note, severity)` MUST return one verdict. The tool result MUST state it as `accepted`, `duplicate`, `noise`, or `budget`.

- `noise`: the normalized note is empty.
- `duplicate`: since the last reset, the guard accepted the same normalized note at the same or a higher severity. A re-raise at a strictly higher severity MUST NOT be a duplicate.
- `budget`: the note is not a `blocker`, the current review already holds `max_notes` non-blocker notes, and no displacement applies.
- `accepted`: otherwise.

A rejected note MUST NOT change guard state. A `blocker` MUST NOT use a budget slot.

Displacement: when the budget is full, a non-blocker note MAY replace the lowest-severity pending note of the current review, but only when its severity is strictly higher. The admission MUST name the replaced note in `Displaced`. The caller MUST drop that pending note before it queues the accepted note. A re-raise of a pending note from the same review at a higher severity MUST name that note in `Displaced`. A pending note that a `blocker` re-raise replaces MUST free its slot. `Guard.Delivered(key)` MUST mark a note as delivered. A delivered note MUST keep its slot and MUST NOT be displaced. Notes from an earlier review MUST NOT be displaced.

`Guard.BeginReview()` MUST clear the budget slots and MUST keep the duplicate history. `Guard.Reset()` MUST clear both. The runtime MUST call `Reset` when the cursor resets. `Admit` MUST be safe for concurrent calls.

### Delivery

The primary MUST journal each accepted note as `advisor.note {advisor, severity, note, review_seq, delivery}`. The model MUST receive the note in the next user-role content as `<advisory advisor="<name>" severity="<severity>">` + escaped note + `</advisory>`. The note text MUST escape `&`, `<`, and `>`.

`Route(state, severity, policy)` MUST choose `delivery`:

- `steer`: the primary runs, and the note interrupts the current turn.
- `aside`: the note is shown and queued for the next turn without an interrupt.
- `continue`: the primary is idle, and the runtime starts one continuation turn.

The immune window is active when a concern or blocker steer was delivered and fewer than `immune_turns` boundaries have passed since then. Inside the window, a `nit` or `concern` MUST be `aside`. A `blocker` MUST ignore the window.

The primary is running when `Status.Busy` is true. It is idle when it is not busy and auto-continue is on. It is interrupted when it is not busy and auto-continue is off.

| Primary | Severity | Outside window | Inside window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| running | nit | aside | aside |
| running | concern | steer | aside |
| running | blocker | steer | steer |
| idle | below `continue_severity` | aside | aside |
| idle | nit or concern, at or above `continue_severity` | continue | aside |
| idle | blocker | continue | continue |
| interrupted | any | aside | aside |

An idle primary MUST start at most one continuation per batch of notes. After that continuation started, more notes from the batch MUST be `aside`. A continuation MUST NOT schedule another review. A user interrupt (Esc, `turn/interrupt`) MUST put the primary in the interrupted state until the next user input. In that state, auto-continue MUST be off.

### Sync

`sync = "off"` MUST NOT make the primary wait. `sync = "final"` MUST make the primary wait at each `agent-end` boundary until every review requested so far has ended, before it reports the turn completed. `sync = "strict"` MUST also make the primary wait at every boundary that requested a review. A wait MUST end when the review ends with any outcome, when the advisor halts or is disabled, when the primary turn is interrupted, or when the runtime closes.

### Failures

Reviews MUST use the shared retry rules. A review fails when the advisor turn does not complete, when its output is unsafe, or when a delivery fails. After 3 failed reviews in a row, the advisor MUST stop with status `halted`. It MUST stay halted until `Runtime.Reset` (`/advisor reset`) or a restart. A successful review MUST reset the count. A failed review MUST NOT move the cursor.

The output of a review is unsafe when an assistant text of the review contains a destructive shell directive that the review input does not contain. The rule set MUST come from `internal/agent/rules`: `rules.Check` with the rules `recursive-delete`, `git-destructive`, `publish`, and `deploy`. Candidates MUST be each text line, with backticks removed and a leading `$` removed, and each backtick span. An assistant text stored as a blob MUST count as unsafe. A `blocker` MUST be delivered only when the review output up to its call is safe and the advisor is enabled. Otherwise its result MUST be `discarded`. An unsafe review MUST deliver none of its pending notes. A blocker that was delivered before later unsafe output MUST stay delivered. When a live blocker delivery fails, the guard MUST forget that admission, so that a re-raise can be accepted.

### Protocol

The server MUST send the notification `dalgona/advisor/note {threadId, advisor, severity, note, delivery}` for each delivered note. Each note MUST also appear as a `dynamicToolCall` item named `advisor`.

- `dalgona/advisor/status {threadId}` MUST return `[{name, model, status, notes, usage}]`. `status` MUST be `idle`, `reviewing`, `halted`, or `disabled`.
- `dalgona/advisor/set {threadId, enabled}` MUST turn the advisor on or off for the thread.

The server MUST serve these methods from the thread runtime. `Runtime.Status()` MUST return one entry per roster entry, sorted by name. `notes` MUST count the `advisor.note` events of the advisor on the primary active path after its last compaction. `usage` MUST sum the usage of the assistant messages on the advisor session active path after its last compaction. `Runtime.SetEnabled(enabled)` MUST turn every roster entry on or off. An entry with `enabled = false` MUST stay `disabled`. Turning an advisor off MUST interrupt its running review, and that review MUST deliver no more notes and MUST NOT count as a failure. Turning it on MUST start the cursor at the current head.

The TUI MUST render a note as a dim card `advisor · <severity>: <note>`. `/advisor` MUST toggle the advisor. `/advisor status` MUST list the advisors.

### Subagents

A subagent MUST run without an advisor, unless the `task` call, `[advisor] subagents = true`, or the advisor entry opts in. `Attach` MUST start the runtime of a thread with a `parent` as disabled for every advisor that does not apply. An entry with `subagents = true` MUST advise every subagent thread, also when the global key is `false` and the `task` call did not opt in. An entry with `subagents = false` MUST never advise a subagent thread, also when the global key is `true` or the `task` call opted in. An entry with omitted `subagents` MUST advise a subagent exactly when the global rule opts in. A `task` call opts in when its caller passes a configuration with `Subagents` set. The key MUST NOT change behavior on a top-level thread. `[advisor] enabled = false` MUST turn every advisor off, and an entry with `enabled = false` MUST stay off.

# Advisor


## Configuration

`config.toml` and `settings.toml` MAY contain an `[advisor]` table and an `[advisors.<name>]` roster. Both products MUST accept both tables. `settings.toml` MUST override `config.toml` key by key. Unknown keys MUST fail `config.Load` with `<file>:<line>: unknown key "<key>"`.

| Key | Type | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `advisor.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true` MUST turn the advisor on. No command-line flag sets it. |
| `advisor.review` | string | `"turn"` | `turn`, `agent-end` |
| `advisor.interval` | int | `1` | 1 or more |
| `advisor.sync` | string | `"off"` | `off`, `final`, `strict` |
| `advisor.continue_severity` | string | `"blocker"` | `nit`, `concern`, `blocker` |
| `advisor.immune_turns` | int | `3` | 0 or more |
| `advisor.max_notes` | int | `3` | 0 or more |
| `advisor.tools` | string list | `["read", "search"]` | Tool names. `[]` grants no investigative tool. |
| `advisor.subagents` | bool | `false` | `true` MUST advise subagents too. |

An `[advisors.<name>]` entry MAY set `model`, `instructions`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `tools`, `subagents`, and `enabled`. An omitted `review`, `interval`, `sync`, or `tools` MUST inherit the `[advisor]` value. An explicit `tools = []` MUST replace the inherited list. An omitted `subagents` MUST inherit the subagent decision of `[advisor]`. `enabled` MUST default to `true`. `model` and `instructions` MUST default to `""`.

When no `[advisors.<name>]` entry exists, the roster MUST contain exactly one advisor named `advisor` with inherited values. When one or more entries exist, the roster MUST contain only those entries.

An advisor runs only when `advisor.enabled` is `true` and its entry has `enabled = true`.

### Validation

`config.Load` MUST reject an invalid value with `<file>:<line>: <message>`. The line MUST point at the key. Each message MUST match byte for byte:

| Key | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `advisor.review` | `[advisor] review must be one of turn, agent-end` |
| `advisor.interval` | `[advisor] interval must be at least 1` |
| `advisor.sync` | `[advisor] sync must be one of off, final, strict` |
| `advisor.continue_severity` | `[advisor] continue_severity must be one of nit, concern, blocker` |
| `advisor.immune_turns` | `[advisor] immune_turns must not be negative` |
| `advisor.max_notes` | `[advisor] max_notes must not be negative` |
| `advisors.<name>` | `[advisors.<name>] name must be lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, 1-32 chars` |
| `advisors.<name>.model` | `[advisors.<name>] model must be smol, default, slow, advisor, or provider/model` |
| `advisors.<name>.review` | `[advisors.<name>] review must be one of turn, agent-end` |
| `advisors.<name>.interval` | `[advisors.<name>] interval must be at least 1` |
| `advisors.<name>.sync` | `[advisors.<name>] sync must be one of off, final, strict` |

A name MUST match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`. When a name is invalid, the loader MUST report only the name error for that entry. Errors MUST come in this order: `[advisor]` keys, then entries sorted by name. Inside one table, the order MUST be `review`, `interval`, `sync`, then the table-specific keys.

### Model role

`[roles] advisor` names the advisor model. An empty entry `model` MUST mean the role `advisor`. The role `advisor` MUST resolve in this order:

1. `[roles] advisor`, when set.
2. `[roles] slow`, when set.
3. The `slow` preset of the thread model's provider, when the provider offers it.
4. The thread model.

When the preset is not offered, the resolver MUST log `roles.advisor preset <id> is not offered; using <model>`. The advisor request MUST ask for effort `medium`, clamped to the efforts that the model supports.

## WATCHDOG.md

`WATCHDOG.md` holds guidance for the advisor only. The primary thread MUST NOT receive it.

`Watchdog(home, cwd)` MUST read candidates in this order:

1. `<home>/WATCHDOG.md`.
2. For each directory from the repository root down to `cwd`: `<dir>/WATCHDOG.md`, then `<dir>/.dalgona/WATCHDOG.md`.

The repository root is the nearest ancestor of `cwd`, or `cwd` itself, that contains a `.git` directory or file. When no such ancestor exists, step 2 MUST use only `cwd`. A path MUST appear at most once. The first occurrence MUST keep its position. A candidate that is missing, unreadable, or not a regular file MUST be skipped without error. A FIFO or a directory named `WATCHDOG.md` MUST NOT block discovery.

Each file MUST be wrapped as `<watchdog path="<path>">` + content + `</watchdog>`. The path MUST be HTML-escaped. The content MUST NOT be changed. Blocks MUST be joined with one blank line. When no file is read, the result MUST be the empty string.

## Advisor system prompt

`System(maxNotes, instructions, watchdog)` MUST return the embedded prompt with `{{max_notes}}` replaced by `maxNotes`. Non-empty trimmed `instructions` MUST follow as `<specialization>\n<instructions>\n</specialization>`. A non-empty `watchdog` MUST follow last. Parts MUST be joined with one blank line.

## Runtime

There MUST be one advisor runtime per pair of thread and advisor name. The runtime MUST be a child session in the journal: `session.created` with `parent` and `advisor: <name>`. Its transcript, usage, and in-flight review MUST recover after a crash like any thread. The advisor MUST NOT be a peer. `thread/list` MUST NOT list it. Clients MUST NOT address it, except read-only through `thread/read`.

`Attach(ctx, host, thread, cfg)` MUST build one runtime for every roster entry of the thread. The runtime MUST create the advisor session at its first review. An existing advisor session MUST be resumed with the advisor tools and prompt. `Runtime.Close` MUST remove the boundary hook, stop the review loops, and close every advisor session. A later `Attach` MUST then resume the session with its own tools. When `Attach` fails, it MUST close every advisor session that it opened.

The advisor model MUST be the first non-empty value of: the entry `model`, `[roles] advisor`, `[roles] slow`, the role `advisor`. The host role resolver MUST then resolve that value against the thread model.

### Review input

A review MUST receive the primary's new active-path events after the advisor cursor (a journal seq). The cursor MUST reset on compaction, revert, leaf move, and fork. After a reset, the next review MUST replay the bounded current active path. When the advisor is enabled mid-session, the cursor MUST start at the current head. A fork without an advisor session MUST start its cursor at 0.

The review text MUST be at most 64 KiB minus 1024 bytes, so that the journal keeps it inline. The runtime MUST keep the newest rendered events that fit. When older events do not fit, the text MUST start with `[<n> earlier events omitted]`. The newest event that does not fit MUST keep its first and last bytes, joined by `\n[<k> bytes omitted]\n`, when at least 64 bytes of budget remain.

The advisor session MUST receive the review as one prompt: `<review seq="<head>">\n` + review text + `</review>\n`. `<head>` MUST be the primary journal head that the review covers. The review prompt MUST be submitted with `Input.Verbatim`, so that keywords and `@path` mentions in the primary transcript add no notice, no attachment, and no effort change. Each review prompt MUST request effort `medium`. After a restart, the cursor MUST be the `seq` of the last review prompt whose advisor turn completed. When no such prompt exists, the cursor MUST start at the current head. The last review prompt MUST then complete once. When it succeeds, the cursor MUST move to its `seq`.

`Render(events)` MUST produce the review text with these elements, one per line group:

| Event | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `user.message` | `<user>\n<text>\n</user>` |
| `assistant.message` reasoning | `<reasoning>\n<text>\n</reasoning>` |
| `assistant.message` text | `<assistant>\n<text>\n</assistant>` |
| `assistant.message` tool call | `<tool_call name="<name>" id="<id>">\n<args>\n</tool_call>` |
| `tool.completed` | `<tool_result id="<id>" ok="<bool>" exit="<code>">\n<output>\n</tool_result>`. `exit` MUST appear only when the event has an exit code. |
| `compaction` | `<summary>\n<summary text>\n</summary>` |
| `turn.completed` with status other than `completed` | `<turn_end status="<status>"><error></turn_end>` |

Every element MUST end with a newline. Text MUST escape `&`, `<`, and `>`. Attributes MUST be HTML-escaped. A blob reference MUST render as `[<bytes> bytes in blob <sha256>]`. Other event types MUST NOT render. `tool.started` MUST NOT render, because the assistant tool call already carries the arguments. Tool output MUST be the masked model-visible projection.

Delivered notes MUST NOT appear in review input. The `advisor.note` event MUST NOT render. Every complete `<advisory ...>...</advisory>` element in user text MUST be removed. The remaining user text segments MUST be trimmed and joined with one newline. A user message with no remaining text MUST NOT render. An unclosed `<advisory` MUST stay as escaped text.

### Cadence

A boundary is the point after a model step whose tool calls all completed (`turn`) or the point where the model stops calling tools (`agent-end`). The end of a failed or interrupted turn MUST also be an `agent-end` boundary, but the primary MUST NOT wait there. With `review = "turn"`, every boundary MUST be eligible. With `review = "agent-end"`, only `agent-end` boundaries MUST be eligible. A boundary of a continuation turn MUST NOT be eligible. Only an advisor `continue` delivery while idle MUST start a continuation turn. Input that arrives while the `turn_end` hook runs MUST start a normal turn when auto-continue is on, and MUST NOT start a turn when auto-continue is off. The advisor MUST review at every `interval`-th eligible boundary. Events from skipped boundaries MUST go into the next review. A review MUST NOT start while the previous review of the same advisor runs. Reviews that are requested during a running review MUST merge into one review.

### Tools

The advisor MUST have the `advise` tool with arguments `{note, severity}`, where `severity` is `nit`, `concern`, or `blocker`. It MUST also have the tools in its `tools` list that the runtime can build: `read`, `search`, `exec`, and `web_fetch`. Other names MUST NOT give the advisor a tool. Those tools MUST run through the same approval gate and runner as primary tools, in the advisor's own snapshot store. An advisor session has no approval client, so it MUST NOT wait for a human decision: in `ask` mode its calls fall back to the configured decider, and decline when no decider is configured. A call to a tool that is not granted MUST return `Tool <name> not found`.

The `advise` result MUST be exactly one word: the guard verdict, or `discarded` when the review output is unsafe (see Failures). An accepted `blocker` MUST go to the primary before the tool returns. An accepted `nit` or `concern` MUST stay pending until the review ends. At the end of a completed review, the runtime MUST deliver the pending notes in order. The runtime MUST compute them from the advisor journal: the accepted `advise` results of this review, applied in order through a fresh guard. A pending note that a later admission names in `Displaced` MUST be dropped. Because `Thread.Deliver` journals each (advisor, review_seq, note) once, a repeated delivery after a crash MUST NOT add an event.

### Emission guard

Each advisor MUST have its own guard. `Normalize(note)` MUST apply, in order: NFKC, lowercase, replace each run of characters that are not Unicode letters or numbers with one space, and trim the ends.

- `budget`: the note is not a `blocker`, the current review already holds `max_notes` non-blocker notes, and no displacement applies.
- `accepted`: otherwise.

| running | concern | steer | aside |
| running | blocker | steer | steer |
| idle | below `continue_severity` | aside | aside |

files.pre:
[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["gates", "crates/*"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.99.0"
license-file = "../LICENSE.md"
repository = "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona"

[workspace.dependencies]
blake3 = "=1.8.2"
toml = "=1.1.8"

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_docs = "warn"
unused_lifetimes = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
correctness = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }
suspicious = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
complexity = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
perf = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "warn"
panic = "warn"
allow_attributes = "deny"
allow_attributes_without_reason = "deny"
exit = "deny"
disallowed_methods = "deny"

# Fast feedback: line tables keep backtraces readable while compiling much faster than full debug info.
[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"

# Fast feedback: Faster Tests
[profile.test]
opt-level = 3
debug = "line-tables-only"

[profile.dist]
inherits = "release"
files.post:
[workspace]
members = ["gates", "crates/*"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.99.0"
license-file = "../LICENSE.md"
repository = "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona"

[workspace.dependencies]
blake3 = "=1.8.2"
toml = "=1.1.8"

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_docs = "warn"
unused_lifetimes = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
correctness = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }
suspicious = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
complexity = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
perf = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "warn"
panic = "warn"
allow_attributes = "deny"
allow_attributes_without_reason = "deny"
exit = "deny"
disallowed_methods = "deny"

# Fast feedback for dev profile
[profile.dev]
# 1. Limit debug info to just line tables (removes variable/type info).
# Reduces clean build times by ~9% and rebuilds by ~21%.
debug = "line-tables-only"

# 2. Bypass the heavy linker for DWARF debug info (macOS/Linux).
# Keeps debug info in object files instead of packing it into the binary.
split-debuginfo = "unpacked"

# 3. Increase optimization slightly
# Setting this to 1 can sometimes make the compiler generate cleaner code 
# that LLVM backend can process faster, without doing heavy optimizations.
opt-level = 1

# Fast feedback for test profile
[profile.test]
opt-level = 3
split-debuginfo = "unpacked"

[profile.dist]
inherits = "release"

# dal and dalgona

## Identity

`dal` (달, "moon") is the minimal agent and terminal interface. `dalgona` (달고나, the Korean sugar candy) is the batteries-included harness built on the same core. One brand family, two products.

Use lowercase `dal` and `dalgona` in running text. The executable names are `dal` and `dalgona`. Keep headings in sentence case and actions verb-first. Errors name what happened and how to fix it. Use no exclamation marks or moon puns in errors and status text. Keep any moon motif to at most one visual mark on a user-facing surface.

## Choose a product

Use dal for the agent and terminal interface without a daemon. Use dalgona for a per-user daemon, durable Starlark workflows, remote runners, MCP tools, a web interface, and Codex desktop integration. Both use the same agent core and Codex-compatible client protocol. An optional advisor reviews a thread and sends notes. It does not approve actions.

Sessions use an append-only JSONL journal with a SQLite mirror. Recovery follows recorded tool outcomes rather than assuming that an interrupted command did nothing. See [recovery](docs/spec/recovery.md) for the cases that can resume and those that must report interruption.

## Build from this checkout

Install the Go toolchain declared in [go.mod](go.mod), then run from the repository root:

```sh
go install ./cmd/...
dal --version
dalgona --version
```

Go installs both binaries in `GOBIN`, or in `GOPATH/bin` when `GOBIN` is unset. Add that directory to `PATH` if your shell cannot find them.

`just build` builds both binaries for your platform into `bin/`. `just dal [args...]` and `just dalgona [args...]` run a command from source without installing it, for example `just dalgona web`.

Use `just dist` to build release binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64. `just box-image` builds the remote box image from those binaries.

## Start dal

Start the terminal interface:

```sh
dal
```

In the terminal interface, run `/login <provider>` to sign in, then `/model` to select an offered model. Replace `<provider>` with your provider id, such as `openai` or `anthropic`. API-key providers can use their provider environment variables. No default thread model is shipped.

Enter a task in the composer. Use `/resume` to select an existing session, `/new` to start another, and Esc to interrupt a turn. [The TUI contract](docs/spec/tui.md) lists the commands and keys.

Dal uses `$DAL_HOME`, or `~/.dal` when the variable is unset. On Windows, dal sets a private access list on this directory for your user account, SYSTEM, and Administrators.

## Start dalgona

Start the daemon-backed terminal interface:

```sh
dalgona
```

The client starts the user daemon when needed and connects to it. Use `/login <provider>` and `/model` in the terminal interface. Reopen a recorded thread with:

```sh
dalgona --resume <thread-id>
```

For login-time startup, use `dalgona service install`. Use `dalgona service uninstall` to remove that startup configuration. The platform service rules are in [daemon.md](docs/spec/daemon.md).

Dalgona uses `$DALGONA_HOME`, or `~/.dalgona` when the variable is unset. It does not share dal's home. On Windows, dalgona sets a private access list on this directory for your user account, SYSTEM, and Administrators: daemon start resets the list on the home and everything inside it, and a client refuses to start when it cannot protect the home.

## Configure a product

Put user configuration in `<home>/config.toml`. The program stores mutable settings in `<home>/settings.toml`. Settings override config, which overrides defaults. Client flags such as `-m`, `--approval`, and `--sandbox` set thread options. `--remote` overrides the configured `remote`. Unknown config keys fail loading.

Both products accept this configuration:

```toml
approval = "auto"
sandbox = "workspace-write"

[approval_decider]
decider = "decisions:typesafe/jev-1.14"
threshold = 0.9

[advisor]
enabled = false
```

`auto` uses static rules and an automated decider. A missing or failed decider declines actions that need its decision. Use `ask` for human approval. Use `yolo` only when you intend to bypass the decider and turn off harness confinement.

Set `enabled = true` in `[advisor]` to request transcript reviews. Use `[advisors.<name>]` for named reviewers. There is no `--advisor` CLI flag. [The advisor contract](docs/spec/advisor.md) defines model selection, review timing, and note delivery.

Use `[approval_decider]`, not `[approval]`. TOML cannot use `approval` as both a scalar and a table. See [configuration](docs/spec/config.md) for keys, provider endpoints, edit styles, and product restrictions.

Use these table names and keys:

| Scope | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Both products, top level | `model`, `reasoning`, `approval`, `sandbox`, `sandbox_writable_roots`, `edit_style`, `compaction_threshold`, `compaction_keep_tokens`, `stream_start_timeout`, `stream_idle_timeout` |
| `[providers.<name>]` | `base_url`, `api_key_env` |
| `[models.<name>]` | `context_window` |
| `[approval_decider]` | `decider`, `threshold` |
| `[roles]` | `smol`, `slow`, `advisor` |
| `[advisor]` | `enabled`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `continue_severity`, `immune_turns`, `max_notes`, `tools`, `subagents` |
| `[advisors.<name>]` | `model`, `instructions`, `review`, `interval`, `sync`, `tools`, `subagents`, `enabled` |
| `[secrets]` | `patterns` |
| `[keywords.<name>]` | `notice`, `text`, `hue`, `effort`, `requires`, `enabled` |
| Dalgona only, top level | `tool_mode`, `runner`, `remote` |
| `[runners.<name>]` (dalgona) | `service`, `image`, `template`, `url` |
| `[remotes.<name>]` (dalgona) | `service`, `image`, `template`, `url`, `box_id` |
| `[mcp_servers.<name>]` (dalgona) | `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` |
| `[discovery]` (dalgona) | `sources` |
| `[eval]` (dalgona) | `uses` |
| `[herdr]` (dalgona) | `subagent_panes` |
| `[web]` (dalgona) | `listen`, `token`, `cert_file`, `key_file` |

`edit_style` accepts a style name or a table of model globs with a required `default` entry. Styles are `anchor`, `replace`, `hashline`, `hashline-light`, `hashline-enhanced`, `apply_patch`, `simple`, `balanced`, and `strict`. Model globs match in declaration order. Dal rejects the dalgona-only settings.

## Run inside an outer sandbox

Run dalgona inside a lightweight outer sandbox, such as a container, microVM, or cloud sandbox runner. The local harness sandbox only confines accidental writes and is not a security boundary. See [sandbox.md](docs/spec/sandbox.md) for the write policy. On Linux, when the local write policy applies, a `dalgona` command that a sandboxed command starts is refused by the daemon. On macOS, the sandbox profile denies access to the daemon socket. A daemon that itself runs with `no_new_privs` logs a warning, and sandboxed commands can still reach it.

Windows has no harness confinement. Linux runs without it when Landlock is unavailable. A remote box supplies the sandbox instead of the local write policy. See [sandbox.md](docs/spec/sandbox.md).

## Connect the Codex desktop app

Install the desktop override:

```sh
dalgona codex install
```

Restart the Codex desktop app after installation. The installer records prior settings before it changes the user-level executable override. Use `dalgona codex status` to inspect the override and `dalgona codex uninstall` to restore it. The integration does not patch the signed app bundle. See [Codex app integration](docs/spec/codex-app.md).

`dalgona app-server` bridges the desktop protocol. Its default listener is standard input and output. The app-server and the terminal interface use the same daemon protocol.

## Choose where execution runs

### Keep the orchestrator local

Set `runner` to a named entry in dalgona's config. For example:

```toml
runner = "devbox"

[runners.devbox]
service = "docker"
```

The runner uploads the workspace, records its baseline, and runs tools and subagents in the box. The supported services are in [runners.md](docs/spec/runners.md). A fork shares its parent's box. Archiving one thread does not destroy a box still used by another thread.

Use `dalgona pull <thread-id>` to apply the box's changes to the local workspace with `git apply --3way`. Conflicts leave markers and return exit code 1 with the affected files. `dalgona runner gc` lists unused boxes without deleting them. Use `dalgona runner gc --yes` to delete them.

### Run the whole daemon in a box

Configure `[remotes.<name>]`, then run:

```sh
dalgona cloud up <name>
dalgona --remote <name>
dalgona cloud pull <name>
dalgona cloud down <name>
```

The named remote uses any service in [runners.md](docs/spec/runners.md) except Cloudflare. Cloudflare cannot host a durable whole-daemon home because its containers lose their files on stop.

`cloud up` does not copy credentials unless you pass `--copy-auth`. Without credential copying, use `dalgona --remote <name> login` to authenticate in the box. Remote service and box identifiers live in `[remotes.<name>]` in `settings.toml`.

`cloud down` destroys the box and its journal after confirmation. `--yes` skips that confirmation for scripts. Pull changes you need before deletion.

Use `--remote <name>` with the terminal client, `web`, or `app-server` to connect to the in-box daemon through its bridge. See [the service decision](docs/decisions/sandbox-services.md) and [exec-server wire](docs/spec/exec-server.md) for persistence and transport rules.

## Other product commands

Both products accept these client commands and flags:

| Command or flag | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dal`, `dalgona` | Open the terminal interface. |
| `login [provider]` | List providers or sign in to one. |
| `logout <provider>` | Remove a stored credential. |
| `models` | List offered models. |
| `-p <prompt>` | Run one turn and exit. |
| `--json` | With `-p`, print one JSON status line. |
| `--resume <thread-id>` | Resume a recorded thread. |
| `-c` | Continue the latest thread; cannot combine with `--resume`. |
| `-m <model-id>` | Select the model for a new thread. |
| `--approval auto\|ask\|yolo` | Set the approval mode. |
| `--sandbox workspace-write\|off` | Set the harness sandbox mode. |
| `-C <directory>` | Change the working directory. |
| `--help`, `--version` | Print client flag help or the build version. |

Prefix client commands with the product name, for example `dal models` or `dalgona -p "Explain this repository"`. Dalgona also accepts `--remote <name>` to select a configured remote instead of the local daemon.

These commands are specific to dalgona:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dalgona daemon` | Run the per-user daemon. |
| `dalgona app-server [--listen <address>]` | Bridge the desktop protocol over standard input and output or a loopback WebSocket. |
| `dalgona service install\|uninstall` | Add or remove login-time daemon startup. |
| `dalgona pull <thread-id>` | Apply a thread box's changes locally. |
| `dalgona runner gc [--yes]` | List unused boxes, or delete them with `--yes`. |
| `dalgona cloud up <name> [--copy-auth]` | Create a whole-daemon box. |
| `dalgona cloud pull <name>` | Apply a whole-daemon box's workspace changes locally. |
| `dalgona cloud down <name> [--yes]` | Destroy a whole-daemon box. |
| `dalgona codex install\|uninstall\|status` | Manage the desktop executable override. |
| `dalgona codex record --real <codex-path> [args...]` | Record protocol metadata while running the selected Codex executable. |
| `dalgona web` | Serve the web interface; set its listener, token, and TLS files in `[web]`, not CLI flags. See [web access rules](docs/spec/web.md). |
| `dalgona run <file.star> [--arg k=v ...]` | Run a durable Starlark workflow. A value that is valid JSON is passed as JSON; any other value is passed as a string. |
| `dalgona exec-server [--listen <address>] [--root <directory>] [--data <directory>]` | Serve process and filesystem operations inside a box. |
| `dalgona bridge` | Connect standard input and output to the local daemon, starting it if needed. |
| `just build` | Build `dal` and `dalgona` for this platform into `bin/`. |
| `just dal [args...]` | Run `dal` from source with the given arguments. |
| `just dalgona [args...]` | Run `dalgona` from source with the given arguments. |
| `just dist` | Build release binaries for remote bootstrap. |
| `just box-image` | Build the remote box image. |

`app-server` defaults to `stdio://`. Its WebSocket listener accepts `ws://<loopback-address>:<port>`. Use repeated `-c key=value` or `--config key=value` arguments to set `model`, `approval_policy`, or `sandbox_mode` for new desktop threads.

`exec-server` defaults to `--listen stdio:// --root /workspace`. Its WebSocket listener accepts `ws://IP:PORT` and requires `DALGONA_BOX_TOKEN` with at least 32 characters. `--data` selects a persistent data directory. The bridge and exec server run where you invoke them; `--remote` does not redirect them.

`codex record` defaults to forwarding `app-server` when you omit arguments. It writes protocol metadata to `<home>/census/<unix-seconds>.jsonl`.

## Read the contracts and contribute

[The documentation index](docs/README.md) links every current specification and decision. Start with [journal](docs/spec/journal.md), [recovery](docs/spec/recovery.md), and [protocol](docs/spec/protocol.md) for the core contracts.

Read [CONTRIBUTE.md](CONTRIBUTE.md) before changing code and [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md) before reviewing it. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) contains repository instructions for coding agents. [justfile](justfile) declares the available checks. `just verify` runs the Go, web, and Cloudflare checks. It also runs the hashline model check when `uv` is installed.
