    ("sdk", "# Embed dal in a Rust program

Use `dal-agent` and `dal-core` through their public Rust APIs. The repository has one Cargo workspace and one `Cargo.lock`.

## Run the embedding example

From the repository root, run:

```sh
cargo run -p dalgon --example sdk
```

The example uses a local replay fixture. It needs no provider credentials. It prints `hello from scripted SDK`. Then it shuts down the host. Read the complete implementation in [`cli/dalgon/examples/sdk/main.rs`](../cli/dalgon/examples/sdk/main.rs).

## Depend on dal from your own project

No tagged release exists yet, and the registry has nothing to fetch (see [Install dal and dalgona](install.md)). Depend on the repository instead. Pin `rev` to a commit you tested. Use the latest stable Rust toolchain.

```text
# Cargo.toml of your project
[dependencies]
dal-agent = { git = "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona", rev = "<commit>" }
dal-core = { git = "https://github.com/gosuda/dalgona", rev = "<commit>" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```

The `tokio` line serves the example, which uses `#[tokio::main(flavor = "multi_thread")]`. In a local checkout, replace each `git` and `rev` pair with a `path` to `engine/dal-agent` or `core/dal-core`.

## Own the session lifecycle

Load configuration with `Config::load(ConfigProduct::Dalgon, data_root, product_defaults_toml, user_toml)`. The loader takes TOML text. It does not read files or the environment. Capture those inputs at your process boundary.

Build a `Product` with its data root and extensions. Pass it with the configuration and captured `Env` to `Host::start`. Open a session with `Host::open`. Use `SessionRef::Ephemeral` when the session must not be saved. `Host::close` closes one session by id. It closes descendant child sessions before their parent.

Subscribe before submitting a prompt. Handle a rejected submission, a closed subscription, and a resync request. Read text updates until `UpdateKind::TurnEnded`. Do not wait for the subscription to close before calling `Host::shutdown`. `Host::shutdown` takes a timeout grace duration. It returns a report with the closed session count. The runnable example shows each of these outcomes.

## Store extension state

In saved sessions, file-backed extensions use the session sidecar service for small private values. Sidecars are unavailable in ephemeral sessions, including the example above. Names must contain 1 to 64 bytes of lowercase ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, or `-`. They must start with a letter or digit. Sidecar files stay inside the owning extension's session directory. Writes are atomic. The `judge` service lets a cell ask the session judge a question.

## Exchange waiting mail between sessions

The shared agents service carries mailbox messages for dal and composed dalgona. There is one mechanism, not one per product.

Declare only the agents operations the caller needs. The host mints the caller identity and grants that service. A caller uses the capability-scoped services handle. It never writes the journal directly.

A recipient holds at most 100 waiting `NextTurn` messages. Delivered messages stay as history and do not count toward that bound. The next eligible user turn consumes waiting messages and writes them as turn input in one durable journal record. A new message can queue after that delivery.

Reads use a cursor and leave history in place. Reopening the session revalidates the delivery record. A full mailbox refuses with `Full` and writes no journal row. A missing or finished recipient answers `Gone`. A finished child has no promise of delivery.

Name the mode with `MailMode::NextTurn` and read the answer from `Receipt` (`Buffered`, `Full`, `Gone`). The bound is `MAILBOX_WAITING_LIMIT`.

## Next

- [Protocol](protocol.md): serve the same operations to other processes.
- [Build a client on the dal protocol](integrate.md): connect a program through `dalgon rpc`.
- [Plugins](plugins.md): extend dal in Starlark without a Rust build.

    ("serve", "# Run the dalgon model router and A2A server

`dalgon serve` starts an HTTP server on your machine. The server routes OpenAI-style and Anthropic-style requests to the models you signed in to. It can also run the full dal agent behind the same address. With `--a2a`, it serves the agent-to-agent surface too.

Use it to give a script, a tool, or a second machine one endpoint for your dal sign-in. The server binds to loopback and needs no token by default. `--public` listens on all interfaces and requires a token from `dalgon serve token`. An address from `--bind` or `serve.bind` replaces the all-interfaces address.

## Start the server

```sh
dalgon serve
```

The server prints one line to standard output and keeps running:

```text
dalgon serve listening on http://127.0.0.1:7437 (loopback, no token)
```

The port is `serve.port` in `dal.toml`. Its default is 7437. Pass `--port PORT` or `--bind ADDR` to override the address for one run. Stop the server with Ctrl+C. To change the port for every run, set it in `dal.toml`:

```toml
[serve]
port = 8080
```

## Send a request

The `model` field picks the target. The server accepts these ids:

| id | target |
|---|---|
| `dalgon/normal`, `dalgon/eval-first`, `dalgon/eval-only` | the dal agent in that mode, with its own tools |
| a key of `[aliases]` | the model that the alias names |
| `openai-chat/<model>`, `openai-responses/<model>`, `openai-codex/<model>`, `anthropic/<model>` | that provider, through a pass-through relay |

`GET /v1/models` lists the model ids to use. An unknown id fails with the code `model_not_found` and the text `model "<id>" was not found`.

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7437/v1/models
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7437/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"dalgon/normal","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello."}]}'
```

These routes exist:

| route | use |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` | list model ids |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI Chat Completions |
| `POST /v1/responses` | OpenAI Responses |
| `POST /v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages |
| `GET /v1/ws` | WebSocket upgrade for protocol clients |
| `GET /codex/ws` | WebSocket upgrade for Codex clients |

Every POST needs `Content-Type: application/json`. Otherwise the server answers 415 with `Content-Type must be application/json`. A request with an `Origin` header gets 403 `browser requests are not allowed`, except a WebSocket upgrade. A server without `--public` also refuses a `Host` header that is not a loopback name. It answers 403 with `Host header "<host>" is not a loopback name`.

## Continue a session

A `dalgon/...` id runs the dal harness. The harness refuses client tools, tool choices, and tool history. A request continues a session in one of three ways:

- an `x-dal-session` header that holds a session id
- a `previous_response_id` in a Responses request
- a history that matches an earlier reply

Anything else opens a new session in the directory where `dalgon serve` runs. An unknown session id fails with `session_not_found`.

The router cannot ask anyone. It denies an approval it needs at once, and an extension question takes its default answer. `[serve] approval` sets the approval policy for actions that arrive through the server. It takes `ask`, `edits`, or `all`. Use `edits` or `all` only on a server that nobody else can reach.

```toml
[serve]
approval = "edits"
```

## Listen beyond loopback

Create a token. The command prints the token once and stores it in `serve.token` in the data root.

```sh
dalgon serve token
```

Start the server with `--public`. It then listens on all interfaces and requires the token. When `--bind` or `serve.bind` names an address, the server binds that address instead, and `--bind` wins over `serve.bind`. `--public` still requires the token.

```sh
dalgon serve --public
```

With the default address, the server prints a warning to standard error and a listen line to standard output:

```text
dalgon: warning: --public serves 0.0.0.0:7437 over plain HTTP; the serve token crosses the network in plain text.
dalgon serve listening on http://0.0.0.0:7437 (all interfaces, token from <token-file>)
```

Clients send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or as `x-api-key: <token>`. The server answers 401 `missing_token` when the token is absent. It answers 401 `invalid_token` with `the bearer token does not match serve.token` when the token is wrong.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://HOST:7437/v1/models
```

Pass `--token-file FILE` to read the token from another file. To create the token at that path, put the flag before `token`: `dalgon serve --token-file FILE token`. A second `dalgon serve token` fails with `dalgon: serve.token already exists: <path>` while the file exists. Add `--force` to replace the token. Every client must then use the new one.

The WebSocket address works with the dal terminal. Run `dalgon --connect HOST:7437 --token-file FILE` on the other machine. `--connect` takes `host:port`, a `ws://` or `wss://` URL, or an absolute socket path. dalgon sends the token only to a non-loopback WebSocket address. `--connect` needs the interactive terminal. With `--print` or `--json`, it fails with `dalgon: --connect requires the interactive TUI`.

## Serve A2A

```sh
dalgon serve --a2a
```

The detail in the listen line then ends with `, a2a on`, for example `(loopback, no token, a2a on)`. The server mounts these routes. Without `--a2a`, each one answers 404 with `no route for <method> <path>`.

| route | use |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` | the agent card |
| `POST /a2a` | A2A JSON-RPC |
| `POST /a2a/v1/message:send` | send a message |
| `POST /a2a/v1/message:stream` | send a message and stream the reply |
| `GET /a2a/v1/tasks/<id>` | read a task |
| `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/<id>:cancel` | cancel a task |

On a public server, the agent card needs no token. Every other route does.

## Fix a start error

Each start error prints two lines: what failed, then the fix.

| first line | cause |
|---|---|
| `dalgon: cannot bind 127.0.0.1:7437: <message>` | Another process holds the port. Stop it, or pass `--port` with a free port. |
| `dalgon: serve --bind <address> is not a loopback address: it needs a token` | Pass `--public`, or bind 127.0.0.1. |
| `dalgon: serve --public needs a token: <path> does not exist` | Run `dalgon serve token`. |
| `dalgon: serve.token is open to other users: <path> has mode <mode>` | Run `chmod 600 <path>`, or run `dalgon serve token --force`. |
| `dalgon: [aliases] key "<alias>" shadows a dal mode id` | Rename the alias. |

- [Build a client on the dal protocol](integrate.md) shows a worked client over `dalgon rpc`.
- [Settings in dal.toml](config.md) lists the `[serve]` keys.

    ("sessions", "# Sessions, history, and compaction

Sessions live under the data root. Use `-c` to continue a session. Use `-r` to resume one. Names label sessions. Exit lines and `/name` print the `-r` argument in the exact form the shell accepts. Names that are unsafe to paste degrade to the session id. Use `/tree`, `/fork`, and `/clone` to inspect or change branches. Use `/export` to write a shareable file. Read an entry at `session://<id>/<entry>`. `--no-session` runs without saving.

Child sessions also write a `dal-agent` `child_policy` record with their inherited approval mode and tool allowlist. An absent tool list means unrestricted access. Session replay requires at most one policy record. Duplicate or conflicting records fail replay.

A reopened session shows the model, thinking level, approval mode, execution mode, and name its journal recorded. The last record of each kind wins. A session that never chose a model keeps following the configured default. Its settings name no model while it runs and after it reopens. A default saved after it opened applies the next time it opens. A route the session chose shows exactly as recorded, with its provider when the record names one.


## Durable turn identities

For saved sessions, dal writes a turn-ID reservation to the journal before it acknowledges a prompt, follow-up, or wake allocation. A record counts as saved only after it is synced to disk. The first reservation creates the journal even if the turn never starts.

Private tool effects also require saved receipts. In a saved session, the first private loop or effect receipt creates the journal even if no user turn has started. dal saves the start receipt before running the effect. Ephemeral sessions keep these records in memory and do not create journal files.

Cancelling queued work does not release its identity. Later turns keep their allocated IDs. When a session reopens, unused reservations remain consumed. dal does not restore queued text. Submit it again if you still want to run it. A reservation alone does not create a completed turn.

Reservation records use journal format 2, and mail delivery records use journal format 3. All other record kinds retain format 1, so one journal can contain several versions. Existing journals remain readable and are not rewritten. Once a record of a newer format is written, a build that does not read that format reports the newer format and does not open the journal. Use a build that supports formats 1 to 3.

Multi-record batches still lack atomic framing against process crashes. An interrupted batch is not guaranteed to roll back cleanly on reopen.


## Compaction

Compaction starts by default at 85 percent of the context window, remote first. Use `/compact <focus>` to force it. Compaction retains recent entries and inserts summary text. dal drops raw provider-native history items. They do not continue into subsequent model requests.

## Context measurements

Measured context use applies only to the model route that produced the latest
assistant response on the selected branch after compaction. The route includes
its kind and, for API routes, its API family. A matching model name alone is not
enough. When both routes name a provider, the providers must match too. A
response recorded without a provider still counts for the same model that now
names one.

Completed and partial responses retain this identity when the session reopens.
If the latest response has no route metadata, dal uses a context estimate rather
than an older measurement. Existing journals stay readable and are not rewritten.
See [assistant entries](protocol.md#assistant-entries) for the stored field.

## Next

- [Slash commands](commands.md): run `/tree`, `/fork`, `/clone`, `/export`, `/compact`, and `/resume`.
- [Command line](cli.md): continue or resume a session with `-c` and `-r`.
- [Protocol](protocol.md): list, open, and subscribe to sessions over JSON-RPC.

    ("symbols", "# Symbols: search and structural editing

dal and dalgona provide syntax-aware symbol search and structural block editing over supported programming languages.
Symbol intelligence relies on Tree-sitter parsers to extract semantic definitions and syntactic blocks directly from source code.
No language server protocol daemon runs. Symbol operations are bounded, deterministic parse passes over current file bytes.

## Configuration

Symbol capabilities are gated by the `search_symbols` setting in `dal.toml`.
In dal, `search_symbols` is `false` by default.
In dalgona, `search_symbols` is `true` by default.

- `search: mode "symbol" is off. Set search_symbols = true in dal.toml.`
- `patch: line <n>: block ops (N*) need search_symbols = true in dal.toml.`

## Definition kinds

Symbol extraction folds language-specific syntax nodes onto a closed set of twelve definition kinds:

| Kind | Code construct | Typical scope |
|---|---|---|
| `function` | Free function or procedure | Module or top-level |
| `method` | Method inside a class, impl block, trait, or receiver | Type or instance scope |
| `struct` | Struct or union definition | Type definition |
| `enum` | Enumeration or variant type | Type definition |
| `trait` | Trait definition | Interface definition |
| `impl` | Implementation block named by target type | Type implementation |
| `module` | Module, namespace, or package | Namespace definition |
| `macro` | Macro definition | Macro definition |
| `const` | Constant, immutable value, or static definition | Value definition |
| `type` | Type alias or type definition | Type definition |
| `class` | Class definition | Object type |
| `interface` | Interface or module type definition | Interface contract |

Supported languages include Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Python, OCaml, C, and C++.
Files lacking parser extractors report:
- `search: <p> has no symbol support (<lang>).`
- `patch: <p> has no symbol support (<lang>).`

## Symbol search

The `search` tool accepts `mode: "symbol"` with a `pattern` string.
The query pipeline matches definitions from fresh parses of current file bytes.
Trigram literals from the final segment filter candidate files. Fresh syntax walks follow.

### Pattern grammar

```
pattern = "*" / [ "::" ] segment *( "::" segment )
segment = name [ "[" ordinal "]" ]
ordinal = 1*digit
```

- Suffix matching: `pattern` matches any definition whose qualified name ends with the specified segments. For example, `run` matches `Engine::run` and `Worker::run`.
- Absolute matching: A leading `::` pins the match to the complete qualified name. For example, `::Engine::run` matches only top-level `Engine::run`.
- Ordinal disambiguation: `[k]` specifies the 1-based source-order definition among identical names in the same file. For example, `apply[2]` targets the second definition named `apply`.
- File outline: `pattern: "*"` with `path` set to one file lists every definition in that file in source order.

Invalid patterns return specific errors:
- `search: invalid symbol pattern <pattern>: <reason>.`
  Valid reason strings are `empty`, `empty segment`, `ordinal must be a number`, `ordinal must be at least 1`, or `* with more than one path`.
- `search: pattern * needs path set to one file.`
- `search: <p> is not a file.`
- `search: parser failed on <p>: <msg>.`

### Budgets and caps

- Maximum candidate files parsed: 500 files per query.
- Each file parse has a 250 ms wall-clock budget. A query can parse multiple files.
- Single match reveal limit: at most 2000 lines and 50 KiB (51,200 bytes).
- dal parses text files up to 16 MiB. It skips binary and UTF-16 files.

### Output forms

Multiple matches list matching rows followed by a guidance footer:
```
lib/patch.ml:40-88 function apply
lib/patch.ml:120-130 function apply[2]
lib/tool.ml:12-30 function Tool::apply
[3 definitions. Search a longer name to see one whole with its tag.]
```

A single match within limits reveals the entire definition with line numbers and def tag:
```
lib/patch.ml:40-88 function apply tag 7C2E4B1A
40:let apply w edits =
...
88:  Ok changes
```

Outline queries print definitions without the guidance footer:
```
lib/patch.ml:40-88 function apply
lib/patch.ml:120-130 function apply[2]
[2 definitions.]
```

When search limits are reached:
- `[<n> definitions shown; parse budget reached.]`
- `No definitions match <pattern> in <scope>.`

## Structural block editing

Structural editing enables edits anchored to definition boundaries or syntax blocks.

### Patch by symbol

The `patch` tool accepts `symbol` change objects:
- `symbol`: Definition name matching search mode symbol output (for example, `Engine::run` or `run[2]`).
- `tag`: Optional 8-character hexadecimal tag (`tag8("def:" ++ definition_raw_bytes)`). When supplied, patch verifies that the definition has not changed since it was read.
- `at`: Insertion position relative to definition: `"replace"` (default), `"before"`, or `"after"`.
- `new`: Replacement or inserted text. Passing `new: ""` with `at: "replace"` deletes the definition.
- `old`: When replacing text within a definition without replacing the whole block, provide `symbol`, `old`, and `new`. `old` must occur exactly once inside the definition. You do not need a `tag`.

Symbol patch errors:
- `patch: changes[<i>]: tag <T> does not match <name> now (tag <U>). The file changed since you read it; read it again.`
- `patch: changes[<i>]: definition tag needs a symbol selector.`
- `patch: no definition <name> in <p>.`
- `patch: <n> definitions named <name> in <p>.`
- `patch: changes[<i>]: old is not in <name> in <p>. Copy it again from the lines below, or read <p>.`
- `patch: <p> has no symbol support (<lang>).`
- `patch: changes[<i>]: symbol support is not enabled for this file.`
- `patch: parser failed on <p>: <reason>.` The reason is one of `Budget`, `TooManyParses`, `Panic`, or `Unsupported`.

### Hashline N* block operator

In the `hashline` edit style, the `N*` operator references the outermost named syntactic block beginning at line `N`:
- `PUT N*:` replaces the lines of the resolved syntactic block.
- `CUT N*` deletes the lines of the resolved syntactic block.
- `PUT >N*:` inserts text after the last line of the syntactic block at sibling indentation.

Block syntax errors:
- `patch: no syntactic block begins at line <n> of <p>.`
- `patch: line <n>: block ops (N*) need search_symbols = true in dal.toml.`

## Next

- [Tools, modes, and approval](tools.md): run `search` mode `symbol` and choose a `patch` edit style.
- [Settings in dal.toml](config.md): set `search_symbols`.

    ("terminal", "# dal terminal interface: keyboard shortcuts, inline and fullscreen

The interface is inline by default. It is fullscreen on request. Keys:

| key | action | F1 label |
|---|---|---|
| enter | submit | Send |
| esc | close or interrupt | Close or interrupt |
| up | previous history | Previous history |
| down | next history | Next history |
| ctrl+up | previous prompt | Previous prompt |
| ctrl+down | next prompt | Next prompt |
| ctrl+r | search history | Search history |
| tab / shift+tab | cycle a completion forward or back | Complete |
| ctrl+g | edit the draft in $VISUAL or $EDITOR | External editor |
| ctrl+l | clear the live region | Clear live region |
| ctrl+z | suspend to the shell (not on Windows) | Suspend |
| F1 | help | Help |
| pgup / pgdn | page through the transcript | Transcript page up / Transcript page down |
| end | jump to the latest transcript entry | Jump to latest |
| ctrl+t | transcript overlay (inline) | Transcript overlay |
| ctrl+shift+f or F3 | search the transcript (fullscreen) | Search transcript |
| tab / shift+tab | next or previous action in a dialog | Next action / Previous action |
| shift+left | extend the fullscreen selection left | Extend selection left |
| shift+right | extend the fullscreen selection right | Extend selection right |
| shift+up | extend the fullscreen selection up | Extend selection up |
| shift+down | extend the fullscreen selection down | Extend selection down |

Press F1 to open keyboard help without adding it to the transcript. Use Up and
Down to scroll one row. Use PageUp and PageDown to scroll one page. Press Esc or
Ctrl+C to close help. Your draft stays unchanged. Help ignores typing and
paste. Run `/hotkeys` instead to keep the key list in the transcript.

In fullscreen, and in the Ctrl+T overlay, the transcript viewport follows the live edge. Paging up detaches it. The hint shows `following stopped · press end to jump to the latest` until End returns to the latest entry.

In fullscreen, hold Shift. Use the arrow keys to select transcript text.
Press Ctrl+C to copy the selection without interrupting a running turn.
Typing clears the selection. It returns you to the composer. In inline mode, use
your terminal's native text selection.

Diagram labels use installed fonts captured when the terminal interface starts.
Restart after installing fonts. If a diagram cannot resolve a font, dal shows
the original source and a failure reason instead of an unlabeled image.

In fullscreen only, Ctrl+Shift+F (F3 on terminals without kitty keyboard) opens a filter row over the viewport top. Enter jumps to the latest match. Esc closes it.

When the layout has room, a busy extension has a row `<extension>: <text>` (or `<extension>: busy` with no text) above the status line. The row uses the dim role and extension-name order. When more extensions are busy than the activity rows allow, the last row names the hidden count. It reads `(<n> more extensions busy)` when multiple extensions are hidden. It reads `(1 more extension busy)` when one is hidden. A quiet extension has no row. The rows follow the terminal's color and `NO_COLOR` settings. F1 opens help. Steer types while dal works. Follow up waits for the turn. Stop ends it at once. Copy uses the terminal clipboard. The first non-empty locale selects ambiguous character width. Japanese, Chinese, and Korean select wide. Other locales select narrow. Themes tune contrast. Opt-in inline images show diagrams. Native diagrams render as text when images are off.

## Next

- [Command line](cli.md): start fullscreen with `--screen fullscreen`.
- [Settings in dal.toml](config.md): set the `screen` default.

    ("tools", "# Tools, modes, and approval

Modes: `normal`, `eval-first`, and `eval-only` list the same tools: `read`, `search`, `patch`, `exec`, and `eval`. The eval modes additionally reach plugin tools and prompt sections marked `eval_only`. Other modes hide them. Calls to hidden tools fail. Each tool takes typed parameters with limits. Edit styles: `anchor` by default. The per-model table picks `replace`, `apply_patch`, `anchor`, `hashline`, `hashline-light`, or `hashline-enhanced`. Tiers: `simple`, `balanced`, `strict`. Search modes are `find`, `grep`, and `symbol`. There is no LSP. The approval ladder `--approval ask|edits|all` carries ask, edits, all. By default, dal asks before every `patch` and every `exec`. When no person can answer, dal denies the operation and says why. Approval previews show control and bidirectional characters as visible escape sequences instead of sending them to the terminal. Call-scoped argv-prefix grants allow one command prefix. Background jobs run detached. Subagents are off by default in dal. Read schemes: `dal://`, plus plugin schemes.

## Recover from a failed patch

If a patch fails after changing files, dal tries to restore each completed operation. If restoration fails, the error names every affected path and any retained backup. Inspect those paths. Restore the affected files before retrying. Keep the backups until recovery is complete.

## The eval tool

`eval` runs one Starlark cell per call. Nothing but Starlark runs in it. Every effect a cell requests goes through the same approval as the tool of that name. A call you deny outside `eval` is denied inside it. `eval` is not a sandbox.

The request has one required field and two optional ones. It takes nothing else:

```json
{"code": "tools.search(\"TODO\", path = \"src\")", "uses": ["tools.search"], "data": {"limit": 20}}
```

- `code` is the cell.
- `uses` narrows the operations the cell may request.
- `data` is any JSON value. The cell reads it as `data`. It is `None` when absent.

A cell inherits its operations from `eval.uses` in `dal.toml`. If you leave out `uses`, the cell may request all of them. If you give `uses`, the cell may request only those. Each must be in `eval.uses`. An id outside `eval.uses` stops the cell with `scope_exceeded`. If you give `uses = []`, the cell can only compute: no tools, network, state, or child sessions. With no `eval.uses`, every cell can only compute.

Each cell starts fresh. It has five names: `ctx`, `tools` (the same as `ctx.tools`), `judge`, `judge_batch`, and `data`. `judge(question)` asks the session judge one yes-or-no question and returns a `bool`. `judge_batch(questions)` asks up to 32 and returns one `bool` per question in the same order; an empty list returns an empty list. A question is one line of 1 to 4096 bytes. A cell may call them only when the operation it calls, `judge.ask` or `judge.batch`, is in its `uses` and in `eval.uses`. It needs no `load` and no wrapper function. It keeps no globals for the next cell. The last expression is the result. If the last statement is not an expression, the result is `None`. There is no `return`.

```starlark
page = tools.search("TODO", path = "src")
{"count": len(page.matches), "truncated": page.truncated}
```

Calls return their values directly. A failed call stops the cell. To inspect an expected failure, pass the operation itself to `ctx.try_call`, not the result of calling it:

```starlark
r = ctx.try_call(tools.exec, "cargo test")
{"exit_ok": r.ok}
```

Denial, cancellation, and hard limits stop the cell. You cannot catch them. A patch that ran before a later failure is not undone.

A pure cell reads only its data:

```starlark
sorted(data["names"])
```

Send it with `"uses": []`. To call a plugin tool from a cell, write `tools["quality.todos"](path = "src")`. The cell needs the tool's id and the operations it declares. [Plugins](plugins.md#call-a-plugin-tool-from-eval) explains this. To run calls at the same time, open a scope with a limit from 1 to 64. Then collect the results in submission order:

```starlark
s = ctx.scope(limit = 2)
for path in ["src", "tests"]:
    s.tools.search("TODO", path = path)
s.all()
```

The reply is an envelope, not just the value:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `invocation_id` | the id of this cell run |
| `status` | `completed`, `failed`, `denied`, `cancelled`, `limit_exceeded`, or `indeterminate` |
| `value` | the result; present only when `status` is `completed` |
| `error` | `code`, `message`, and `stage`; present when the cell did not complete |
| `prints` | the lines the cell printed and whether they were cut; a diagnostic channel only |
| `cleanup` | whether dal finished cleanup, and the ids of any calls still outstanding |
| `observer_errors` | hooks that failed while watching the cell |

A `completed` status means the code finished. It does not mean the goal was met, that a test passed, or that every handled failure succeeded.

## Next

- [Plugins](plugins.md): register tools and hooks that `eval` can reach.
- [Sandbox](sandbox.md): limit where `exec` children can write.
- [Symbols and structural editing](symbols.md): use `search` mode `symbol` and structural `patch`.

[package]
name = "dalgona"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license-file.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true

[lints]
workspace = true

[features]
default = ["tui"]
tui = ["dalgon/tui"]

[dependencies]
dal-agent = "=0.1.0"
dal-core = "=0.1.0"
dal-tools = "=0.1.0"
dalgon = { version = "=0.1.0", default-features = false }
dalgona-batteries = { version = "=0.1.0", path = "../dalgona-batteries" }
thiserror = "=2.0.21"
toml.workspace = true
[dev-dependencies]
clap = { version = "=4.6.7", features = ["derive", "string"] }

path = "src/bin/dalgona.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "dg"
path = "src/bin/dg.rs"

.ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq
.el .ds Aq '
.TH dalgona-__sandbox 1  "dalgona-__sandbox " 
.SH NAME
dalgona\-__sandbox \- Enable the configured sandbox.
.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBdalgona\-__sandbox\fR [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] 
.SH DESCRIPTION
Enable the configured sandbox.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Print help

.ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq
.el .ds Aq '
.TH dalgona-acp 1  "dalgona-acp " 
.SH NAME
dalgona\-acp \- Serve the Agent Client Protocol on standard input and output.
.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBdalgona\-acp\fR [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] 
.SH DESCRIPTION
Serve the Agent Client Protocol on standard input and output.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Print help

.ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq
.el .ds Aq '
.TH dalgona-app-server 1  "dalgona-app-server " 
.SH NAME
dalgona\-app\-server \- Serve the Codex app\-server protocol on standard input and output.
.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBdalgona\-app\-server\fR [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] 
.SH DESCRIPTION
Serve the Codex app\-server protocol on standard input and output.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Print help

.ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq
.el .ds Aq '
.TH dalgona-completion 1  "dalgona-completion " 
.SH NAME
dalgona\-completion \- Generate shell completion scripts.
.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBdalgona\-completion\fR [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] <\fISHELL\fR> 
.SH DESCRIPTION
Generate shell completion scripts.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Print help
.TP
<\fISHELL\fR>

.br
\fIPossible values:\fR
.RS 14
.IP \(bu 2
bash
.IP \(bu 2
elvish
.IP \(bu 2
fish
.IP \(bu 2
powershell
.IP \(bu 2
zsh
.RE

.ie \n(.g .ds Aq \(aq
.el .ds Aq '
.TH dalgona-docs 1  "dalgona-docs " 
.SH NAME
dalgona\-docs \- Read a dalgon documentation page.
.SH SYNOPSIS
\fBdalgona\-docs\fR [\fB\-h\fR|\fB\-\-help\fR] [\fIURI\fR] 
.SH DESCRIPTION
Read a dalgon documentation page.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Print help
.TP
[\fIURI\fR]

[workspace]
members = ["cargo:."]

# Config for 'dist'
[dist]
# The preferred dist version to use in CI (Cargo.toml SemVer syntax)
cargo-dist-version = "0.32.0"
# CI backends to support
ci = "github"
# The installers to generate for each app
installers = ["shell", "powershell"]
# A prefix git tags must include for dist to care about them
tag-namespace = "dalgona"
# Target platforms to build apps for (Rust target-triple syntax)
targets = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-pc-windows-msvc", "x86_64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
packages = ["dalgona"]
# Whether to embed dependency information using cargo-auditable
cargo-auditable = true
# Extra static files to include in each App (path relative to this Cargo.toml's dir)
include = ["man"]
# Publish jobs to run in CI
publish-jobs = ["./dalgona-publish-crates"]
# Post-announce jobs to run in CI
post-announce-jobs = ["./dalgona-smoke-install"]
# Path that installers should place binaries in
install-path = "CARGO_HOME"
# Whether to install an updater program
install-updater = false

[dist.github-custom-runners]
aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu = "ubuntu-24.04-arm"
aarch64-pc-windows-msvc = "windows-11-arm"

# Changelog

## Unreleased
- Fix tool and command panics that happen before the work starts. The call now returns an error and the session stays usable.

- Add `cancel_queued`, a command that removes one queued follow-up by its turn id. The `queued` reply to a follow-up now carries that `turn`; a queued steer still has none. The removed text comes back in a `discarded` notice, and an id that is not queued is rejected and changes nothing. A follow-up that has already started cannot be removed; cancel its turn instead.
- Fix provider requests built from a journal that holds more than one result for the same tool call. The request now carries only the first result for each call of a model response, so providers no longer reject it. The journal is not changed.
- Fix child sessions: a child started with a `tools` list now sees and can call only those tools, on every turn and after every reload, through the model, scripts, and extension services. An empty list gives the child no tools, and a start with no list leaves it unrestricted. A child also starts under the approval mode its parent runs under now, not the configured default.
- Add the `-32009` error code ("server draining") to the dal protocol. A WebSocket connection answers every new request with it once the listener begins to stop, lets running requests finish for up to one second, and then closes. A request to a host that has shut down now answers `-32009` instead of `-32603`.
- Fix the text the model reads when a `tool_call` hook blocks a call: it now starts with `blocked by <extension>:` so the model and the user can see which extension refused the call and why.
- Add `image_bytes_elsewhere` to compactor input: the bytes of the images that stay in the request, so a compactor can keep its images within a request size budget.
- Fix an HTTP 413 "request too large" answer from a provider: dal now compacts the history and retries the turn, as for a context-overflow error, instead of failing the turn.
- Price model requests by context size: a model can list request-wide price tiers in its prices (`dal.toml` and the bundled price table), and dal uses the highest tier that the request's input tokens exceed.
- Add opt-in fenced-diagram rendering for terminal transcript rows and ask previews: the `/settings` picker toggles `tui.diagrams` for the session and a save row persists it to `dal.toml` through the standard product configuration; CLI-backed diagram renders run on background workers with a pending placeholder, and pixel results draw through the terminal's image protocol (kitty, sixel, or iTerm2) instead of a text card.
- Fix ACP permission requests: `toolCall.toolCallId` now carries the provider's tool-call id that the tool-call updates announced, so a client can match a permission request to its call. Approval questions gain an optional `call` member for this; encoded questions without it still decode, and a question with no call keeps the request id.

- Persist image-bearing compaction parts and their extension letters atomically, replay them from the journal, and resolve letter history sources after resume; pass the selected catalog image profile, retained-image count, and carried summary to compactors.
- Accept mapped MCP tool names in registration, dispatch, approval, and replay; send provider-safe aliases to providers and restore internal names on streamed calls.
- Fix extension questions raised while no front end that can answer is attached, such as print mode, `--json`, child sessions, the router, and A2A: the question now takes its no-answer default at once instead of waiting for its time limit. A question raised while a front end is attached keeps waiting, up to its time limit, if that front end disconnects, so a client can reconnect and answer it. The time limit counts from when the question is raised and nothing extends it. Router and A2A runs no longer wait for approvals: they deny them at once, as print mode does.
- Fix the approval timeout text: it now reads `Permission denied: <tool> needed approval and no one answered within <n> s.`, with the colon the manual names. An approval that nobody could answer is now reported as unavailable, not as a refusal by a person; it is still denied.
- Fix `tool_call` hook rewrites: the rewritten arguments now pass the same checks as the model's original arguments before the tool runs. A rewrite the tool rejects, such as a path outside the workspace, ends the call with the same "invalid arguments" error instead of reaching the tool.
- Fix a panic in a tool or slash command handler: it no longer ends the session's driver task and leaves the turn or command hanging. The tool call settles with an error that names the tool and carries the panic message, and a command answers an error that names the command. The session keeps running, and ACP clients see the failure instead of waiting forever.
- Fix `dalgon acp`, `dalgon rpc`, and `dalgon app-server` over standard input and output: the command now moves the protocol onto private copies of standard input and output and points the shared streams at the null device and standard error. Output from tool children, extensions, or libraries can no longer corrupt the JSON-RPC stream on Unix; it appears on standard error. Windows keeps the shared streams.
- Add `DAL_THREAD_ID` and `DAL_TOOL_CALL_ID` to the environment of `exec` children. They carry the session id and the tool call id, and they replace values with the same names in the captured environment. A value that contains a NUL byte is left out.
- Fix `patch` text matching on large files: the search now does linear work instead of rescanning the file for each match. When `old` has no exact match, the patch also accepts the same text with CRLF line ends, copied line-number prefixes, curly quotes, dashes, special spaces, or trailing spaces. Indentation must still match.
- Fix Anthropic replay after the system prompt or tool list changes: signed thinking blocks from the old prefix are dropped instead of failing the request with "Invalid signature in thinking block".
- Fix Anthropic replay from older sessions: signed thinking blocks without a recorded prefix are dropped unless they are needed to continue an active tool call.
- Fix Claude login when the preferred callback port is busy: login now uses a free loopback port and sends that port in the redirect address, instead of falling back to pasting the code.
- Fix terminal presentation: the queued and steering counts now come from the host's turn state, multiline question titles keep each line, wrapped transcript rows keep their links, and file paths in settled rows are clickable OSC 8 links.
- Initial release.
- Add extension status consumers. A registered status kind now publishes an `ext_status` update (`busy` or `quiet`, with optional text) only when it changes; `Agent::ext_status`, `Agent::poll_status`, `Agent::is_quiet`, and `Host::is_quiet` read it. The terminal shows busy extensions above the status line when the layout has room, ACP sends a `status` notice, A2A adds `dal.status` metadata, and the router sends nothing. `dalgon --json` writes its line only after every status kind is quiet; print mode waits 3 seconds and exits 1 with `dalgon: extension status is not quiet` if a kind stays busy.
- Breaking: change the plugin API to Plugin and Eval v1. A plugin now publishes one `plugin` value built after `load("@dal/v1", "dal")`. Tools take an `input` schema, handlers are `run(ctx, args)`, each tool, hook, and model lists its operations in `uses`, and the plugin requests host services through `inject`. This replaces `dal.tool(name = ...)`, `dal.prompt_section`, and `run(args, ctx)`. To update a plugin, follow `dal://plugins`.
- Add scripted synthetic model routes to Plugin and Eval v1. The `models` map associates a plugin-local key with `dal.model(id = ..., caps = ..., run = ..., uses = [...])`; `id` is the public `namespace/route` name. `run(ctx, request)` receives the provider-neutral request and can call `ctx.models.infer` or `ctx.models.forward`. Add `infer` to the plugin's `inject` services when models call those operations. A scripted model can forward once per run; the host rejects cycles and synthetic model chains deeper than four routes.
- Add `always_apply`, `scope`, `interrupt_mode`, `repeat_mode`, and `repeat_gap` to `dal.rule`, so a plugin rule can apply every turn or fire only in chosen content, such as `scope = ["tool:exec"]`.
- Change `eval` to take `{code, uses?, data?}`. A cell inherits its operations from `eval.uses`, and `uses = []` makes it pure.
- Remove the `notify` example plugin; its behavior cannot run under the v1 hook limits.
- Fix extension records: `append_record` now writes a journal record before it returns, `records` reads only the calling extension's rows on the current leaf path, and a tool call runs as the extension that registered it, with that extension's `inject` set. Records survive resume and follow `/tree` leaf moves.

This replaces `dal.tool(name = ...)`, `dal.prompt_section`, and `run(args, ctx)`. To update a plugin, follow `dal://plugins`.
- Add scripted synthetic model routes to Plugin and Eval v1. The `models` map associates a plugin-local key with `dal.model(id = ..., caps = ..., run = ..., uses = [...])`; `id` is the public `namespace/route` name. `run(ctx, request)` receives the provider-neutral request and can call `ctx.models.infer` or `ctx.models.forward`. Add `infer` to the plugin's `inject` services when models call those operations. A scripted model can forward once per run; the host rejects cycles and synthetic model chains deeper than four routes.
- Add `always_apply`, `scope`, `interrupt_mode`, `repeat_mode`, and `repeat_gap` to `dal.rule`, so a plugin rule can apply every turn or fire only in chosen content, such as `scope = ["tool:exec"]`.
- Change `eval` to take `{code, uses?, data?}`. A cell inherits its operations from `eval.uses`, and `uses = []` makes it pure.
- Remove the `notify` example plugin; its behavior cannot run under the v1 hook limits.
- Fix extension records: `append_record` now writes a journal record before it returns, `records` reads only the calling extension's rows on the current leaf path, and a tool call runs as the extension that registered it, with that extension's `inject` set. Records survive resume and follow `/tree` leaf moves.
